News.title: Moment off duty police officers heading home pounce on bungling burglar with crowbar trying to make a getaway
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment two off-duty cops caught a bungling burglar as he sought to make his escape while carrying a crowbar.

Eagle-eyed Police Sergeant Jake Clarkson and PC Shafi Chowdhury spotted a burglary taking place at a business in Old Street, Hackney on Sunday 13 September at around 6.30am.



The two police officers were on their way home after finishing a night shift in Camden when they went past a business they suspected was being burgled.

The glass door had been ripped off its hinges and left wide open.



The cops called 999, with footage showing them waiting on either side of the building’s entrance until they pounced on the suspect.

Michael Lawrence, 43, then casually walks outside carrying a crowbar and a torch, blissfully unaware of the two cops waiting for him.



The suspect had successfully stolen cash from the till and was wearing a backpack that had a wrench and hammer inside it.

Michael was also donning a large camo hat, black coat and grey tracksuit bottoms.



PS Clarkson and PC Chowdhury lunged at Michael, took hold of his arms and seized the crowbar before pulling him to the ground.

Once their on-duty colleague arrived, Michael was placed in handcuffs.

One of the officers said: “You’ve been identified trying to burgle into this place which you’ve maybe stolen from.”

Michael repeatedly says “no”, but later pleaded guilty to burglary and going equipped for burglary at a hearing at Stratford Magistrates’ Court on Monday.

He was remanded on conditional bail and will be sentenced at a later date.



Recounting the incident, PS Clarkson said: “We were chatting about our weekend plans one minute, and seconds later we were back in work mode.

“When you see something like that unfolding, your training just kicks in – you don’t stop to think, you act.”

PC Chowdhury added: “It was very satisfying to see the look on the man’s face as he was greeted by the two of us.

“It was also a great feeling to see him quickly charged and later plead guilty, knowing he had been held accountable.”

A spokesperson for Metropolitan Police said: “Two off-duty Met officers were heading home after a night shift when they spotted a burglary in progress.



“They called 999 and waited outside as the suspect emerged from the premises carrying a crowbar.

“Despite being off duty, the officers stepped in and detained him.

“He later pleaded guilty to burglary and going equipped for burglary.”

News.title: Fury in Spain after PM admits Moroccan warships sailed near Ceuta at same time 80,000 migrants invaded enclave
News.content:
Next

MOROCCAN warships sailed near Ceuta without permission on the same day tens of thousands of migrants flooded the enclave, Spain’s prime minister admitted.

Several vessels violated Spanish waters in late July – with the revelation sparking fresh rage over border security.



Around 80,000 people crossed the border into Europe in 48 hours this summer – the largest single-day arrival of irregular migrants in EU history.

Hundreds of people died, dozens of sexual assault cases were reported, and facilities were overwhelmed amid the chaos.



Reports say Moroccan naval incursions into Spanish waters took place while the mass crossing was unfolding – and continued into early August.

Some encounters came close to a collision or confrontation, El Pais reported.



The outlet said according to its sources: “It was not… a mere crossing or an accidental entry, rather an intentional and repeated violation of territorial waters, for which there are few precedents.

“Morocco‘s naval incursions continued during the first days of August, amid high tensions, and almost caused a collision between military boats from both countries.”

Additional Spanish ships were deployed to deter further breaches.

Spain‘s PM Pedro Sanchez admitted the incursions but played down their importance.



He said: “We are geographical neighbours and these kinds of incidents happen.

“It did happen, but it was resolved through dialogue at the highest level.”

Sanchez claimed communication between both countries was “very fluid” and insisted no such encounters have taken place since.



Madrid deployed its navy ship Rayo to the region on August 3 to help the official response.

It was followed quickly by the frigate Santa Maria – later replaced by the Navarra after suffering a breakdown.

The waters around Spain‘s enclave of Ceuta are a sensitive issue between Rabat and Madrid.

Spain claims a 12 nautical-mile territorial sea around the territory, but Morocco does not recognise this claim.

It is part of a long-running dispute over Ceuta and Melilla – two Spanish territories located on the African continent.



The report also comes on the eve of the first royal visit to Ceuta since 2007, which could strain Spain’s historically delicate relations with Morocco over the city’s status.

Tens of thousands of people have returned to Morocco since the mass crossing.

Earlier this month Sanchez called a snap election in the face of huge housing protests.

The beleaguered Spanish leader confirmed the move following mass demonstrations sparked by the eviction of a pensioner who has since died.

Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was kicked out of her apartment by riot police after her rent saw a huge hike.



The OAP’s plight made her a symbol of the country’s housing crisis, with hundreds of thousands of protesters turning out on the streets.

News.title: Belmarsh inmates brag of chomping on McDonald’s & watching Netflix on mobiles as they mock jail as ‘more like a holiday’
News.content:
Next

Inmates have boasted of living the high-life as they chomp on McDonald’s burgers and appear to smoke a joint at one of Britain’s highest-security jails.

The lags are also seen with illicit mobiles and Sim cards while one took a picture in his cell at Category A HMP Belmarsh as he watched Netflix.



Their antics are revealed in pictures posted on TikTok with mocking captions such as “HMP Belmarsh — more like holiday” and “His Majesty’s prison is mine”.

Sources suspect the contraband food has been brought in by a corrupt officer who was probably paid hundreds of pounds to do so.



One said: “The prisoners posting this are also taking the p*** and making a joke out of how lax the security is.

“Staff and governors need to get a grip and stop stuff like this happening inside jails where people are meant to be being punished.”



The images show one inmate at the South London jail holding a £2.59 McDonald’s double cheeseburger under the caption “HMP Royalty”.

An empty chicken wrap in McDonald’s packaging could also be seen on the lag’s table.



Another image shows an inmate watching a clip on a smuggled smart phone — with an old-fashioned brick mobile next to it.

In another video, he smokes what appears to be a joint. Another clip shows Sim cards and USB sticks.

Last night, the account which posted the images had been disabled after we alerted authorities, who had begun an investigation.

Our source said: “It’s worrying that pictures and video like this is being posted online especially at Belmarsh, which is meant to be Britain’s most secure jail.

“It’s clear that it was awash with phones and it’s highly likely staff brought in the McDonalds food — how else would it get in there?



“If inmates are boasting about this, it makes you wonder what else is going on.”

Belmarsh houses 750 to 800 male inmates, including terrorists and killers.

The Prison Service said: “Contraband has no place in prisons and those who break prison rules can face extra time behind bars.”

News.title: Supermarket fridges hacked across France as temps soar to 50C spoiling millions worth of frozen food
News.content:
IN HOT WATER Supermarket fridges hacked across France as temps soar to 50C spoiling millions worth of frozen food







Next

DEVIOUS hackers have targeted hundreds of supermarket fridges across France causing food stocks to overheat and spoil.

Millions of euros of fresh and frozen food were left rotting after a cyberattack sent some fridge and freezer temperatures soaring to 50c overnight.



The attack compromised cold-chain control software across nationwide stores of Intermarché, E.Leclerc, and Coopérative U.

The chief executive of Coopérative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the “extremely serious and unprecedented” attack.



Other major food retailers including Carrefour and Monoprix were also hit by the attack.

The hackers reportedly remotely reprogrammed cooling regulators to force a continuous defrost cycle, driving internal temperatures up to 50C.

While the full extent of the attack is still unclear, figures supplied by individual chains suggest about 500 stores were affected overall in France, according to the BBC.

French law enforcement and national cybersecurity agency ANSSI have launched an investigation to identify the perpetrators of the supermarket attack.

Store workers were stunned when they clocked in for their Monday morning shift to discover vast quantities of fresh produce, meat, dairy, and frozen goods completely ruined.

Some employees were hit with a hot rush of air from the freezer when they entered their workplace.



Carrefour said fridges in 80 of its 6,000 stores were hacked, while Monoprix said five per cent of its more than 400 stores had been hit, with food removed from sale if its condition could not be guaranteed.

But it may not just be isolated to France, as Dutch supermarket operator Ahold Delhaize, which operates the ⁠Netherlands’ largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn said it was dealing with a “security issue” in its network.

European Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen vehemently condemned the hack in a post on X and said: “Food security requires more attention at all levels.

“Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality.”

French prosecutors have opened a specific cyber-crime investigation into the incident.



The incident comes against the backdrop of growing concern over the potential havoc that can be caused in Europe in all sectors by cyber-attacks by malicious actors.

The French president, Emmanuel Macron last month ordered measures to protect France’s critical infrastructure from Russian “hybrid attacks”.

Last year, a cyber hack caused chaos across the continent after airport software was held ransom by criminals.

Airports across Europe scrambled to resume normal service after the massive attack in last September.

Heathrow, Brussels and Berlin airports all faced major disruption in its wake.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Criminals can use ransomware to inflict damage on computing systems and demand a bitcoin payment to undo the harm.

It is still not known for sure who is behind the crippling cyber attack.

News.title: Woman, 22, killed in horror A1 crash is pictured with tributes paid to ‘bubbliest girl’ as man, 31, charged with murder
News.content:
TRAGIC SMASH Woman, 22, killed in horror A1 crash is pictured with tributes paid to ‘bubbliest girl’ as man, 31, charged with murder







Next

A WOMAN killed in a horror A1 crash has been pictured as tributes flood in for the “bubbliest girl” – as cops charge a man with murder.

Elena Chiriac, 22, tragically died following a fatal two-vehicle crash on the motorway in North Yorkshire on Sunday, October 4.



North Yorkshire Police said specialist officers continue to support her family as an investigation into the shocking incident remains ongoing.

The horror unfolded on the A1 earlier this month between Junction 57 and Junction 56 near Barton.



A silver Ford Transit and a silver Volkswagen Golf – which were both travelling southbound – were involved in the collision at around 6.10pm.

Elena, from Newcastle, was tragically pronounced dead at the scene, despite the best efforts of emergency medics.



Cops have now arrested a 31-year-old man who has been charged with murder, attempted GBH and dangerous driving.

A 25-year-old man was arrested on Friday and has been charged with encouraging or assisting the commission of assault offences, believing that one or more would be carried out.

And a 24-year-old man who was arrested following the crash has been released with no further action.

A friend of Elena’s paid tribute to her on social media, adding: “Oh Elena, the bubbliest and craziest girl with a heart of absolute gold.



“Someone who would walk into a room and brighten up anybody’s day.”

Emanuel Pentecostal Church in Newcastle, which held a three-day prayer vigil in Elena’s honour, also paid tribute, saying: “With broken hearts and pain in our souls, we bid farewell to our dear young Elena Lăcrămioara Chiriac (Bibi), who has departed to the eternal.

“May God comfort and strengthen the family!”

North Yorkshire Police said in a statement that they continue to appeal for witnesses.

“If you saw either vehicle in the moments leading up to the collision or witnessed the collision itself and have not yet spoken to police, please get in touch,” they said.



“We are particularly keen to hear from drivers with dashcam footage that may have captured either vehicle before the collision or the collision itself. Even the smallest detail could prove significant to our enquiries.”

News.title: Terrifying moment machete-wielding youths brawl & swing blades at each other on UK train station platform
News.content:
Next

THIS is the terrifying moment machete-wielding youths brawl and swing blades at each other on a UK train station platform.

The horror unfolded in front of passengers at Worthing Station, West Sussex, in scenes of chaos on Sunday evening.



In shocking footage filmed from inside a train carriage, three men can be seen in a violent confrontation armed with blades.

Two of the men, dressed in black, appear to be targeting a third with one brandishing a huge machete-style knife.



The three men can be seen on the platform lunging and slashing at each other, wildly swinging their weapons in shocking scenes of violence.

Meanwhile, terrified passengers from inside a train carriage watch on in horror as the chaos unfolded.



Toward the end of the clip and as the train starts moving away, the man donning a grey tracksuit can be seen running from the other two men down the platform.

The circumstances around the incident remain unclear.



Police rushed to the scene at around 6.30pm on Sunday evening but the men had fled the scene before officers arrived.

Officers could be seen searching the area and cordoned off the station as an investigation got underway.

It’s unknown whether any of the men were injured following the altercation.

British Transport Police is now urging any witnesses or anyone with information to come forward.

A spokesperson for British Transport Police said: “We were called at around 6.30pm yesterday (October 11) to reports of an altercation involving three males on a platform at Worthing railway station.



“They were all reported to be in possession of knives and had fled the station prior to police arrival.

“Officers conducted a thorough search of the area with Sussex Police colleagues, however no one was found.

“Enquiries are ongoing. Anyone who witnessed the incident or has information that could help officers and has yet to speak to police should text BTP on 61016, or call 0800 40 50 40, using the reference 543 of 11 October.

“Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Robot ‘sexually assaults girl, 16, on livestream’ after ‘being remote controlled by teen boys’
News.content:
PAEDO BOT Robot ‘sexually assaults girl, 16, on livestream’ after ‘being remote controlled by teen boys’







Next

A ROBOT has allegedly sexually assaulted a young girl on livestream while being controlled by a group of teenage boys.

The droid is said to have crept up on and grabbed the 16-year-old by the buttocks before making “thrusting motions” , it is alleged.

Police have seized the robot following the alleged assault outside a fast-food restaurant in Germany.

The 1.2m tall red and gold device is suspected to have approached the girl while she was standing with a group of pals.





Cops rushed to the scene after being alerted and found the robot hidden in the back of a car.

A criminal investigation has now been launched to understand the full circumstances of the ordeal.

Footage circulating on TikTok shows a red and gold humanoid bot next to two men before the droid touches a girl.

The teenager appears to scream and move away after the automaton presses up against her, according to the video.



Two mobile phones as well as the robot have been seized by German cops as part of the probe.

Authorities called the ordeal an “assault” and said they were weighing up sexual harassment charges.

Cologne cops said: “A red and gold robot triggered a police operation on Cologne’s Ringstrasse in the early hours of Sunday.

“The device allegedly touched a 16-year-old girl’s buttocks and made thrusting motions against her.”



They added: “The robot’s 16-year-old owner and his 19-year-old companion are said to have filmed the alleged assault, streamed it live on social media, and acted as commentator.

“According to current findings, the teenager was with her 17- and 18-year-old friends in front of a fast-food restaurant at the corner of Palmstrasse and Hohenzollernring between 11.45pm and midnight.

“The robot, approximately 1.20 meters tall, is said to have approached the 16-year-old from behind and performed the actions.”

Emergency services found the suspects at the corner of Magnusstrasse and Hohenzollernring, cops added.

The robot was discovered in the trunk of a VW.



The 16-year-old from Wegberg had previously placed the device there, police alleged.

Authorities continued: “The criminal investigation department is now examining how the robot was functioning at the time of the incident and whether someone was deliberately controlling its movements.”

News.title: Yorkshire tiger attack - latest: Police say man mauled to death by tiger at wildlife park had visited alone
News.content:
Yorkshire Wildlife Park, which is near Doncaster, remains closed following Saturday’s tragedy — tributes to the man have been left at the scene

A man who was mauled to death by a tiger at a wildlife park on Saturday is believed to have been visiting alone.

Police said today that the visitor was not thought to have been accompanied when he was attacked at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, near Doncaster. The man had entered the animal's enclosure at the popular attraction, which remained closed today.

A South Yorkshire Police spokesperson said today: "It is not believed that the man who died at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park was being accompanied by anybody." The force will not be naming the man at the request of his family, it is understood.

A health and safety investigation has now been launched, with City of Doncaster Council leading the probe. The council said it is "deeply saddened" by the incident.

Dan Swaine, the council’s executive director of place, said: "We are deeply saddened by the incident that occurred this weekend and our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with everyone involved, including the family and loved ones of the person who tragically lost their life, those who witnessed the incident and the staff at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, as well as the emergency services who responded swiftly."

News.title: Shabana Mahmood announces review of politicians' safety after Ann Widdecombe death
News.content:
Shabana Mahmood announces review of politicians' safety after Ann Widdecombe death

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood told MPs that an attack on any politician is an attack on all as she voiced her solidarity with Nigel Farage after Ann Widdecombe's suspected killer was charged with a terrorism offence

View 2 Images Ann Widdecombe was killed in her own home in July (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

Shabana Mahmood has announced that security for MPs and senior politicians, as well as Royals, will be reviewed following Ann Widdecombe's death.

The Home Secretary told MPs that dedicated police support will be expanded to cover former MPs, party spokespeople, and others not already covered. Ms Mahmood voiced her "sympathy and solidarity" with Nigel Farage after it was alleged that the man suspected of murdering Ms Widdecombe had travelled to his home more than a year earlier.

She said: "Those who enter public life do so to serve. Robust debate and criticism are part of the job. Threats, abuse and violence are not. An attack on any individual in public life is an attack on every one of us, and it is an attack on democracy itself.

"We owe it to those public servants we have tragically lost, and to everyone who believes in a fair and open country, to ensure those who serve receive the protection they deserve."

View 2 Images Shabana Mahmood announced the new review to MPs

Former Tory MP Ms Widdecombe, who since defected to Reform UK, was killed in her Devon home in July. Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with her murder.

He also faces a charge of preparing terrorist acts, including an allegation he attempted to break into Nigel Farage's home.

Ms Mahmood announced a review will be carried out by Sir Stephen Lovegrove, who will examine whether there is adequate protection for those most at risk. This includes "high-profile individuals" including Royals, government ministers, MPs, councillors and other political figures.

The Home Office also announced that dedicated police support will be expanded to leaders of political parties who are not MPs. Also eligible are peers, former MPs, former members of the devolved parliaments and political party spokespeople.

Sir Stephen's review will fit alongside a review by former Tory minister Sir Robert Buckland, who is examining the murder of Sir David Amess MP - which will consider the security of MPs in their constituencies.

In an update to MPs, the Home Secretary said: "I start with the threat posed by terrorists and extremists. I know one case in particular will be on the minds of many in this House today.

"It is now three months since the murder of Ann Widdecombe at her home in Devon. We continue to mourn her loss. On October 2, the suspect was charged with a terrorism offence, including preparing an act of terror against the leader of Reform UK, the honourable member for Clacton (Mr Farage).

"I know that news that that happened will have been deeply distressing for the honourable member, so may I say to him and to his family, they have my profoundest sympathies at what must be an awful time. As I have said before, an attack on any one of us is an attack on us all.

"I know other members, as well as people outside of this House, have recently been contacted by the police in connection with this case. To all of those affected, may I offer the same sympathies and solidarity as I do to the honourable member for Clacton.

"Mr Speaker, at times like these, we must stand together as one House. For those who serve, politics is a calling. Robust debate and criticism are part of this job.

Article continues below

"Threats, abuse, and violence are not." Ms Mahmood paid tribute to Ms Widdecombe and murdered Tory MP Sir David Amess and Labour's Jo Cox.

News.title: Reform's 'lethal force' on small boats targets desperate human lives
News.content:
Reform's 'lethal force' on small boats targets desperate human lives

ROS WYNNE-JONES: Refugees are real people facing life-and-death choices. Political calls from Reform's Robert Jenrick for "lethal force" ignore the horrific realities driving families across the Channel

View 3 Images Kurdish Syrian family: Wadir Sale, his wife Amal, son Abdul and son Wassim, in their makeshift camp in Calais (Image: PHILIP COBURN)

Dear Robert Jenrick,

I’ll never forget meeting Wissam in Calais, on a trip to Northern France with Lord Alf Dubs. A little disabled boy with the sweetest smile, his Syrian parents were trying to keep him alive in a rubbish dump so he could get to Britain for medical treatment.

‌



‌



We could see how ill he was, and how filthy his living conditions, so we tried to get him to safety via a legal route. There weren’t any - not even for a Lord and a national newspaper, never mind for a pair of bewildered Syrians with a young family living in hell.

‌



They came by boat in the end, a hellish journey that contributed to Wissam’s death at the age of seven. His parents were torn between their son’s certain death on the rubbish dump, or his likely death following the boat journey. Are they the kind of people you’d deal with, using “lethal force”?

‌



View 3 Images Reform's Nigel Farage with Robert Jenrick (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

You see, people like you and me don’t have to face these kind of dilemmas, Robert. I wonder what you would have done? Your party, Reform UK, made a game about this kind of thing, didn’t you - a ‘small boats’ video game? It helps, doesn’t it, when these people are just pixels on a screen.

I wonder what you would do if you were one of Karim’s parents in Afghanistan? Karim was 22 when I met him. His parents were being hunted by the Taliban for being academics and had made the heartbreaking decision to try to send him to safety. He made five attempts to cross the Channel in a dinghy.

‌



“After a few hours,” he told me, “the dinghy is going down. Everyone is screaming....The people sitting at the edge - they don’t have anything to hold onto now the dinghy is deflating. With my own eyes, I see three young guys my age fall from the boat and drown... No-one counted how many people were on the boat. We didn’t know each other’s names.”

Is Karim, a quiet poet, one of the people you would target with lethal force? And, I wonder, what would you say to my friend Abdul, who lost his entire family and village in a massacre by the Janjaweed in Darfur when he was seven years old?

View 3 Images A group of migrants try to cross the channel from France to Britain on a dinghy boat (Image: AP Photo/Jean-Francois Badias)

‌



We wrote a book together called The Journey, about the years he spent seeking safety. He was 15 when the lorry he was clinging onto inside the wheel arch, stopped off the M4 in Swindon, and his second life, working with horses, began.

I’m sorry Robert, but I don’t think you would last one night in Calais, in a freezing tent, with armed police hunting you down, destroying your tent, and burning your clothes. It’s a lot tougher than chasing people around the tube.

But I’d be interested to know if you would choose to send your children to safety when the Taliban came knocking on your door? And what you’d do living on that rubbish dump with a disabled child - stay or go to sea? And where you’d go if your village had been burned to the ground?

‌



I’m not stupid. I know this is the only way it works for you - dehumanising people. Treating them like rats, or vermin. Calling them migrants, not people. And I think we know, by now, where this leads.

I know it’s autumn, so it’s ‘Small Boats’ season. By which I mean it’s ‘right-wing politicians trying to get attention’ season, as you fight like rats in a sack amongst yourselves.

And I can see your problem. Zia Yusuf keeps raising the stakes, so you have to go one bet higher. And now, we’ve reached the logical conclusion - gunning down small boats.

Article continues below

But, if you are really ready to threaten people whose shoes you have never walked in, you should at least know who you would be unleashing lethal force against.

News.title: Delta Goodrem 'absolutely gutted' as injury forces her out of Strictly Come Dancing this week
News.content:
Delta Goodrem 'absolutely gutted' as injury forces her out of Strictly Come Dancing this week

Delta Goodrem has to miss Strictly Come Dancing this week after suffering an injury and has told fans that she is "absoutely gutted" that she will not be on screen on Saturday

View 3 Images Delta Goodrem has to miss Strictly Come Dancing this week after suffering an injury (Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC/BBC Studios)

Delta Goodrem has been forced to miss Strictly Come Dancing this week after suffering an injury. Doctors have ordered her to rest and its not yet known if she will dance the following week.

‌



‌



The pop star, 41, is currently taking part in the BBC show but has now announced that she will be unable to compete in the upcoming Icons Week after injuring her rib.

‌



Delta said: “I’m absolutely gutted that a rib injury means I won’t be able to dance on Strictly this week. I’ve been loving every second of this experience, so having to sit this one out is heartbreaking - especially after the high of Saturday night.

‌



"I cannot tell you how much I love being a part of this magical show. I’m going to focus on resting and recovering, and hopefully I’ll be back on that dancefloor very soon.

View 3 Images Delta and Kai topped the leaderboard on Saturday after performing the Salsa and obtained a score of 33 from the judges (Image: PA Wire)

‌



"Thank you so much to everyone for all the love and support. It’s so appreciated. I’ll be cheering everyone on from the sidelines this week! Sending all my love, Delta."

It had been a good weekend for Delta, who is paired up with Kai Widdrington, and the former Neighbours actress and her professional partner had managed to top the leaderboard.

The pair had scored a 33 after doing the Salsa that was set to a mashup if Incognito hit Always There and the Chaka Khan classic Ain't Nobody.

‌



A spokesperson for Strictly Come Dancing said: “Due to injury, Delta Goodrem has been advised by doctors to rest and, as a result, will not dance on this weekend's Strictly Come Dancing.

View 3 Images Delta was supported by her Strictly co-stars and fans of the BBC show when she announced the news (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

"In line with the rules of the show, Delta and Kai will receive a bye through to next week when it is hoped they will be able to dance again. We wish Delta the very best as she continues her recovery."

‌



Delta, who shot to fame when she was cast on Australian soap Neighbours as a teenager before going onto enjoy huge success with hits like Innocent Eyes, was instantly supported by her Strictly co-stars when she announced the news on social media.

Nancy Xu said: "We waiting for you back with us, recover soon my beautiful girl," and her fellow professional dancer Lauren Oakley said: "Get well soon, can't wait to have you back."

Fans also rushed to the comments section, with one writing: "Hoping you feel better soon and can be back next week - really love watching you and Kai dance."

‌



Another said: "The way my heart DROPPED cuz I thought she was gonna have go retire injured from the entire series!!! We love you delta!!! Wishing for a super speedy recovery for you!!"

A third wrote: "Gutted for you Delta. Hopefully it heals up soon and you can get back to dancing," and a fourth said: "Wishing you a speedy recovery Delta and so sorry you won’t get to perform your icons dance."

When it was first announced that Delta, who also represented her home country in Eurovision earlier this year, had joined Strictly, she spoke about just how excited she was to be taking part.

Article continues below

She said: "I've been incredibly honoured to perform on many different stages throughout my career - from TV, theatre, film sets, to touring my own shows around the world.

"There is, however, one stage I’ve never stepped onto, and that is the ballroom floor! I’m absolutely thrilled to be joining Strictly and can’t wait to get started!"

News.title: Two retired police officers and their daughter dead in suspected murder-suicide in US
News.content:
Two retired police officers and their daughter dead in suspected murder-suicide in US

Investigators believe Kevin Mannix shot his wife, Ann, 65, and their 24-year-old daughter, Katie, before turning the gun on himself at their home in Strawberry, a neighbourhood in Mill Valley, California

View 3 Images Deputy Chief Ann Mannix, 65, and her 24-year-old daughter, Katie Mannix

Two retired San Francisco police officers and their daughter have died in a suspected murder-suicide in northern California, authorities say.

‌



‌



Ann Mannix, 65, and her daughter Katie, 24, are believed to have been shot dead by Kevin Mannix, 68, before he turned the gun on himself.

‌



The three bodies were found inside a home in Strawberry, a neighbourhood in Mill Valley, Marin County, on Sunday evening.

‌



Ann was formerly deputy chief of the San Francisco Police Department (SFPD), where her husband served as a police sergeant.

View 3 Images The shooting happened in a home in the Strawberry neighbourhood of Mill Valley, California (Image: ABC7)

The Marin County Sheriff’s Office said it received a report of shots being fired shortly after 5pm local time. The person who called emergency services was inside the property at the time but managed to leave safely, authorities said.

‌



The San Francisco Police Officers Association (SFPOA) confirmed the identities of the three people in a statement on Monday.

The SFPOA described Ann as "a trailblazer in our department", saying she was "the first woman to join and lead the SWAT team".

Ann went on to lead both the Field Operations and Special Operations Bureaus before retiring in 2021, according to a police announcement at the time.

‌



View 3 Images Kevin Mannix, 68, was a retired San Francisco police sergeant

Kevin retired from the SFPD in June 2018 after 27 years of service, according to a farewell letter published in the Taraval Station Newsletter.

The SFPOA said the deaths of Ann, Kevin and Katie "in a suspected murder-suicide" have left the entire SFPD community "reeling".

Article continues below

"There are no words that can fully capture the depth of this tragedy, nor are there simple answers to the painful questions we are all asking," the association said.

"To see their lives, and the life of their 24-year-old daughter Katie, end in such a horrific and senseless manner is a burden that weighs heavily on every officer, active and retired."

The sheriff’s office said there is no ongoing threat to the wider community. The investigation is continuing.

News.title: Andy Burnham statement recap - PM says Brexit status quo 'not good enough for Britain' as he updates MPs
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said he holds Nigel Farage "very significantly responsible" for Britain's failure to move forward in the last decade.

In a rare personal attack on the Reform UK chief, he tore into Brexit "lies" and questioned whether Mr Farage still has the appetite to lead.

The Prime Minister accused him of giving Britain "a decade of division and drift" - and accused Russia of interfering with the 2016 referendum.

In an interview with The Rest is Politics podcast, Mr Burnham signalled he is open to joining a migration pact with the European Union, saying the UK's ability to control its borders was weakened when it left the bloc.

Mr Burnham said: "I don't know whether Nigel Farage has got the appetite that he once had. We will see. I certainly wouldn't be one of those who would write him off. I think people have done that before at their peril.”

He added: "He's (Nigel Farage) given Britain a decade of division and drift. I would hold him very significantly responsible for our failure to move forward in the last decade."

Later this year the PM will hold a crunch summit with European leaders about ways of bringing Britain closer to its neighbours.

News.title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs 'rushed to hospital from prison with head injury'
News.content:
Sean 'Diddy' Combs 'rushed to hospital from prison with head injury'

Disgraced rapper Sean 'Diddy' Combs was reportedly rushed to hospital from prison over the weekend after suffering a head injury, the cause of which remains unknown

View 3 Images Sean 'Diddy' Combs was reportedly rushed to hospital from prison over the weekend after suffering a head injury behind bars (Image: Jordan Strauss/Invision/AP)

Sean 'Diddy' Combs was rushed to hospital from prison over the weekend, it has been claimed. The musician, 56, was jailed in October 2025 after being found guilty on prostitution-related charges, and handed a 50-month sentence following a lengthy trial.

‌



‌



Currently incarcerated at low-security federal New Jersey prison Fort Dix, it's thought that Combs suffered a head injury, the cause of which remains unclear, on Saturday, and was taken to hospital for treatment.

‌



Sources told TMZ that "the ambulance pulled out of Fort Dix around 1am," but then claimed that the injury was "not life-threatening," as it was noted that the rapper was "conscious and speaking" when he was transported back to the prison early on Saturday morning.

‌



In October last year, the musician was sentenced to four years behind bars, minus a year that he had already spent in prison.

View 3 Images The cause of the apparent head injury remains unclear (Image: Getty Images)

Upon release, he will be subjected to five years of supervised release. Combs was convicted in federal court of two counts of transportation for the purposes of prostitution. But the jury found him not guilty of the most serious offences of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking.

‌



It's expected that Diddy will be released in January of 2028. He's currently behind bars at FCI Fort Dix, having been transferred from MDC-Brooklyn in October. A representative for the rapper said at the time that Diddy "is an active participant in the Residential Drug Abuse Program (RDAP)" and takes the process "seriously".

Ahead of his sentencing last year, Diddy wrote a four-page apology letter to the judge, where he claimed: "I literally lost my mind. I'm sorry for that and always will be… I lost my way. My downfall was rooted in my selfishness.

"I have been humbled and broken to my core… The old me died in jail, and a new version of me was born. Prison will change you or kill you – I choose to live."

‌



View 3 Images The rapper was handed a 50-month sentence after being convicted on two counts of transportation for the purposes of prostitution (Image: AP)

In December last year, Diddy's legal team pleaded with an appeals court to release him from prison. They claimed in a filing with the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Manhattan that Combs was treated harshly at sentencing by a federal judge who let evidence surrounding charges he was acquitted of unjustly influence the punishment.

At sentencing, Judge Arun Subramanian said that when calculating the prison term, he considered Combs' treatment of two former girlfriends who testified that the Bad Boy Records founder beat them and coerced them into having sex with male sex workers while he watched and filmed the encounters, sometimes masturbating.

News.title: Met Office weather maps warn 55 areas to face rain on Tuesday – full list of areas affected
News.content:
Met Office weather maps warn 55 areas to face rain on Tuesday – full list of areas affected

The Met Office's forecast is of heavy rain, which is set to sweep southeastwards across the UK on Tuesday — becoming the strongest over parts of the Northwest of England

View 3 Images Rain is forecast for Tuesday (Image: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock)

Striking weather maps show dozens of areas across the UK will be battered by heavy downpours tomorrow morning — but temperatures will remain "very mild".

‌



‌



The rain will make a seemingly timid start at around 9pm tonight in south Wales, with some patches of rain also developing in Devon and Scotland. Heavy rain will then take over most of Northern Ireland and the western Scottish Highlands overnight, the Met Office says.

‌



This will move easterly and evolve, turning into heavy rain by 5am, when most of Scotland will be covered. By 6am, heavy rainfall will also cover most of Wales as the band of rain continues to move east throughout the morning.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Precipitation levels at 5am tomorrow, with the red areas indicating up to 32mm/hour of rainfall (Image: Met Office)

Storm Rachel batters California with fears more misery on the way READ MORE :

Shortest day of the year 2026: Exact date and time of winter solstice READ MORE :

Most areas across England will experience patches of heavy rain at various points during the morning as a result. More moderate to heavy rain will then cover Scotland into the afternoon, with some patches also above Northern Ireland. A total of 55 areas will be covered by heavy rain across the UK tomorrow.

‌



Meanwhile, England and Wales will remain largely dry throughout the afternoon and evening. Some areas in the North West, however, will still be hit by moderate to heavy rain throughout the afternoon. By the evening, most of the rain will have cleared all across the UK, precipitation maps from the Met Office show. The level of precipitation will vary between 0.5 and 32mm/hour.

An outlook for tonight provided by the forecaster reads: "Gales developing across northern Scotland this evening. Staying cloudy for many areas overnight, with outbreaks of rain and drizzle. A spell of heavy rain will move into the northwest during the early hours. A very mild night to come."

Regarding tomorrow, the Met Office said: "Heavy rain will move southeastwards across England and Wales during the morning with blustery winds, but turning drier and brighter in the afternoon. Heavy showers move into the north later."

‌



View 3 Images The areas covered by rain at 7am (Image: Met Office)

Alex Deakin, Met Office meteorologist, explained that despite the heavy rain, temperatures will be "very mild" and hold around 14-15C overnight in the south, with some places even reaching 16-17C. He said a spell of "quite heavy rain" will then move across Northern Ireland and much of Scotland by 4-5am tomorrow, with some of the precipitations also covering the west coast of Wales initially.

Mr Deakin said: "Tuesday will start pretty wet through central and southern Scotland, northwest England and much of Wales. A narrowing band of rain moving across all of England as we go though Tuesday morning. [...] Much brighter skies follow on behind, with plenty of sunshine in the Midlands, south Wales and southern England on Tuesday afternoon."
