Gabriel Magalhães is likely to be partnered by Ezri Konsa again against the Brazil defender’s former club on Tuesday. Gabriel insisted he would not hesitate to take another penalty in a shootout despite missing the crucial spot-kick in the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain. “I was sad, and I didn’t want to miss a penalty, but I have learned from this and if I have another opportunity, I will be ready to take it,” he said.

Sports.title: Almost half of female footballers considering retiring early, players’ union survey shows
Sports.content:
Almost half of female footballers are considering leaving the sport because of financial concerns or psychological stress, and 57% have struggled with their mental health, according to a report highlighting the working conditions for players worldwide.

About 800 players were surveyed by the global players’ union, Fifpro, for the report, which found that average club wages have tripled in the women’s game since 2017 but also raised concerns about the gulf in pay and the support provided to players. Fifpro said “average pay is not significantly higher than national minimum wage levels” in many regions.

Quick Guide How do I 

The report, entitled Working Conditions in Women’s Football, heard that 49% of players were considering leaving football earlier than planned. Of those more than half cited financial reasons and 46% pointed to psychological stress as the reason.

Only 56% of players surveyed had an individual employment contract, and only 13% receive a club pension. The average contract length has risen from 12 months in 2017 to 19 months, but financial uncertainty remains for players. The average monthly wage of those surveyed – nearly half of whom play for their countries, and over half of whom have a university degree – was $2,601 (£1,966), but that is inflated by a small proportion of much higher earners. The median monthly salary was only $1,669 (£1,261). Only 76% of players said they were always paid fully and on time and 5% had experienced delays of more than three months to be paid.

“Away from the best-resourced clubs, there is a recurring theme of precarity and fragile conditions,” Fifpro’s director of women’s football, Alex Culvin, said. “The women’s football industry has come a long way, [but] for the rest of the industry, there is a hell of a long way to go.

“The professionalisation of women’s football is accelerating in some parts of the world and, as our report highlights, revenues are increasing. However, the progress and benefits are not evenly distributed among players across the world.

“At the most basic level, regulatory and policy intervention is required to ensure that players in some countries are not left behind – a rising tide lifts all boats. These interventions should focus on salary, facilities, staffing, performance and health of players. Resource allocation and access are key to a thriving employment market. This is not just about players earning enough to make a living from football but also making sure they have a safe and stable environment.”

The players were asked whether their club employed enough staff to fulfil players’ needs, and 47% said no.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The former England and Chelsea defender Millie Bright – who, when she ended her highly decorated career in April said: “I’ve given all I can” – told Fifpro’s media channels that creating an environment where players can ask for help with their mental health without judgment was essential.

“You’re a little bit embarrassed to say that you’re struggling a little bit, so you just hide it and just keep playing,” she said. “A big thing for me in mental health is the environment and the culture. To have a positive impact, it needs consistency and daily behaviours.”

Sports.title: Six questions facing England as they target next year’s Women’s World Cup
Sports.content:
England have two jobs to do on Tuesday. The first, avoiding an almighty upset and progressing past Greece on aggregate in their Women’s World Cup playoff to reach a final tie, should be a formality for one of the world’s best-resourced teams. The second, honing their style to play like contenders for next summer’s World Cup in Brazil, is a far trickier but crucial challenge.

Friday’s relatively uninspiring 3-1 first-leg victory in Crete left room for improvement and England had plenty to work on as they trained at St George’s Park on Monday under gloomy-looking clouds. More broadly, over the next eight months, there are six questions facing the European champions.

Can England defend well enough to win a world title?

England had 58 touches in Greece’s box and turned that into three goals, whereas Greece had two touches in England’s box but managed to score and hit the crossbar. Sarina Wiegman said she was not happy her team had conceded. Their defending in June’s 4-0 defeat by Spain also left much to be desired, and it feels as if England are not yet certain about who should be the captain Leah Williamson’s centre-back partner. Wiegman mentioned on Monday that stopping counterattacks was something they must fix – they also struggled defending quick breaks in April 2025 when losing in Belgium. That year, they found a way to win the Euros but they must tighten up defensively if they want to win a first world title in the Maracanã in July.

Why are the forwards not clicking?

England were wasteful in the final third in Greece and not for the first time in recent months. In the World Cup qualifying group England were 1-0 and 2-0 winners over Iceland in games where they should have scored more. A ruthless Spain, the world’s No 1 side, secured 6-1 and 3-0 wins over Iceland. On Monday Wiegman was asked what one element of Friday’s performance she would most like to improve and replied: “The execution in the final third. We got in good positions but then it’s [about] staying onside, having the final pass, the right pass at the right moment, the run at the right time, and deciding what cross or cutback you’re going to choose.”

View image in fullscreen England preparing for the second leg against Greece on Tuesday. Photograph: Jacob King/PA

Who should start in attacking midfield?

For the past year, it has repeatedly felt as if Wiegman does not know who should start as the No 10, with Jess Park, Lucia Kendall and Laura Blindkilde Brown given chances along with Lauren James. Dropping – and recalling – Ella Toone, plus the late addition of Grace Clinton to this squad, adds mystery. Erica Meg Parkinson’s debut on Friday adds another youngster into the mix, and Beth Mead can also play as a 10. Asked on Friday whether the No 10 position had the most question marks surrounding it, Wiegman said: “There’s a lot of competition on that position, where we have a lot of options, which also means, tactically, we can do different things. You can call it a ‘question mark’ – I call it many options.”

What about the right wing?

England’s left-wing starting position feels nailed on for Lauren Hemp, who has been in tremendous form for Manchester City. The right side, however, looks uncertain, not least because Chloe Kelly has been left out. James, England’s most technically gifted player, would be the first choice for many, but she can also play centrally, and the uncapped Freya Godfrey has impressed for London City Lionesses. On Friday, Blindkilde Brown started on the right before being replaced at half-time by Mead. Whoever starts, there are only a handful of matches before next summer to build fluidity.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Laura Blinkilde Brown started at right wing in the first leg against Greece. Photograph: InTime Sports/AP

Which youngsters should be given a chance?

There have been growing calls for the 20-year-old Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter to be handed her debut and the 21-year-old Godfrey could be in line for her debut on Tuesday. If England held a greater first-leg advantage, England would surely be more likely to experiment in Leicester, although Wiegman confirmed she would make changes. Keira Walsh said of her Chelsea teammate Potter that it was “a really good thing that she’s finally being appreciated for how good she is”, and added: “Her intelligence gives me confidence, knowing that she’s perfectly capable of stopping the counter.” There has also been praise for Parkinson, with Esme Morgan, who has played against Parkinson in the NWSL, describing the 18-year-old as a “smart player, really tidy on the ball, with incredibly good movement”. It remains to be seen whether Wiegman will opt for youth or experience as the season progresses.

Do England need clarity over Wiegman’s future?

Off the pitch, the biggest unknown facing England is the future of Wiegman, whose contract runs until the end of the World Cup. There have been no reasons to suspect the squad are unsettled by the uncertainty, but the topic is likely to be mentioned in every England press conference until there is clarity. Walsh said on Monday: “Obviously I’d want her to stay. I think everyone in England would love her to stay. I really appreciate her as a manager but it’s her decision.” Wiegman did not wish to discuss the matter, saying: “We’re only focused on Greece and I don’t want to talk about me.”

Sports.title: Leicester takeover deadline extended with £200m asking price questioned
Sports.content:
Leicester City have extended the deadline for a takeover of the club to Friday, October 16, talkSPORT understands.

The Foxes had initially given prospective buyers until September 14 to complete a deal to buy the club.

3 Prospective buyers have until Friday to wrap up a deal to buy the Foxes after the initial deadline was extended by over a month Credit: Getty

However, an extension has been made due to interested parties seeking more time to conclude their purchase.

At least one American consortium are showing interest in buying Leicester.

Meanwhile, Scottish-Indian businessman Neil Lal claims to be in the race.

Lal has yet to enter the process of a takeover with the relevant stakeholders, though.

But Leicester's current asking price could still prove to be a stumbling block for any prospective buyer.

The owners' valuation of over £200million, plus inherited debt, is being viewed as steep by those who have enquired about a deal so far.

King Power's Leicester reign

King Power have owned the Foxes for 16 years after purchasing the club back in August 2010.

Chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has been in the role since 2018 after taking over from his late father, Vichai.

Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha bought the club from Milan Mandaric and remained chairman until his tragic death in a helicopter crash eight years later.

Under King Power's ownership, Leicester clinched promotion back to the Premier League in 2014 following a 10-year absence from the top-flight.

3 King Power and Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha are looking to sell Leicester, but prosepective buyers have doubts over his valuation Credit: Getty

The club went on to win the title two years later under Claudio Ranieri despite being 5000-1 outsiders.

Leicester also won the FA Cup for the first time in their history in 2021.

However, recent seasons have seen the club struggle on the pitch, suffering two relegations from the Premier League in three years.

Last term saw the Foxes drop into the third-tier for the first time in 17 years after a second-successive relegation at the end of last season.

Russell Martin's side currently sit 17th in League One after winning just two of their opening eight matches.

Their latest defeat to Peterborough United on Saturday has left the Leicester boss under mounting pressure.

3 Martin's side have made a slow start in League One this season Credit: Getty

Martin has been warned his days in charge are numbered following the 3-1 home loss.

The Foxes boss was appointed this summer on a three-year deal through to 2029.

Sports.title: Emmanuel Petit backs Arsene Wenger for FIFA President – but there could be one key issue
Sports.content:
Emmanuel Petit backs Arsene Wenger for FIFA President – but there could be one key issue

Arsene Wenger has been endorsed for the FIFA presidency by one of his former Arsenal players.

However, talkSPORT's Simon Jordan doubts he will win the upcoming election.



4 Wenger has been urged to challenge for the FIFA presidency in March with Infantino still running for election Credit: Getty

The 77th FIFA Congress will be held in Rabat, Morocco in March, with a presidential election also taking place at the summit.

Incumbent president Gianni Infantino is running for re-election despite losing the support of multiple national federations.

The FA is amongst those to have pulled their backing for Infantino following his failed FIFA Forward Enterprise plans to sell private equity in tournaments such as the World Cup.



Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega is the only other confirmed candidate.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is also considering challenging Infantino in the election, though.



Wenger backed for FIFA presidency

Meanwhile, there have been calls for Wenger to enter the race, a suggestion which Emmanuel Petit supports.

Speaking on Monday's White & Jordan, his fellow Frenchman was asked about the clamour for his former Gunners boss to run for the FIFA presidency.



Petit explained: "When he was a manager, Arsene, I had a huge respect and we have a long relationship between us.

"But when he was a manager, I remember how many times he was fighting against UEFA or FIFA for any decisions and he was always protecting the club interest and the players.

"Now that he stopped and joined FIFA, maybe he’s playing a role actually. Keeping his head down and not making any noise, trying to walk step by step until the top.

4 Wenger has worked with FIFA since 2019 as chief of global football development Credit: Getty



"That’s probably his strategy because I was very surprised when he joined FIFA, but now he represents himself.

"He was so close to Infantino since he arrived at FIFA, that I’m quite surprised. Now, maybe I understand why he joined FIFA, for this moment.

"I think if you want to change something in football then you need to get on top of it, to get the power to change it.

"(Michel) Platini tried to do that and he was kicked off very easily. So I don’t know, but I’m very happy he’s putting his name on the next election because Infantino, the door is over there."



Wenger has worked with FIFA as their chief of global football development since 2019.

He took on the role after leaving Arsenal the previous year following a tenure which spanned almost 22 years.

4 Petit won a Premier League title under Wenger at Arsenal Credit: Getty

The 76-year-old has faced criticism at times, though, notably for his radical proposals which included moving the World Cup to two-year cycle.



Petit continued: "I think he has the knowledge of football, he’s intelligent as well, he knows how FIFA is running now, he knows everybody that’s important as well in this institution and I think he’s got some ideas.

"Not the ones he presented as soon as he came into FIFA, he wanted to get a World Cup every two seasons, but I think it’s probably a strategy from him to get into the top of it and to change things.

"I hope, but I’m not a kid, I’m not stupid, I’m not naive. I know that the system won’t change, but if Arsene can replace Infantino, he was a manager in football, Infantino knows nothing."

Jordan doubts Wenger will run

But Jordan is not convinced Wenger will put himself forward.

The former Crystal Palace chairman admitted: "As much as we might think that Wenger could potentially fulfil that role, I think it would destroy any influence they then had over the football side of the operation that he has supposedly been running for them.



4 Infantino is set to run for re-election in March at the 77th FIFA Congress Credit: Getty

"Which is developed with the next generation of footballers and the way that money is distributed around the federations.

"I don’t think Infantino is going anywhere anytime soon and if you haven’t done him in by now, I don’t think you’re going to do him in by February."

When asked by Petit if Wenger has a chance, he replied: "I don’t think he is going to put himself forward."



Candidates must submit their nominations for the election by November 18.

They must also have the support of at least five FIFA member nations.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi names Max Dowman, Arsenal target and Crystal Palace signing among 10 future stars
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has updated his list of football's 10 future stars with Arsenal's Max Dowman among two Premier League players named.

Shortly after his emotional farewell to international football, the 39-year-old has fittingly picked the youngsters who he believes will shape the game's next generation.

6 Messi bid farewell to the international scene shortly after netting his 126th and final goal for Argentina Credit: Getty

Messi has previously highlighted the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold, Phil Foden, Jadon Sancho and Mason Mount as his top wonderkids.

Six years on from his original list, the Inter Miami superstar is now in his third iteration of naming the young stars he is tipping for the top.

Messi’s 10 future stars he believes are football's ‘next chapter’

Can Uzun

The Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder is one of the more senior names on Messi's list despite still only being at the tender age of 20.

The German-born 10-cap Turkey international has scored 19 goals and provided 12 assists in 65 Bundesliga matches thus far in his career.

Tomás Aranda

Messi has named just one of his compatriots in his new list, with Boca Juniors talent Aranda earning rave reviews back in Argentina.

The 19-year-old only made his professional debut in January but was handed his senior international debut five months later.

Aranda had registered one assist in six league games for his club since the World Cup before he fractured a fibula in his right leg.

6 Aranda is one of Argentina's brightest young talents and is said to be wanted by several Premier League giants Credit: Getty

Max Dowman

The future of Arsenal is fresh from receiving three Guinness World Record certificates as a reward for his historic debut season.

The teenager, who made his senior debut in August 2025, became the Premier League’s youngest ever goalscorer last year en route to helping the Gunners win their first top-flight title for 22 years.

Dowman, who was drafted into first-team training at age 14, has been tipped by Simon Jordan to become a world-beater like Lamine Yamal.

6 Dowman became the youngest ever Premier League winner in May Credit: Getty

The England Under-19 international, whose heroics last season have seen John Terry and Henry Winter already compare him to Messi and Kaka, has already made an imperious start to the new campaign.

The 16-year-old earned the Carabao Cup Player of the Round award following his two goals against Ipswich last month, which saw him join an exclusive club alongside Wayne Rooney.

Gilberto Mora

The 17-year-old Mexican, one of the breakout stars at Liga MX club Tijuana, has been strongly linked with both Arsenal and Liverpool.

The attacking midfielder underlined his status as his country's top talent by starting the 3-2 defeat against England at the Azteca in July.

In the round before, Mora became the youngest starter in a World Cup knockout tie after Pele, across the four appearances he made.

Since returning from the tournament, he has scored five goals and registered an assist in seven outings for his boyhood club.

6 Gilberto Mora made four appearances for Mexico at the World Cup - including against England - and recently scored his first senior international goal Credit: Getty

Zavier Gozo

The 19-year-old has been rewarded for making the step up to the Premier League with his first senior appearance for the US national team.

Crystal Palace signed the highly-rated American prospect from Real Salt Lake for a reported £11.1million in August.

Gozo, who made his MLS debut as a 16-year-old in October 2023, scored six goals in RSL's first 16 league games of the year.

He endured a baptism of fire on his Premier League bow by coming off the bench in the 4-1 defeat to Manchester City, and has also enjoyed a late cameo in the 3-2 loss to Ipswich Town last month.

6 Gozo made his senior United States debut in the 4-1 win over Peru last month and is trying to break into Crystal Palace's first team Credit: Getty

Jesús Rodríguez

The 20-year-old is hoping to go from strength to strength under Arsenal and Chelsea legend Cesc Fabregas at Como in Italy.

The two-cap Spain international started the club's first Serie A game of the season but has since had to make do with a substitute role.

Rodriguez is still waiting on his first goal contribution across four outings, and was even sent-off for Spain's Under-21s last month.

The ex-Real Betis talent, who scored twice and registered nine assists in 31 Serie A games last year, set up Mario Martin's goal for 12-0 against San Marino before he saw red a few minutes later.

Kees Smit

Earlier this year, Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand told talkSPORT that he didn't want his old club to miss out on Smit.

The 20-year-old Netherlands midfielder had previously been named as one of the stars to watch in Europe at the start of last season.

talkSPORT even revealed that Newcastle and Crystal Palace were competing with Real Madrid to sign the AZ Alkmaar star.

However, no summer move to the Premier League transpired, and Smit has registered two assists in five Eredivisie matches this term.

6 Smit was a surprise omission from the Netherlands' World Cup squad after his impressive season Credit: Getty

Chloe Sarwie

Messi also named three future stars of women's football in his list, with Chelsea's Sarwie the headline selection for England fans.

The 17-year-old made seven senior appearances for Chelsea last season and was in the Lionesses squad for the Under-20 World Cup.

Giovanna Waksman

The Brazilian youth international only joined OL Lyonnes in March, having first come through the ranks at Botafogo in her homeland.

The 17-year-old is still waiting for her first senior appearance at club level this season but is in double digits for goals for Brazil's U17s.

Lotta Wrede

The 18-year-old has made three appearances in the Frauen-Bundesliga this season with her childhood Hamburg outfit.

The club's No.32 has also scored three times in nine appearances for Germany's Under-19s and has been linked with a move to Barcelona.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a pity’ – Emmanuel Petit explains Arsenal relationship as fans make complaints known
Sports.content:
Emmanuel Petit has voiced his disappointment over the growing disconnect between Arsenal and its supporters.

The Frenchman appeared on talkSPORT's White and Jordan to discuss all things Gunners, where he enjoyed a trophy-laden three-year stint between 1997 and 2000.



4 Petit made 118 appearances and scored 11 goals for Arsenal but now feels there is a disconnect building between the club and fans Credit: Getty

Petit became a club icon in north London as his all-action midfield displays helped deliver Premier League and FA Cup glory.

While the 56-year-old also enjoyed huge success at first club Monaco, as well as stints at Barcelona and London rivals Chelsea, he remains a popular figure at Arsenal.

However, the former midfielder believes his old team may be losing touch with their fanbase.



Premier League clubs have come in for increased criticism in recent years over rising ticket prices, with Arsenal no exception.

Ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, the Gunners announced a 3.9 per cent average increase on season tickets - the fifth year in a row that the Premier League champions have increased their prices.



And Petit admitted he has become aware of this himself after a recent interaction with an Arsenal supporters' group, as he bemoaned the transactional relationship between club and fans.

Petit: Times have changed at Arsenal

Appearing on talkSPORT, Petit shared his experience visiting the Arsenal Fans Association in Denmark, where he joined up with former teammate and fellow icon Freddie Ljungberg to greet supporters.



But the 1998 World Cup winner revealed fans were growing disillusioned with the club, before admitting there is a similar feeling among their former players.

Petit said: “They are saying the same thing - that they are not fans anymore, they are customers. And the relationship they had before with Arsenal, it's not the same anymore.

“I said, 'Don't be surprised, because as former players, it's kind of the same with us'.

4 Petit enjoyed a League and FA Cup double in the 1997/98 season with the Gunners Credit: Getty



4 Despite rising ticket prices, Arsenal's fans continues to pack their 60,000 capacity Emirates Stadium Credit: Getty

Explaining why he feels a lack of connection with Arsenal, Petit explained that the club have never approached him over an ambassadorial role, but insisted he will never ask for opportunities.

He continued: "There are a few exceptions, with former Arsenal players that link with Arsenal and they do events around the world.

“I'm not asking Arsenal to call me tomorrow for that. But I've never received anything. They never asked me to do anything for them.



“Every time I represent Arsenal, it's because of the company [his talent agency], but nothing from the club.

"So it was a pity for me to hear that, because the fans are so important. They regard themselves as customers."

Sharing his disappointment over the fans' disillusionment, Petit said he was 'embarrassed' by Arsenal for keeping them at arm's length.

4 Petit shared his disappointment over Arsenal's lack of relationship with its fans Credit: talkSPORT



The Frenchman said: “For me, they are the most important pieces in the football industry. If there are no fans, no customers, no money at all, they are buying for everything.

“And that's what I said to them. I'm very happy and honoured to be in Copenhagen because of you, because of what you're doing with us, former players, we still live through your memories. And it's amazing.

“But the fact that they were so disappointed with the club, I felt embarrassed."

Urging Arsenal to do better, he added: “I understand it's a business. I understand there are customers. But I think at the end, this is not a common industry. Football matters.



“It’s different than a normal company because of the fans. So you have to take care of your fans. You have to protect them. You have to build something alongside the fans.

“And this is not happening anymore.”

Sports.title: Alvaro Arbeloa under intense pressure as Fulham manager after just six Premier League games
Sports.content:
Alvaro Arbeloa under intense pressure as Fulham manager after just six Premier League games

Alvaro Arbeloa is under intense pressure to save his job as Fulham manager.

The Spaniard is in trouble after just three months in charge at Craven Cottage.

3 Arbeloa has collected just two points from six matches as Fulham boss Credit: Getty

Arbeloa is yet to win a Premier League match as Cottagers boss, picking up just two points from their opening six matches.

Saturday's humbling late defeat at Ipswich Town also saw his side sink to the bottom of the table.

Arbeloa under pressure

talkSPORT understands this coming weekend's home meeting with Hull City is now a must-win fixture, despite the Tigers' good form - losing just once in six.

The following week's trip to fellow strugglers Coventry City is also seen as crucial to Arbeloa's future.

It comes after the 43-year-old signed a three-year deal as Marco Silva's successor back in July.

Silva left the club to join Portuguese giants Benfica in the summer following five years in charge in west London.

The role marks Arbeloa's second in senior management after five months as Real Madrid boss last season.

Across 28 matches in all competitions, Arbeloa collected 18 wins with Los Blancos.

However, losses to Chelsea, Sunderland, Crystal Palace and now Ipswich have piled the pressure on Arbeloa in his new job.

Fulham's only wins under their current boss have so far been in this season's Carabao Cup.

3 Arbeloa faces a must-win clash with Hull this weekend Credit: Getty

Victories over AFC Wimbledon and West Ham United have set up a fourth round tie with Palace later this month.

Arbeloa on 'unlucky' Fulham

Speaking during his post-match press conference on Saturday, Arbeloa told reporters: "We were a little bit unlucky, but we need to improve.

"It doesn’t matter if you concede in the first minute or the last. As a coach, I don’t like to concede goals.

"When you give the ball away so easily, the opposition will attack you, and we must change our mentality when we score.

"I am so happy with many things that my team are doing, and I know it is not easy for them.

"The most important thing is Fulham’s position, and we need points. It’s a massive game for us at home next week, and we need to be ready."

3 Fulham conceded a 92nd minute winner against Ipswich last time out Credit: Getty

This season marks Fulham's fifth successive campaign in the Premier League.

Since promotion in 2022, they have not finished lower than 13th in the table.

Sports.title: Where to watch Atletico Madrid v Manchester United plus talkSPORT commentary for blockbuster
Sports.content:
Where to watch Atletico Madrid v Manchester United plus talkSPORT commentary for blockbuster

Manchester United will hope to put their Premier League woes behind them as they prepare to face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

The Red Devils beat Sabah 4-0 upon their return to the continental competition last month, while Atletico started the league phase with a 2-1 defeat to Liverpool.



3 Shaw was involved in the situation which seen Bentancur's being sent off for Tottenham Credit: Getty

This is an important match for under-pressure United boss Michael Carrick.

Carrick's men were held to another draw against Tottenham on Saturday in the Premier League despite Spurs being down to ten men.

Diego Simeone's side, meanwhile, have had a strong start to their domestic season having won their last four matches.



The Red Devils have never beaten Atletico, with two of their last four meetings resulting in victory for the Spanish side.

The United boss has also been hit with a double injury blow as Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo missed Manchester United training on Monday.



Shaw started Saturday's clash at Old Trafford but was replaced in stoppage time by Ayden Heaven.

Mainoo, who withdrew from England duty during the break, played the full 90 minutes at the weekend.



Also missing from Monday's session was Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui as they recover from their respective injuries.

United training squad for Atletico Goalkeepers: Lammens, Heaton, Mee Defenders: Maguire, De Ligt, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Martinez, Yoro, Heaven Midfielders: Mount, J. Fletcher, Tielemans, Baleba, Santos, Fernandes Forwards: Lacey, Zirkzee, Mbeumo, Rashford, Cunha, Amad

3 Simeone's men will be playing an English side in the Champions League for a second time this season Credit: AFP

Where to watch Atletico v Manchester United

This European tie will kick-off at 8pm on Tuesday, October 13.

It is being played at the Spanish outfit's home stadium of the Metropolitano Stadium.

The last clash between Atletico and United in Madrid came in February 2022, with the two teams drawing 1-1.



talkSPORT will be providing live commentary with Adrian Durham, alongside Ian Danter and former England captain Stuart Pearce.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Additionally, fans in the UK can watch the match on Prime Video - with build-up starting from 6:30pm.

Prime Video signed a new contract that means they will broadcast the top-pick Tuesday match through to the 2030/31 season.

The matches will be available to Prime Video members at no additional cost.



3 Mainoo played the full match after resting over the international break Credit: Getty

Manchester United 'fresh start'

Following their draw with Spurs, Carrick said: "We definitely had a tough spell in the game early on. That’s pretty obvious.

"The positive is that we worked through that, and the second half was much better.

"There are certainly things we can improve, but there are fine lines within that as well. We’ve got to stay positive and keep doing the right things.



"We’ve got games coming up, and we’ve got to be ready for them and embrace the challenge. It’s a big challenge, a great challenge, and we’re more than capable of winning games.

"We've got big games coming up and are looking forward to Tuesday now [at Atletico].

"A fresh start, a fresh game and we will go there looking forward to the game."

Sports.title: What time is LASK v Liverpool? Reds in early Champions League slot as Iraola looks to bounce back
Sports.content:
What time is LASK v Liverpool? Reds in early Champions League slot as Iraola looks to bounce back

Liverpool travel to Austria to face LASK in the Champions League this week, with Andoni Iraola's men looking to hit back after their loss to Manchester City.

Following a highly anticipated matchup against Enzo Maresca's City, the Reds will hope for better against LASK, who currently sit third in the Austrian Bundesliga.



3 The loss against City was Iraola's first as Liverpool manager Credit: Getty

The Merseyside-outfit is coming off the back of Ryan Gravenberch being sent off before Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored to sink Liverpool.

Iraola had become the first manager since Joe Fagan to avoid defeat in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool.

However, their top-flight form of two wins, three draws and now a defeat shows the difficulty the ex-Bournemouth boss has faced at Anfield.



Liverpool did win their first Champions League fixture of the season, beating Diego Simeone’s Atletico Madrid 2-0 last month.

Despite that win, Liverpool have been warned by European football commentator Kevin Hatchard not to misjudge LASK.



On talkSPORT's Trans Euro Express, Hatchard said: "This is one of those where LASK have done brilliantly to get there.

"We saw what they did to Celtic over two legs in the play-off. They came back from 4-0 down on aggregate.



"This is one of those classic games where if Liverpool are even slightly off it, they could come unstuck."

3 Liverpool fans are still waiting for Wirtz to fully click into gear Credit: Getty

How to follow LASK v Liverpool

This Champions League league phase tie will take place on Wednesday, October 14.

The match has been picked for the early slot so will kick off at 5:45pm UK time.



It is being held at the Raiffeisen Arena in Linz, Austria.

talkSPORT will have commentary from Joe Shennan and former England striker Dean Ashton.

LASK v Liverpool team news

Regarding injured players such as Dominik Szoboszlai, Cody Gakpo, and Alexander Isak, Iraola was unable to confirm whether they would be fit enough to return for the Champions League fixture.



After the City loss, he said: "It'll be difficult because it's two days. You never know."
