Sports.title: Lucas Bahdi Threatens To Put Shakur Stevenson To Sleep
Sports.content:
Lucas Bahdi turned Shakur Stevenson’s “F-level fighter” insult back on him, claiming he would knock Shakur out and telling him to focus on getting Zuffa Boxing to book his next fight.

Shakur is grading other fighters while his own next bout remains unsettled. Bahdi spotted the obvious opening: he has been in the ring with Floyd Schofield, while Shakur is still talking about who he might fight.

“Well this ‘F level fighter’ would put your little running ass on the canvas and to Zzzzzz,” Bahdi said on X. “Keep focused on Zuffa actually getting you a fight.”

That was his response to Shakur’s October 10 post: “A C lever fighter beat a F level fighter!!”

The knockout claim is something Bahdi would have to prove. Getting to Shakur would require cutting off the ring and landing against a fighter who gives opponents few clean opportunities. Bahdi’s willingness to trade with Schofield doesn’t tell us how he would handle that task.

His comment about Zuffa is harder to ignore. Shakur has been discussing potential opponents, but negotiations don’t keep a fighter active. Until those talks produce a date, Bahdi can point to the difference between fighting and commenting on everyone else.

The “F-level” label also looks excessive when placed beside Shakur’s own opposition at lightweight. He fought Shuichiro Yoshino, Edwin De Los Santos, Artem Harutyunyan, Josh Padley and William Zepeda. Zepeda is the best answer to criticism of that run. The rest leave room for an argument about how far below them Bahdi really belongs.

De Los Santos would be a difficult opponent for Bahdi because of his speed, power, and southpaw stance. Even so, there is a reasonable case that Bahdi could compete with several fighters Shakur faced at 135. Dismissing him with a letter avoids explaining what makes him so inferior.

Shakur has zero room to be handing out letter grades to anyone right now. That signature win over Teofimo Lopez gave him all the momentum in the world, but sitting on the shelf degraded that goodwill in a hurry. Fans have short memories, and prolonged inactivity turns yesterday’s masterclass into old news.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol vs Callum Smith Confirmed For December 12
Sports.content:
Matchroom Boxing made it official: Dmitry Bivol defends his unified light heavyweight titles against Callum Smith on December 12 in Yekaterinburg, Russia. Everyone knew this matchup was coming, but now Smith finally has an exact calendar date locked in.

This marks Bivol’s second ring appearance following his brutal rematch win over Artur Beterbiev last year. A back procedure slowed his calendar down, which left Smith on standby while putting the trilogy on pause.

Smith brings solid credentials, yet he isn’t who the crowd was craving. Bivol holds one win, Beterbiev holds one win, so fight fans wanted that tiebreaker settled first. Beating Smith keeps Bivol active, but it won’t satisfy everyone holding out for chapter three.

The downtime hurt Smith’s momentum, too. He hasn’t competed since taking down Joshua Buatsi. Taking on David Morrell during the wait never appealed to him because a loss would have erased his title shot entirely.

Sitting tight preserved his golden ticket, though it leaves him walking into his biggest light heavyweight test with noticeable ring rust. Timing Bivol’s footwork without warm-up rounds will be tough.

Both guys share nearly identical ages, so youth won’t decide this one. Smith must capitalize on his height advantage alongside his trademark left hook. Lingering effects from Bivol’s spinal surgery could play a huge role as well.

Smith can’t just trail Bivol around the canvas. If the champion darts in, connects, then vanishes, Smith will quickly fall behind on the scorecards.

December 12 settles things for these two fighters. The true blockbuster boxing fans really crave still sits on ice.

Smith showed his ceiling against both Canelo Alvarez and Beterbiev. When the elite guys close distance, take away his range, or refuse to stand in front of his left hook, his plan disappears. Beterbiev wore him out by applying physical pressure and breaking his guard, while Canelo neutralized him by taking away the left arm and dictating every inch of real estate.

Against Beterbiev, Smith looked battered and overmatched. Now going up against Bivol, he risks looking flat-footed and technically outclassed. The problem for Smith is that sitting on the shelf for eighteen months while waiting for Bivol to heal from back surgery could backfire on him.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois–Fabio Wardley Rematch Carries Thin PPV Card
Sports.content:
Saturday’s DAZN pay-per-view puts nearly all the pressure on Daniel Dubois against Fabio Wardley. Look past that headline attraction, because the undercard barely gives fans an incentive to reach for their wallets.

The event lands at The O2 arena in London on October 17, featuring Dubois putting his WBO belt on the line. Priced at £24.99 across the UK alongside an expected $59.99 tag in America, the supporting cast leaves buyers wondering what their cash actually buys.

Fans online shredded the fight schedule, making an entirely fair point. Dubois vs Wardley 2 brings plenty of heat after their brutal eleven-round initial meeting, but the undercard fails to offer real backup.

Bakhodir Jalolov meeting Solomon Dacres stands out as the most recognizable heavyweight clash on the lower bill. Tracking an Olympic gold medalist develop is fun, yet watching a prospect work differs completely from getting an explosive co-feature.

Jalolov is thirty-two years old, still wading through the prospect phase after spending years hopping back and forth between the Olympics and small pro shows. Solomon Dacres got wiped out in a single round by David Adeleye not that long ago, and while he ground out a win against Sirenko, he remains British domestic grade at best

Further down, Louie O’Doherty squares off with Michael Gomez Jnr, while Nelson Birchall takes on Levi Giles. Both scraps could bring plenty of excitement, though neither matchup seals the deal for a hefty price tag.

The rest of the broadcast leans on developing talent alongside domestic pairings. Young talent deserves room to grow on massive platforms, but spotlighting them doesn’t automatically create genuine value for paying customers.

Subscribers with DAZN Ultimate get the card bundled into their monthly plan, which softens the blow. Everyone else facing a standalone purchase has to judge if a single scrap justifies the full cost.

Queensberry staked the entire night on the main event producing magic. Dubois versus Wardley could easily deliver pure entertainment, yet that thrill can’t rescue a thin supporting bill. Boxing fans can crave the rematch while demanding more substance across the whole night.

Sports.title: Jose Valenzuela Pushes WBA for Floyd Schofield Fight
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela wants the WBA to put him next in line for Floyd Schofield’s lightweight title, potentially complicating the new champion’s unification plans before his first defense is arranged.

“Let’s make it happen,” Rayo wrote on X, tagging the WBA in response to a post arguing that Schofield must first face a mandatory or leading available contender after winning the vacant belt.

Schofield defeated Lucas Bahdi in Chicago on Saturday to become champion. Oscar De La Hoya has discussed unifications, but Rayo is asking the sanctioning body to consider its own ranked contenders before moving forward with those plans.

The WBA’s September rankings listed Schofield first, Bahdi second, and Rayo third. With Schofield now champion and Bahdi coming off the defeat, Rayo has a credible case for consideration. His position does not automatically establish him as the mandatory challenger.

Rayo, 27, holds a 16-3 record with 10 knockouts and is coming off a second-round knockout win over Edwin De Los Santos on June 28. Some fans criticized the finish, believing he hit De Los Santos while he was down and arguing for a no contest or disqualification. The official result remains a knockout victory.

There is also a promotional and broadcast hurdle. Rayo fights for Zuffa Boxing on Paramount+, while Schofield is promoted by Golden Boy, whose events air on DAZN. Making the fight would require the promoters to agree on terms and a broadcast arrangement.

A WBA order could push those discussions forward, but it would not decide which platform carries the event or how the revenue is divided.

The post Rayo shared also overstated the vacant-title rule. The WBA rules version amended through April 2024 requires a non-heavyweight vacant-title winner to make his initial defense within 120 days. That provision does not itself say every voluntary defense is prohibited.

Golden Boy therefore cannot treat Rayo’s request as an official order, but neither can it assume Schofield has an unrestricted choice of opponents. Rayo has publicly asked for the opportunity. The WBA’s response will determine whether that request becomes an obligation.

Sports.title: David Benavidez May Lose His Edge at Heavyweight
Sports.content:
David Benavidez might find that moving to heavyweight strips away everything that makes him effective. Stepping through 175 and cruiserweight before chasing the big men could easily backfire on a fighter who relies on physical advantages, high volume, and quick hand speed.

Before any of that happens, he still needs to deal with Michal Cieslak, while keeping Jai Opetaia and an aging Artur Beterbiev on his radar. Jumping to heavyweight forces yet another drastic body transformation before anyone even knows if his power carries through the cruiserweight elite.

“The heavyweight division is definitely a division I’ve got my eyes on. [But] we’ve got two great fights at cruiserweight before we get up there,” Benavidez told Inside The Ring. “We’ve got Jai Opetaia, then I think Beterbiev is going to come up to cruiserweight.”

The real problem lies in what gets sacrificed when packing on bulk. Benavidez built his reputation by being the bigger man in the ring, bullying smaller opponents into the ropes, and drowning them in extended combinations. Against genuine heavyweights, that physical edge vanishes completely.

Piling on muscle rarely translates to better punch resistance or sustained stamina. If the extra weight dulls his hand speed or drains his work rate, Benavidez turns into a stationary target who lacks the one-punch eraser needed to keep giant opponents from walking him down.

If he slows down by even ten percent, he stops being a swarm puncher and turns into a flat-footed target. Without blistering hand speed, large heavyweights will simply time him with straight shots from the outside or tie him up in clinches, leaning on his shoulders to drain whatever legs he has left.

David Morrell already exposed how much damage Benavidez absorbs when a fight gets tough. Routine wins over Anthony Yarde and Gilberto Ramirez did not prove he can stand in the pocket against massive punchers and survive the return fire.

Careful matchmaking could hide some flaws. A washed-up Andy Ruiz Jr. gives him an accessible name, while Oleksandr Usyk showed clear signs of slippage at 39 years old against Rico Verhoeven, needing an eleventh-round rescue after trailing on one card through ten rounds.

Those soft targets might make the jump tempting, but they do not solve the fundamental issue. Benavidez could pack on thirty pounds, only to end up slower, easier to hit, and far less dangerous than the fighter who dominated at 168.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Picks Abdullah Mason To Beat Schofield
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield would lose his newly won lightweight belt to Abdullah Mason, according to Tim Bradley, who believes his movement against Lucas Bahdi exposed weaknesses a quicker opponent could exploit.

“Even Abdullah Mason is on an entirely different level than Schofield,” Bradley said on his channel in his post-fight breakdown. “You ain’t going to keep that belt that long, bro.”

That puts Bradley against the matchup Schofield’s father has been pushing for. His confidence in his son beating Mason faces a different reading from Bradley, who sees technical flaws beneath Schofield’s speed and athleticism.

Bradley’s main criticism concerns how Schofield controls distance. He believes Schofield moves too much without maintaining a stable punching position, leaving openings as he bounces around the ring. His proposed correction is a firmer jab, feints, and smaller steps that allow him to defend while remaining ready to punch.

Bahdi’s slower feet, in Bradley’s view, prevented him from consistently taking advantage. Being able to move away from Bahdi doesn’t establish that Schofield could do the same against an opponent who closes distance faster.

But Bradley’s own breakdown also offers reasons to question how emphatically he dismisses Schofield’s chances.

He praised the switch to southpaw, which disrupted Bahdi’s right-hand attacks and helped Schofield land shorter combinations. He also credited Schofield’s stamina and use of clinches to interrupt Bahdi’s momentum.

“That was a great technical and tactical shift,” Bradley said of the stance change.

Those adjustments deserve consideration when discussing Mason. Schofield showed he could change his approach when his initial offense wasn’t enough. Bradley identified weaknesses, but he also described a fighter capable of solving some of the difficulties in front of him.

A Mason fight would test whether Schofield can control distance with less movement and fewer openings. His speed gives him options; learning when to plant his feet and when to take a small step could make those options more effective.

Bradley favors Mason strongly. Schofield’s performance gives his camp plenty to work on before trying to prove him wrong.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia’s Catchweight Defense Overlooks Who Benefits
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia’s defense of catchweights leaves out who benefits when the more popular fighter dictates the conditions. He argues that flexible limits create bouts that otherwise could not occur, entirely skipping over how that dynamic forces concessions onto opponents.

“Impossible @Showbizz. That stops matchups that couldn’t happen without it. It will actually limit boxing and boxing is a sport without any [limits],” Ryan said on X.

Meeting between divisions can bridge weight classes, sure. Yet the marquee attraction can easily use contract terms to tilt the contest before either man touches a glove.

The B-side contender gets squeezed into a corner. Walk away, and he surrenders his career-high purse, elite visibility, plus a rare spotlight. Agree, and he secures the event while compromising his physical prime on fight night.

Ryan overlooks that reality. A signed contract proves agreement occurred, not that both sides wielded equal clout during negotiations.

His 2023 clash with Gervonta Davis proved the exact dynamic. The deal called for a 136-pound limit, paired with a morning check capping rehydration at 146 pounds. Davis wanted that second barrier.

Even when contract terms apply equally on paper, they rarely extract the same toll. One athlete cruises in comfortably while the other drains himself dry just to qualify.

Garcia also sidesteps rehydration stipulations altogether. These terms extend far past the opening weigh-in, policing how much bulk a fighter recovers before entering the ring. Paired with strict weight caps, they hand the A-side major leverage over an adversary’s preparation.

Nobody can claim Davis definitely loses without those rules in place. Still, simply getting two big names into the ring cannot stand as proof that the contract was balanced. Ryan loves talking about flexibility. His case still needs to account for contenders who must surrender their physical strength just to earn their shot against the bigger star.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Sticks With Original Riyadh Fight Plan
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez plans to proceed with his October 31 bout against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh, Turki Alalshikh confirmed, standing by the Saudi boxing chief amid ongoing uncertainty around the event.

“Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens. He fears nothing,” Alalshikh wrote on X.

That commitment signals a fighter acting in full partnership with organizers. Instead of requesting a change of venue, Canelo gave private assurances that he will make the trip as scheduled. For someone working to hold the fight card together, receiving that backing from the main attraction carries serious weight.

Alalshikh made his appreciation unmistakable in his closing message.

“Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends.”

Canelo is displaying loyalty by keeping the original arrangement intact. Alalshikh has put substantial muscle behind major events featuring the Mexican superstar, and Canelo appears determined to return that backing when complications arise.

Turki Alalshikh is holding the deepest checkbook the sport has ever seen. For an aging superstar whose standard pay-per-view numbers in Las Vegas had begun to settle, maintaining direct favor with Riyadh Season is essential.

How prospective spectators respond to the situation remains less certain.

A promise from the headliner aids the promotion, yet it will not settle the concerns of traveling supporters. Individuals looking at plane tickets, hotel reservations, or seat prices will reach their own conclusions. Canelo’s willingness to compete does not guarantee their presence.

Sparse seating on fight night would still mean Alalshikh values the champion’s pledge. Still, empty sections would drain energy from the arena once Canelo and Mbilli step under the lights. Official ticketing numbers remain unconfirmed, making lower attendance an open risk rather than a settled fact.

The boundary is simple: the fighter controls his arrival, while paying fans decide if they make the trip.

At this point, Alalshikh holds the guarantee he needed most. Based on his statement, Canelo is staying the course in Riyadh.

Ghana News.title: EcoBank invests in digital education of 4 Garisson School to mark 40 years in Africa
Ghana News.content:
Ecobank is set to strengthen digital education in Ghana with the commissioning of a newly refurbished and fully equipped Digital Learning Centre at the 4 Garrison School in Kumasi.

The corporate social initiative is part of activities marking the bank’s 40th anniversary celebrations in Africa.

The initiative forms part of Ecobank Day, the Ecobank Group’s flagship corporate social responsibility programme observed annually across its 33 affiliate countries.

This year’s celebration, under the theme “Building Tomorrow’s Skills Today,” marks the culmination of the bank’s three-year Transforming Africa Through Education programme.

The new Digital Learning Centre will provide pupils of the 4 Garrison School with access to digital learning resources and practical opportunities to develop skills in emerging technologies.

These include coding, web development, animation, robotics and artificial intelligence (AI), among other areas shaping the future of work and innovation.

The facility is designed to help bridge the digital skills gap by exposing pupils to technology at an early stage of their education and equipping them with relevant knowledge for an increasingly digital world.

Through access to modern learning tools, pupils will have the opportunity to explore their interests, develop problem-solving skills and build a foundation for future careers in science, technology and innovation.

Ecobank’s investment in the centre underscores the importance of equipping young people with the skills needed to participate meaningfully in the digital economy.

“These are extra skills the students will acquire. It will help them in their academic progression and in learning the fundamentals to support SMEs,” Head of Corporate Communications, Dr. Kasser Tee, said.

The initiative also reflects the bank’s broader commitment to education, digital inclusion and skills development in Ghana.

By supporting access to technology-based learning, Ecobank seeks to contribute to efforts to expand educational opportunities and empower young people with skills relevant to national and continental development.

The commissioning of the Digital Learning Centre forms part of activities commemorating Ecobank’s four decades of operations in Africa, highlighting the institution’s continued focus on social impact alongside its banking activities.

Through its Transforming Africa Through Education programme and the annual Ecobank Day initiative, the bank continues to place education at the centre of its corporate social responsibility efforts, with particular attention to developing the capabilities of young people.

The investment at the 4 Garrison School therefore represents more than the provision of digital infrastructure; it is an opportunity to introduce pupils to emerging technologies, encourage creativity and innovation, and prepare them to contribute to Africa’s evolving digital future.

In the last three years of the programme’s implementation across Africa, EcoBank has established over sixty digital laboratories with seven of them in Ghana.

Education Director at the 4 Garrison School, Lt. Col. Niminga-Baka, is upbeat about the benefits of the initiative to the over 6,000 pupils of the school.

“In this era, IT is really important for national development. Exposing the students to emerging technologies is quite an important step to transform the country through digital innovation,” he said.

As Ecobank celebrates 40 years in Africa, the initiative reinforces the message that investing in education and digital skills is an important step towards building a more inclusive and technology-driven future for the continent.

Ghana News.title: AGI urges investment in skills and raw materials to strengthen local manufacturing
Ghana News.content:
The Association of Ghana Industries (AGI) is stepping up efforts to strengthen Ghana's garment, textiles and leather sector, following the government's decision to engage local manufacturers to produce uniforms and other apparel for the security services.

The initiative is expected to create opportunities for local businesses, but industry players say addressing skills shortages, high production costs, and limited access to raw materials will be critical to strengthening industry demand.

Chairperson of AGI's Garment, Textiles and Leather Sector, Edwina Assan, says the association is engaging training institutions and industry players to develop the skills needed to strengthen local production.

She noted that some institutions lack the technical expertise and personnel to train workers for the industry, making collaboration with experienced manufacturers necessary.

"We are looking at coming up with programmes that the industry players can help with, supporting the institutions in training," she said.

She also identified the high cost of imported raw materials and other production inputs as major constraints affecting local manufacturers.

According to her, reducing dependence on imported materials through local production will help lower manufacturing costs and make Ghanaian products more competitive.

"It's only when we have our raw materials produced locally that we can also produce at a cheaper price and be able to pay well," she added.

Meanwhile, the Chief Executive Officer of Horseman Shoes, Tonyi Senayah, says Ghana must be deliberate in building the capacity of local footwear and leather businesses before considering restrictions on imported products.

He questioned whether local companies currently have the production capacity to meet domestic demand, arguing that protecting the industry must go hand in hand with investment in skills, enterprise development, and market access.

"What we are advocating for is that we start building the capacity of players or enterprises in the footwear and leather space. And we have to be intentional," he said.

Mr. Senayah noted that successful industrial economies developed their manufacturing sectors through deliberate policies and sustained support for local businesses.

He believes the leather industry presents significant opportunities for job creation, particularly among young people, but says local enterprises need the right support to expand and compete.

"By being intentional, we have to start building the capacity of these businesses, developing skills and also giving them access to market," he added.

The industry says stronger collaboration, improved technical training, and increased local raw material production will be essential to expanding Ghana's manufacturing capacity.

It believes these measures will help local businesses take advantage of government procurement opportunities, create employment, and strengthen the country's garment, textiles and leather value chain.

Ghana News.title: GPL 2026/27: ‘We have to rectify our mistakes’ – Boadu reacts to Aduana FC defeat
Ghana News.content:
Aduana FC head coach Samuel Boadu has urged his team to quickly put their latest defeat behind them and focus on correcting their errors ahead of upcoming Ghana Premier League fixtures.

Aduana FC brought their three-match winning streak to an end following a 1-0 defeat over the Young Apostles at the Wenchi Sports Stadium.

A first-half penalty converted by Samuel Prempeh shortly before the break proved decisive, securing all three points for the home side.

“I don’t want to talk about officiating. It is football," Boadu said.

"We have lost, and we have to rectify our mistakes going into the remaining games. I wasn’t expecting a defeat, but one mistake we made resulted in their goal."

“It was really bad, but we will talk to ourselves and improve in subsequent games. I will congratulate my players despite the defeat. It was one unpardonable mistake that led to the loss.”

Despite the setback, Boadu declined to set explicit targets for the remainder of the campaign.

“It is still early days to talk about our target. We will go home, work hard, and aim to accumulate more points in our subsequent matches,” he explained.

The result leaves Aduana FC sixth on the Ghana Premier League standings with 10 points after six matches.

Ghana News.title: No disability access, no building permit – KMA declares
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive of the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA), Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi, has admitted that most public infrastructure in the metropolis, including his own office, is not disability-friendly.

According to him, the challenge stems from the fact that most public buildings in the city were constructed before the passage of Ghana's Disability Act and are housed in old institutional structures not designed with accessibility in mind.

"Even my office and the entire KMA complex are not PWD-friendly, but these are old buildings and there is nothing we can do about them now. However, we will ensure that accessibility for PWDs is prioritized in any future infrastructure development or redevelopment on the KMA premises," he said.

Speaking to Adom News, Mr. Boadi stated that since he assumed office, he has ensured strict enforcement of the accessibility requirements stipulated in the Persons with Disability Act, 2006 (Act 715), for all new developments within the metropolis.

"For every new building permit proposal that comes before us, we ensure that if it is going to serve the public, you must create ramps and channels that will ensure accessibility for our brothers and sisters with disabilities before we give approval," he said.

He disclosed that the Assembly has captured 18 projects in its 2027 development plan aimed at making public spaces more inclusive.

The projects include the massive renovation of parks and community centres across the metropolis.

The renovation, he explained, will involve the demolition and reconstruction of stages to incorporate appropriate ramps and accessible facilities to enable talented PWDs to access the platforms, showcase their talents and earn a living.

"It is something the Assembly has not taken its eyes off. For example, the Prempeh Assembly Hall is not disability-friendly, so its renovation to make it accessible has been captured in our budget," the Mayor assured.

Mr. Boadi reaffirmed KMA's commitment to promoting disability inclusion and ensuring that persons with disabilities participate fully in the social and economic life of the metropolis.

Ghana News.title: Asantehene to lead environmental restoration effort at Jimi Land Reclamation Site
Ghana News.content:
Galamsey

The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, will undertake a royal visit to the Jimi Land Reclamation and River Watercourse Rehabilitation Project near Obuasi on Wednesday, October 14, 2026.

During the visit, he will plant trees and inspect Lot 1, marking a major milestone in restoring lands severely degraded by unregulated small-scale mining.

The environmental initiative responds to widespread damage caused by unregulated small-scale gold mining, known as galamsey, which has stripped forest vegetation, contaminated soils, and left hazardous open, water-filled pits across the Obuasi and Adansi areas.

Toxic runoff and heavy sediment buildup along the Jimi River threaten the Jimi Dam, a critical source of drinking water for communities across the Adanse Traditional Area.

The reclamation effort stems from Otumfuo’s advocacy against illegal mining during the Mining in Motion forum, which led to the creation of the Ashanti Green Initiative.

Operating as the initiative's flagship pilot project, the Jimi reclamation brings together key institutional partners, including the Manhyia Palace, providing overall strategic vision and royal patronage; Ashanti Green Initiative, serving as project lead on behalf of the Asantehene and drives community engagement; and AngloGold Ashanti, delivering technical and operational support.

Others are the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, overseeing policy, permitting, and security enforcement through NAIMOS and the Blue Water Guard; and the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), providing regulatory guidance for ecological restoration along the river and buffer zones.

Covering 153 hectares across three designated lots in the Obuasi East Municipality as well as the Adansi Akrofuom and Adansi Asokwa Districts, the pilot targets heavily impacted sites near Gyimisokakraba, Ayease, and Akwesi Ankromakrom.

Restoration works are structured around a six-step process: Backfilling open mining pits and deep gullies; Re-grading spoil heaps and terracing steep slopes; Containing, capping, or removing heavy-metal soil contamination; Installing drainage and erosion control structures to safeguard the river corridor; Restoring and enriching topsoil health; and replanting the land with kenaf, a commercial fibre crop.

Due to residual heavy-metal contamination risks in the soil, kenaf was selected over food crops. The fast-growing fibre crop will be harvested for manufacturing sacks, rope, and eco-composites, establishing a secure income stream for local farmers.

Long-term project plans include continuous water testing to protect the Jimi Dam, as well as ongoing tracking of soil, vegetation, biodiversity, and community health outcomes.

Organizers intend for the Jimi pilot to serve as a national model to rehabilitate other mining-damaged land and water systems across Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Poor Ghanaians are being jailed because they cannot afford justice – Crime Check Foundation
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of the Crime Check Foundation, Ibrahim Oppong Kwarteng, has criticised Ghana’s justice system, arguing that poverty is contributing to the imprisonment of people who cannot afford fines or adequate legal representation.

“What we see at times is not justice. What we see is poverty on trial,” he said, recounting cases encountered by his organisation during more than a decade of work in Ghana’s prisons.

Mr Kwarteng made the remarks at an event following a tour of prison establishments across the country, where he highlighted cases he believes expose inequalities in access to justice.

“For over 10 years, Crime Check Foundation has worked in Ghana’s 49 prison establishments. And what we see at times is not justice. What we see is poverty on trial,” he said.

Mr Kwarteng cited the case of a young mother who, he said, was sentenced to two years in prison after being unable to pay a GH¢300 fine arising from a fight.

He also recounted the case of a 19-year-old who was jailed for stealing a bunch of plantain to feed his seven siblings.

Another case involved a commercial transport vehicle assistant, commonly known as a trotro mate, who Mr Kwarteng said was imprisoned because he could not afford a lawyer to defend him.

“Their crime at times is not stealing. Their crime perhaps is being poor,” he said.

The cases, he argued, raise questions about whether people’s financial circumstances are determining how they experience the criminal justice system.

Mr Kwarteng also questioned how the justice system could adequately serve poor communities when many people struggle to afford transportation to court or secure legal representation.

“Distinguished guests, how can justice be at their doorstep when they cannot afford the transport to the court? And how can justice be at their doorstep when legal aid has less than 40 lawyers across the country?” he asked.

He further raised concerns about people spending extended periods on remand without legal representation.

“I stand to be corrected. How can justice be at their doorstep when a petty offender spends three years on remand for a case that would have attracted six months if he had a lawyer?” he said.

His comments come amid calls for increased resources for the Legal Aid Commission, which provides legal advice and representation to people who cannot afford private legal services.

The Commission’s Board Chairman, Supreme Court Justice Samuel Kwame Asiedu Adibu, recently disclosed that it operates 45 offices across Ghana’s 261 districts, with a total staff strength of 190. He said the Commission needed about 180 additional staff to improve its reach.

Calls for broader reform

The Crime Check Foundation has worked in Ghana’s prisons for more than a decade, supporting inmates, helping secure releases through the payment of fines and advocating for prison reform.

The organisation has also raised concerns about the difficulties former prisoners face after their release, including social rejection and barriers to reintegration.

Mr Kwarteng’s remarks add to wider concerns about whether poverty, inadequate legal representation and delays in court proceedings are undermining fair access to justice.

Addressing those challenges would require stronger legal aid services and closer attention to the circumstances of people held in custody, particularly those unable to afford lawyers or meet court-imposed financial obligations.

His account puts the focus on a broader question for Ghana’s justice system: whether a person’s ability to pay should determine how quickly they regain their freedom or how effectively they can defend themselves in court.

Ghana News.title: No conflict in appointing Emelia Agbenyo as Deputy EC Chair – NDC
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy National Director of Elections and IT of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Rashid Tanko-Computer, has dismissed concerns about a potential conflict of interest in the appointment of former party spokesperson Emelia Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC).

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Monday, October 12, he said the appointment should not be considered problematic, citing what he described as similar appointments made under the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) government.

He insisted Madam Agbenyo is qualified to fill that position.

“There’s no conflict of interest here. I mean, let’s be frank with ourselves,” he said.

Mr Tanko-Computer said the NDC had raised concerns about the appointment of individuals with perceived links to the NPP to positions at the EC under former President Nana Akufo-Addo.

He cited the appointment of Dr Bossman Asare as a Deputy EC Chairperson, arguing that the NDC had objected to the appointment because of his links to the NPP.

According to him, the party had taken its concerns to the Council of State, presenting evidence of what it considered to be the appointees’ political affiliations.

However, he said the then Council of State maintained that the individuals were qualified for their positions and that their political affiliations were immaterial.

Mr Tanko-Computer said the NDC’s concerns at the time were not heeded, adding that the party’s position on the current appointment should be considered in that context.

His response follows cocerns over Ms Agbenyo’s appointment as a Deputy Chairperson of the EC followig her previous role as a governance sector spokesperson for the NDC during the party’s 2024 manifesto process and whether that political association could affect perceptions of the EC’s independence.

Ghana News.title: 87-year-old man jailed 20 years for defiling 9-year-old girl at Ofankor
Ghana News.content:
An 87-year-old man, Yaw Gahornu, has been sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with hard labour for defiling a nine-year-old girl at Ofankor, a suburb of Accra.

The sentence was secured by the Tesano Divisional Police Command following investigations into the case, according to a statement issued by the Accra Regional Police Command on October 12, 2026.

The Police said preliminary investigations indicated that on August 29, 2026, the girl’s mother returned from work and noticed bloodstains on her daughter’s clothing.

When questioned, the child disclosed that Mr Gahornu had allegedly subjected her to repeated sexual abuse between July and August 2026.

Further investigations indicated that the accused allegedly lured the girl to his sleeping quarters and threatened to kill her if she reported the abuse to her mother.

The Police said the alleged abuse was witnessed by the accused’s granddaughter on August 31, 2026. She subsequently informed family members, including the girl’s mother, leading to a report to the Police.

Mr Gahornu was charged and arraigned before the Gender-Based Violence Court at the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) Headquarters, where he was found guilty and sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with hard labour for defilement.

The Accra Regional Police Command welcomed the outcome of the case and reaffirmed its commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons.

It urged the public to promptly report suspected cases of child abuse to the Police for investigation and appropriate action.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Cuba forges ahead with renewable energy plans amid US oil blockade
World.content:
Cuban energy minister denies link to fuel shipments intercepted by US, says oil imports by private firms insufficient.

The Cuban government is pushing ahead with its plans to transition to renewable energy, amid a de facto oil blockade from the United States that has strangled the island’s economy.

In an interview with the Reuters news agency on Monday, Cuban Minister of Energy and Mines Vicente de la O Levy explained that the blockade has forced Cuba to explore domestic alternatives to foreign fuel imports.

“We are seeking our own alternative solutions, using our own resources, our sun, wind, tides, fuel, Cuban crude oil and the gas produced in our wells,” de la O Levy said.

He said 144 solar farms with a combined capacity of about 1,418 megawatts have been installed on the island in recent years.

China has been the largest supplier of solar panels to the island, and shipments have increased since the blockade began in early January.

At the time, US President Donald Trump halted all oil shipments from Venezuela, a close ally of the Cuban government.

Later that month, Trump also announced he would impose heavy tariffs on any country that exported oil to Cuba, justifying the threat by calling the island’s government a “national security” threat.

Since then, only a single oil tanker from Russia has reached Havana. The US has increased its shipments of oil to Cuba’s private sector, but it has largely barred fuel exports for nationalised industries on the communist-led island.

The government-run electrical grid, widely considered to be antiquated, relies heavily on fossil fuels. Only 40 percent of Cuba’s electricity comes from ‌‌‌‌domestic ‌‌‌‌oil production, according to the International Energy Agency.



As of 2023, only nine percent of the country’s energy consumption was covered by renewable sources.

De la O Levy admitted in his interview with Reuters that the country was facing difficulties. The blockade has caused shortages of medicine, water and fuel, pushing Cuba to the brink of a humanitarian crisis.

“We are surviving and moving forward, little by little, even if not at the pace we would like,” he said.

“We face long hours of blackouts and lack fuel for cooking and transportation. We lack fuel, but we are gradually making headway through our own solutions and our people.”

Cuba’s production of domestic crude oil remains stable, he added, but is almost entirely allocated to power plants.

The United Nations and human rights watchdogs have criticised the oil blockade as a violation of international law.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla also condemned the oil blockade in his speech at the UN General Assembly last month.

“It is an unusual and unprecedented action,” Rodriguez said of the blockade.

“A superpower unilaterally deprives all states of their right to export the commodities that they wish to the country that they wish.”

The US has maintained an economic embargo on Cuba for more than 60 years, since the Cold War era.

But since taking office for a second term as president, Trump has sought to squeeze Cuba’s economy further, as part of a “maximum pressure” campaign. His administration has indicated that it wants to topple Cuba’s government.

On October 7, US authorities announced they had seized 90 biodiesel fuel shipments valued at over $2.8m destined for Cuba.

“These shipments were part of an attempt to unlawfully export fuel to Cuba in violation of federal export laws,” US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said in a statement.

But in his interview with Reuters, de la O Levy denied the Cuban government had any link to the shipments.

“No Cuban state-owned company has managed to secure a fuel contract, whether for small or large quantities,” he said.

He added that any US oil shipments to private firms fall far short of the country’s requirements.

“I would venture to say that the amount entering the country doesn’t even cover 3 percent of its fuel needs,” de la O Levy said.

World.title: UK blames Iran for airbase plot, sanctions two Iranian nationals
World.content:
Britain’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said that a suspected plot targeting Royal Air Force (RAF) base Fairford was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), raising the diplomatic stakes over the largely unexplained incident for which Tehran has denied any responsibility.

“We will not tolerate these threats on our soil,” Burnham told parliament on Monday, adding that the government, “will crack down on Iran’s use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams”.

“We will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to do us harm”, he said.

The incident near the airbase in southern England occurred in the early hours of September 27 when five British men in their 20s were arrested on suspected “terrorism” and explosives offences.

Police said they found a supply of petrol in three vans linked to the suspects, but no explosives.

They were later released without charge on ‌‌‌‌police ⁠⁠⁠⁠bail “under stringent conditions”. Last week, Counter Terrorism Policing arrested a 22-year-old British national on suspicion of a “terror” offence linked to the security incident. Earlier this month, a 25-year-old British-Iranian man was arrested in London.

In a statement on X, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Britain was sanctioning two Iranians for their “role in facilitating or engaging in hostile activity on behalf of the Iranian regime”, without specifying their identity.

“We have repeatedly made clear to Iran, Britain will not tolerate threats on our soil”, he said.



The move came as 29 countries, including Britain, the US, most European states, Canada, Australia and New Zealand issued a joint statement on Monday blaming Iran for the attempted infiltration.

“Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable”, it said.

‘Categorical rejection’

On Monday, Ali Mousavi, Iran’s ambassador to the UK, met Stephen Doughty, the UK’s minister for the Middle East, and “categorically rejected” allegations of any Iranian role while urging “the British side to refrain from any unsubstantiated statements”.

Mousavi told British authorities that Tehran is willing to cooperate with the investigation into the incident, Iran’s ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠state news agency IRNA reported.

Iran’s embassy in London issued a statement last month saying Iran “categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations” attempting to link the country to the arrests, adding that it will “fuel Iranophobia propaganda”.

The US moved its B-52 and B-1 bombers from the base earlier this month.

RAF Fairford has served as a stopping point for US bombers participating in the war against Iran, which began more than seven months ago, on February 28.

Located roughly 160km (100 miles) west of London, RAF Fairford is the preferred European base for US bombers. Their withdrawal was made over concerns about a suspected Iranian plot to carry out a complex drone attack on the facility, according to US officials.
