World.title: Egypt’s press union chief rejects pressure over detained journalists
World.content:
The head of Egypt’s Journalists Syndicate has insisted the organisation will continue to fight for press freedom after it came under fire for defending six journalists who were detained last month and charged with joining a “terrorist” group.

“What happens to one colleague affects us all, and may happen to others tomorrow,” Khaled Elbalshy said in a statement on Sunday. “An infringement of one journalist’s freedom is an infringement of everyone’s freedom and a weakening of the safeguards protecting that freedom.”

His comments came after the syndicate filed a complaint with Egypt’s public prosecutor over allegations that the detained journalists, who work for the investigative website Matsadaash, had been tortured. Egyptian authorities denied the accusations, while pro-government commentators criticised the organisation for defending the journalists.

Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Mahmoud and Abdallah Qadry were arrested on September 28 and 29 and have since appeared before the Supreme State Security Prosecution, which prosecutes national security cases. They have been ordered to be held in pretrial detention for 15 days pending investigations.

Egyptian prosecutors have accused the six journalists of working for a media organisation tied to the Muslim Brotherhood, a group Egyptian authorities have cracked down on for years following a 2013 coup against democratically elected Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, who was a member. Egypt has officially designated the Muslim Brotherhood as a “terrorist” group, an allegation the organisation has strongly denied, while human rights groups have accused Egyptian authorities of repressing freedoms.



Matsadaash co-founder Abdelrahman Mansour has also rejected any links between the media platform and the Muslim Brotherhood.

In his statement, Elbalshy said: “The fundamental principle governing all such matters, particularly when dealing with accused persons in general and vulnerable people in particular, remains that an accused person is innocent until proven guilty.”

Allegations of torture

The Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), whose lawyers are representing the six journalists, said they were initially held for five days without any contact with their families or lawyers. After complaints, the journalists appeared before prosecutors and were questioned in the presence of their lawyers and a representative from the Journalists Syndicate.

The EIPR said the journalists were being held under Egypt’s 2015 Counterterrorism Law that allows for suspects to be held in custody before appearing before prosecutors “when there is a risk of a terrorist crime and a necessity to confront that risk”. The rights group, however, noted that the prosecution only alleges that the journalists published rumours or “false” reports.

“The public prosecution should have identified the imminent terrorist threat that required denying them their right to appear before a judicial authority within 24 hours of their arrest,” the EIPR said on October 7.

The EIPR has also said that most of the six journalists said they were tortured following their arrests, including being beaten and subjected to electric shocks. It added that several of the detained had been forced to record fabricated confessions.

Egypt’s Interior Ministry has rejected the allegations.

Matsadaash was founded in 2018 as a fact-checking platform, but has since expanded into investigative journalism. Its website is blocked in Egypt, but it has more than 1.3 million followers on Facebook.

The outlet has previously faced pressure from Egyptian authorities, including in 2023, when one of its journalists, Karim Asaad, was arrested after Matsadaash published an investigation into a suspected smuggling scandal involving a plane that had flown from Cairo to Zambia. He was later released.

World.title: UK PM Andy Burnham met Man City chairman during time as Manchester mayor
World.content:
Statement comes after criticism of Burnham’s initial response ⁠to City being found guilty of serious financial breaches.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham met Manchester City Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak at an investment summit several years ago when he was mayor of the city, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority has said.

The announcement on Monday comes after Burnham said he would be “really concerned” if City’s owners sold the football club following the decision to find the 10-time English champions guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules.

Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, faced criticism for appearing to express support for City’s hierarchy.

Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was “above the rules”.

But there were demands for clarification regarding Burnham’s relationship with City’s owners, who have driven significant investment in Manchester through partnerships with local authorities.

City are owned by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), controlled by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the United Arab Emirates’ royal family.

A Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) spokesman said: “In October 2021, Andy Burnham, in his role as mayor of Greater Manchester, had a formal meeting with Khaldoon Al Mubarak at the UK Government’s Global Investment Summit arranged by the Department for International Trade.

“In his capacity as mayor, he was a guest of Manchester City FC at home matches on a small number of occasions, including attending Vincent Kompany’s testimonial match in September 2019, where he met the chairman informally in the stands. These have been declared in the usual way.”



The statement added that during Burnham’s time as mayor “representatives of Greater Manchester sporting clubs would routinely join business delegations as part of mayoral international visits.

“This included representatives from Manchester United travelling to Austin and Dublin, Lancashire Cricket Club joining a delegation to India, and Manchester City FC staff supporting visits to China and Japan.”

But Louie French, the opposition Conservatives spokesman for sport, said the statement contained “precious little information about these meetings, what was discussed and what may have been agreed”.

It was far “from the full transparency that football fans deserve. Burnham cannot hide behind the GMCA – he must take responsibility for this himself”, French added.

City have been found guilty of breaking more than 100 Premier League financial regulations by arranging “sham” contracts to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs in a nine-season run between 2009 and 2018.

The Premier League leaders have appealed against the verdict, saying it contains “clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”.

City could be hit with a huge points deduction or even face expulsion from the Premier League if they lose the appeal.

World.title: Stolen Renoir paintings found behind wall in France following arrests
World.content:
Share Stolen Renoir paintings found behind wall in France following arrests on social media

Two paintings by the impressionist master Renoir which were stolen from a French museum last month have been found damaged behind a false wall in a private home after police made several arrests ahead of what prosecutors say was an imminent second heist.

Marseille prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said six suspects were arrested on Wednesday after authorities discovered they were planning to target the Fondation Maeght in Saint-Paul-de-Vence, home to one of Europe’s largest collections of modern art.

Bessone said the arrests were prompted by the “very strong suspicion that another heist was imminent”.

“We were very clearly looking at the repetition of a criminal scheme”, said Eric Antonetti, the head of the Alpes-Maritimes judicial police.

On September 8, thieves used an electric saw to cut through a fence to enter the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera, according to investigators.

An alarm sounded and police officers arrived four minutes later, a swift response that “apparently caused the perpetrators to panic,” Bessone said.

The stolen works, “Madame Colonna Romano” and “Young Woman at the Well” by impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir, were valued at about 4.2m euros ($4.7m), Bessone said.

The thieves also attempted to steal two other Renoir paintings, “Madame Pichon” and “Coco Reading”, which depicts Renoir’s young ‌son ‌Claude. They abandoned them in the museum gardens while fleeing police.

“As they fled, they were unable to take all four paintings and abandoned two of them, which were later found in a protective sleeve,” he said.

Damaged and torn

The paintings were found hidden behind a false wall in a house on Friday. Both works were damaged and will need ⁠restoration. One of the paintings, “Madame Colonna Romano”, had been torn.



“These two paintings are not simply works of art. They are part of our city’s history,” Bryan Masson, the mayor of Cagnes-sur-Mer, near Nice, said on Friday. “Knowing they have been recovered is an immense relief.”

The recovery came almost exactly one month ⁠after the theft, following an investigation that used ⁠DNA evidence, mobile phone geolocation data and surveillance video.

The two key suspects include a 29-year-old, who was charged after investigators recovered DNA from a bag left behind during the getaway.

They ⁠were charged with organised theft and other offences. A third man, accused of hiding the paintings, was charged with organised handling of stolen goods.

A fourth suspect, who investigators say was approached about buying the artworks, was charged ‌with handling stolen goods and taking part in a criminal conspiracy.

Bessone said the suspects had denied planning a second museum raid, but he added that he did “not believe the principal suspect visited that ‌museum simply out of a love of art”.

World.title: Ethiopian forces enter strategic Tigray town of Adwa, witnesses say
World.content:
Ethiopian government forces have entered the town of Adwa without a fight, days after capturing Adigrat from rebel fighters as flights resumed to Mekelle in the country’s northern Tigray region.

Residents of the northwestern town of Adwa, roughly 40km (24 miles) from Eritrea’s border, said federal forces and an allied militia entered the town on Sunday, a day after the withdrawal of fighters from the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).

TPLF Vice President Amanuel Assefa said he “did not wish to comment”.

“All the shops in the town are closed. Last night, many government institutions, including Adwa Hospital, were looted,” Aferwerki, a local resident who gave only one name, told AFP.

Conflict monitor ACLED said that Ethiopian drone strikes targeted a hotel in Adwa on October 4, wounding between “five and nine people, including security personnel”, who were taken to hospital. Some ACLED sources indicated that TPLF Chairman Debretsion Gebremichael and other senior officials were at the hotel, but stressed the information had not been verified.

Another resident who requested anonymity confirmed the TPLF forces withdrew from Adwa but said that although government forces were deployed in the town, they had not reached the centre.

“The roads are deserted. People are very afraid of theft,” he said.

Last week, Ethiopian forces captured Tigray’s regional capital Mekelle, days after the TPLF confirmed that it had withdrawn from the city and moved its regional administration “temporarily” to another location.



Ethiopian Airlines resumed flights from the capital, Addis Abba, to Mekelle on Sunday for the first time since September 23, when a seven-group armed alliance, including the TPLF, started fighting Ethiopian forces and captured the airport.

“I would like to assure you on this occasion that we will bring visible change, a change beyond mere hope,” Getachew Reda, a former Tigray leader who now advises Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed told supporters greeting Reda and Ethiopia’s intelligence chief Redwan Hussein at Mekelle airport.

Ethiopia has accused Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt of backing the rebel alliance.

Khartoum and Cairo have denied involvement. Eritrea, which fought alongside Ethiopia’s federal army in the 2020-2022 war, severed diplomatic ties with Ethiopia over the accusations last week.

World.title: Zohran Mamdani orders use-of-force review for New York City police
World.content:
A city spokesperson says the calls for reform are not connected to the police response to an ICE shooting last week.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani has ordered a review of the New York City Police Department’s use of force for the first time in a decade amid renewed pressure from his progressive base for law enforcement reform.

On Monday, the city said it would introduce a “package of reforms” in addition to the review, to “strengthen accountability when police officers are accused of serious misconduct”.

The New York Police Department (NYPD) is the largest police force in the United States.

The reforms follow the retirement of a police officer involved in the shooting death of 19-year-old Win Rozario during a reported mental health crisis in 2024.

“That officer retired before a disciplinary trial could take place,” the mayor’s office said in a statement.

Among other measures Mamdani announced is $2.6m in additional funding for the Office of the Inspector General, which investigates NYPD policies and misconduct.

Monday’s statement also calls for a new notification system to ensure disciplinary hearings are completed before an officer retires, and it includes a renewed push for the department to comply with state-level reporting requirements about police-involved deaths.

Progressive pressure

The announcement comes amid pressure from Mamdani’s fellow progressives to enforce accountability at the city’s police department.

Much of the focus has fallen on a division within the NYPD called the Strategic Response Group, a rapid-response unit that addresses protests, major events and “civil disorder”.

Earlier this month, 17 state-level politicians and political nominees, including congressional candidates Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier, called for the group to be disbanded. Both Valdez and Chevalier were endorsed by Mamdani.



In a statement, the politicians denounced the Strategic Response Group’s deployment during protests against a recent US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operation.

On October 8, an ICE officer shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal while he was inside an SUV last week with his five-year-old son. The shooting, which took place in New York’s Marble Hill neighbourhood, sparked days of demonstrations against ICE’s tactics, as well as a police response.

Chevalier wrote in a post on social media that she was “shoved to the ground by an officer” during the protests. She also claimed to have observed other instances of excessive violence.

“When I was in Marble Hill last night I saw NYPD officers rapidly escalating violence,” Chevalier said.

“I witnessed unmarked law enforcement cars hitting protesters as NYPD officers pushed people out of its path.”

Mamdani condemned the shooting and called for Belgal’s release from federal custody.

Calls for police chief’s removal

Critics have frequently pointed to such incidents as examples of why greater police oversight is necessary.

Reported use of force within the NYPD has increased over the last decade, including physical force, the deployment of firearms, and the use of electrical weapons like tasers.

There were 12,348 reported use-of-force incidents in 2025, compared with 4,087 in 2016, when the department first started collecting such statistics.

Crime in New York City, however, has been on the downturn. Earlier this month, the city reported the “fewest shooting incidents, shooting victims, and murders” in the first nine months of the year and in the third quarter of the year, compared with any time in recorded history.

Major crime, which includes murder, rape, felony assault and grand larceny, declined 9.4 percent in the third quarter and 6.6 percent compared with the same period last year.

Still, Chevalier and other progressive politicians remained critical of the excess force authorised under the city’s police leadership. They have called on Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, who was originally appointed by Mamdani’s predecessor, Eric Adams, to step down.

The commissioner is appointed by the mayor. She can be removed either by the mayor or the governor of New York State.

According to recent reporting from The Atlantic magazine, New York State Governor Kathy Hochul made retaining Tisch as police commissioner a condition of her endorsement for Mamdani in the 2024 mayoral election.

In a statement to the magazine, Mamdani questioned that framing, saying Hochul’s support for keeping Tisch was “more of a recommendation” than a demand.



A New York City Hall spokesperson told Al Jazeera that the use-of-force review was already in the works prior to the October 8 ICE shooting and the protests that followed.

World.title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
World.content:
Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities".

There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight.

On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

World.title: Documents falsified to evade tax on Abramovich's wealth, BBC finds
World.content:
The world's biggest accountancy firm helped in falsifying documents to hide Roman Abramovich's wealth and evade tax, BBC Panorama has found.

Accounts signed off by Deloitte in Cyprus meant assets such as superyachts, mansions and private jets worth $672m (Â£508m) vanished from Abramovich's company accounts.

Deloitte also appears to have advised on a scheme to evade a huge tax bill on the oligarch's wealth through the falsification of documents.

Barrister Andrew Mitchell KC, an expert in financial services law, said Panorama's evidence showed the scheme was "straightforward" tax evasion and "it couldn't be more blatant".

Roman Abramovich's lawyers said he denies that he evaded tax or concealed his fortune. They said Panorama provided no evidence he knew about, authorised or directed the falsification of any document and said it was legitimate to rely on advice from professionals.

Deloitte Cyprus said it "acts in compliance with applicable laws".

The findings are being revealed following a joint investigation between BBC Panorama and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism.

For nearly two decades, Roman Abramovich was the most famous Russian oligarch in the UK, welcomed in London where he bought Chelsea Football Club in 2003 and bankrolled the club's most successful period. But after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he was sanctioned by the UK government as an associate of President Vladimir Putin and forced to sell the club.

Abramovich has been reported to be living in Turkey, a safe haven for him because it did not apply sanctions. In the Channel Island of Jersey, Â£5.4bn of his assets remain frozen and a criminal investigation has been going on for four years.

The oligarch's lawyers told the BBC he denies the allegations in the Jersey investigation and says it was "undertaken for political purposes".

Our investigation has uncovered new evidence about the way Abramovich's business empire has been run. It also raises serious questions about the integrity of some of his professional advisers.

World.title: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
World.content:
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.

On Sunday evening, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said in a video statement that its forces had launched missiles and drones at Riyadh and Dammam's airports, as well as two oil and gas facilities in Eastern Province, in response to 124 Saudi air strikes in Yemen over the previous 24 hours.

Sarea also reiterated a warning to airlines and passengers against using Saudi airports and airspace, except for journeys to and from the Islamic holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

The Houthis' forces, he vowed, would "continue their escalating operations deep inside Saudi, imposing the equation of 'a blockade for a blockade' and 'an escalation for an escalation' and targeting Saudi enemy reinforcements until the aggression ceases and the siege on our dear people is lifted".

Saturday's attack on Riyadh airport drew widespread international condemnation.

UN Secretary General AntÃ³nio Guterres said he was "deeply shocked" and warned that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure were a violation of international law.

President Donald Trump said he would "make a decision" about the US joining Saudi Arabia's strikes on the Houthis. The US military is reportedly already providing intelligence and targeting support to the Saudi-led coalition.

Iran, which has repeatedly denied allegations that it provides weapons and training to the Houthis, said it was "deeply concerned" by the escalation and called for "dialogue and engagement" to resolve the situation.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The Yemeni government claimed it was behind that strike, saying it was trying to prevent an unauthorised Iranian plane from landing.

Last month, the Houthis launched a surprise offensive along Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and ousted pro-government forces from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea.

They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

However, the seizure of the strait contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports after the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

Last week, the Yemeni government announced the start of a new offensive aimed at retaking all territory held by the Houthis.

Pro-government forces said they were quickly able to retake areas around Bab al-Mandab with the help of intense Saudi air strikes, but the Houthis denied losing any territory.

World.title: South Africa's deputy police chief resigns after being charged with sexual offences
World.content:
South Africa's deputy police chief has resigned three weeks after he was charged with sexual offences.

A lawyer representing Lt Gen Shadrack Sibiya submitted his resignation letter at his disciplinary hearing on Monday, a police spokesperson said.

Sibiya, 59, is also accused of having links to organised crime bosses - allegations which led to him being suspended last year.

He denies those allegations, as well as charges that he sexually groomed a 16-year-old girl and raped an 18-year-old woman. He also faces a charge of human trafficking.

Sibiya says he did have sex with the 18-year-old but that it was consensual.

He has been in custody since he was arrested three weeks ago.

Police spokesperson Athlenda Mathe said in a post on X that his departure from the police force was regarded as a dishonourable discharge, external because he was still facing a disciplinary case when he resigned.

The accusations that Sibiya was linked to crime bosses emerged at a major public inquiry over allegations of police corruption and collusion with criminals, known as the Madlanga Commission.

Sibiya was accused of interfering with investigations into political killings in KwaZulu-Natal province.

He was also accused of receiving a gift of cash, as well as 20 impalas, from an alleged criminal kingpin in exchange for a police contract.

He denied the allegation.

The Madlanga Commission has transfixed South Africa over the past year and unearthed widespread allegations of links between police officers and crime bosses.

It was set up by President Cyril Ramaphosa after the KwaZulu-Natal police chief held a press briefing where he accused the then Police Minister Senzo Mchunu of working with criminal gangs.

Mchunu denies the allegations against him but has been suspended.

World.title: Immigration agents search Congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
World.content:
"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," Omar said in a statement. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced."

Her communications director Jacklyn Rogers called the raid "an outrageous abuse of power" by the Trump administration. "The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong."

The nature of the criminal investigation remains unclear.

A BBC crew saw several agents at the home, some carrying boxes to a van. News of the search was first reported by Fox News, which has said the investigation is about immigration paperwork filed by her late father when Omar was a child.

The timing of Monday's raid - 22 days before the November midterm elections which will decide the balance of power in Congress for the next two years - has raised concerns from Democrats who have rallied behind Omar.

The justice department has a longstanding policy of refraining from most enforcement action that is "likely to raise an issue or the perception" it was being brought for the purpose of affecting any election or disadvantage a candidate.

The US House Democratic Party leadership said in a statement that Omar had long been targeted with "vile personal attacks and baseless accusations" by Trump.

"Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family," it said.

Omar's immigration records have been scrutinised in the past by Republicans. Earlier this year, fellow Congresswoman Nancy Mace of South Carolina unsuccessfully filed a subpoena of her records.

Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a conservative podcaster "something is going to happen", making allegations of marital fraud against Omar.

Separately, the White House border tsar Tom Homan told Fox News that Omar was being investigated for unspecified immigration violations.

Omar denied these allegations last month. "I will say it again so it's as clear as possible: I'm not at all worried about these investigations, because they are complete shams," she said in a campaign fundraising email, an archive of which has been seen by the BBC.

World.title: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
World.content:
Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.

Hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight, according to one supermarket chain affected.

The chief executive of CoopÃ©rative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack.

More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while 180 stores from IntermarchÃ© and its Netto brand were affected, with a spokesman saying that another 100 shops were urgently disconnected from the internet to prevent the same thing happening to them.

Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.

The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.

Normally, supermarket freezers go through a short period of defrosting overnight, in which temperatures rise slightly. But the hackers ordered the units to heat up and stay hot, although Danfoss did not confirm any reports about just how warm the fridges and freezers could become in that process.

Danfoss said the affected cold units were older models whose security software could not be updated to ward off a risk they had identified.

The firm added in s statement that it had "long advised" businesses to keep supported systems up to date.

"Reliable refrigeration is critical to our customers' operations, and we remain committed to supporting our customers and helping them maintain secure and reliable systems they are used to."

The full scale of the attack is unclear, but figures supplied by individual chains suggest about 400 stores were affected out of 15,000 or so overall in France.

Carrefour said fridges in 80 of its 6,000 stores were hacked, while Monoprix said 5% of its 400-plus stores had been hit, with food removed from sale if its condition could not be guaranteed.

In a statement to the BBC, Mousquetaires Group - which owns IntermarchÃ© and Netto - said some fresh and frozen food display units remained out of service on Monday afternoon.

The stores had "taken all necessary precautions to remove the products from these units", it said, adding that staff were working to restock the shelves "as soon as possible".

IntermarchÃ© said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported.

As a result of the attack, managers arriving at branches of several supermarket chains on Monday morning were hit by a wave of hot air from the freezers. In some places there were even small fires.

French broadcaster BFMTV published an image showing a freezer in an ice cream aisle displaying a temperature of 26.5C.

Two supermarkets in the Alsace region reported losses of â¬270,000 (Â£228,000) between them, the broadcaster added, meaning the nationwide total could run into the millions.

French prosecutors have opened a specific cyber-crime investigation into the incident, which the Paris prosecutor's office called a "large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France".

European Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen condemned the hack in a post on X and added: "Food security requires more attention at all levels. Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality."

In a post on X, CoopÃ©rative chief executive Dominique Schelcher said staff were "fully mobilised, in co-ordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible".

He called for an investigation into the hack and said targeting equipment essential to the French food supply was "unacceptable".

Have you been affected by this cyber attack? Share your experience.

World.title: Tom Cruise film Digger forecast to become one of Hollywood's biggest flops
World.content:
Tom Cruise's latest film Digger is expected to lose around $245m (Â£185m), Hollywood analysts have said, after the film's continuing poor performance at the box office.

Ticket sales for the satirical black comedy, which stars Cruise as oil magnate Digger Rockwell, dropped by around 60% in the movie's second weekend in cinemas.

It brings Digger's total box office takings so far to around $35m (Â£26m) globally. The film is estimated to have cost its studio Warner Bros around $280m (Â£211m) to make and market.

But Cruise said last week, external that he "never thought of movies when I'm making them [in terms of] opening weekend," adding he was instead focused on making films that "hopefully will translate, last and evolve".

The film's box office takings relative to its budget mean it could become one of the biggest film flops in Hollywood history.

That would put Digger in the same bracket as other films which lost upwards of $100m, including 1995's Cutthroat Island, 2002's The Adventures of Pluto Nash, 2005's Sahara and 2012's John Carter.

Other films estimated to have lost nine-figure sums include Mars Needs Moms (2011), Amsterdam (2022), The 13th Warrior (1999), The Marvels (2023) and Speed Racer (2008).

Digger's performance stands in sharp contrast to the success of major franchises starring Cruise in recent years, such as new instalments of Top Gun and Mission: Impossible.

Hollywood trade publication Variety said Digger was expected to end its box office run with around $50m (Â£38m) worldwide.

The film would need around $350m (Â£264m) to break even, due to its budget, marketing costs, the portion of ticket sales that go to theatres and the likely spend on an awards season campaign.

However, a Warner Bros spokesman pushed back slightly on the figure, telling Variety the film's break even point was $300m (Â£227m).

Digger was the last standalone release for the studio before its recent takeover by Paramount.

The film is directed by Alejandro G IÃ±Ã¡rritu, best known for films such as Birdman, Babel and The Revenant.

Digger received generally poor reviews from critics, prompting Warner Bros to launch a new marketing campaign urging audiences to "decide for yourself".

World.title: US detains man accused in multi-billion Venezuelan money laundering scheme
World.content:
A Colombian man wanted for allegedly laundering money that had been illegally syphoned off a Venezuelan government welfare plan has been detained in the United States.

The US Department of Justice said Ãlvaro Pulido, 62, had been arrested during a Homeland Security Task Force operation on Sunday, but did not provide further details as to how he ended up in US custody.

Pulido had been in jail in Venezuela since March 2023 accused of diverting profits from the state-run oil company PDVSA.

The US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and State Department had been offering a reward of $10m (Â£7.5m) for information leading to his arrest.

He is due to appear in court on Tuesday, according to a statement released by the US Attorney's Office.

Pulido's arrest comes just two months after Alex Saab, another Colombian businessman with close ties to the Venezuelan government, pleaded guilty to money laundering charges in a US court.

The US State Attorney's Office said that Pulido had been charged in two separate federal indictments "involving the alleged laundering of more than $2bn (Â£1.5bn) in connection with Venezuelan government bribery schemes".

US prosecutors say Pulido, along with four other co-defendants, bribed Venezuelan government officials to secure contracts to provide poor Venezuelans with food and medicine.

They accuse Pulido of wildly overcharging the Venezuelan government and laundering the profits through bank accounts abroad, including in the US.

They also allege that Pulido worked with Alex Saab to launder $350m from a separate bribery scheme involving Venezuela's currency exchange system using bank accounts in Florida.

Until recently, Saab was a powerful figure in the Venezuelan government with close ties to the then-leader, NicolÃ¡s Maduro, who named him minister of industry in 2024.

However, after Maduro was seized by US forces in a raid on Caracas in January and taken to New York to stand trial on drug-trafficking charges, Saab's fate quickly changed.

Less than two weeks after Maduro was seized, the new US-backed interim government of Venezuela sacked Saab from his post as minister, and in May it extradited him to the US.

Last month, Saab pleaded guilty to money laundering charges.

World.title: Court rejects Euracare’s bid to stop inquest into Chimamanda Adichie’s son’s death
World.content:
The Lagos State High Court in Ikoyi on Monday rejected a bid by Eurapharma Care Services Nigeria Limited, operator of Euracare Multi-Specialist Hospital, to stop a coroner’s inquest into the death of Nkanu Adichie-Esege, the 21-month-old son of writer Chimamanda Adichie and her husband, Ivara Esege.

Judge Aishat Opesanwo held that the absence of the child’s body did not, in itself, prevent the coroner from investigating the circumstances of his death, Channels TV reported.

The hospital had argued that the cremation of Nkanu’s remains made a post-mortem examination impossible and could leave the inquest relying on speculation.

It also challenged a directive requiring its medical personnel to present evidence before other parties, describing the arrangement as a violation of its right to a fair hearing.

The couple’s lawyer, Kemi Pinheiro, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), had urged the court to dismiss the hospital’s suit, arguing that it was premature because the coroner had not made any substantive decision that could be challenged through judicial review.

At the hearing on 28 September, Mr Pinheiro said no witness had testified and no substantive finding had been made.

He argued that the hospital was asking the High Court to set aside a decision that did not yet exist.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Lagos State Attorney-General, Lawal Pedro, also a SAN, urged the court to strike out the suit.

Abiodun Layonu and Adeniji Kazeem, both SANs representing Atlantis Paediatric Hospital Limited, supported the objections to the application.

Mr Layonu told the court that the order of evidence presentation had been discussed during proceedings before the coroner on 14 April, when it was agreed that the family would present its evidence first.

But Eurapharma’s lawyer, Taiwo Osipitan, SAN, argued that the hospital should not be required to present its evidence before the family had first led evidence to support its allegations of medical negligence.

On the cremation of the child’s remains, Mr Pinheiro relied on Sections 21 and 31(1) of the Lagos State Coroners’ System Law, arguing that the legislation allowed an inquest to proceed where a body had been destroyed or could not be recovered.

In her ruling, Mrs Opesanwo referred to Section 15(2) of the law, which provides for a compulsory inquest in circumstances covered by the provision involving deaths in medical facilities.

The judge said a coroner’s inquest was a fact-finding exercise, not a criminal or civil trial in which parties were prosecuted or held liable.

“A coroner’s inquest is a fact-finding inquiry… It is not a trial. No one is on trial in a coroner’s court,” she said.

She also held that the coroner had the statutory discretion to determine the order in which witnesses and evidence would be presented, adding that judicial review could not be used to halt proceedings required by law.

How the dispute started

Nkanu died on 7 January after receiving treatment at Atlantis Paediatric Hospital before being referred to Euracare Multi-Specialist Hospital in Victoria Island, Lagos.

His parents alleged that medical negligence contributed to his death, raising concerns about sedation, oxygen administration, monitoring and the hospital’s emergency response.

Euracare has denied wrongdoing, maintaining that its medical personnel followed standard procedures and that the child arrived at its facility critically ill.

The Lagos State Government initiated a coroner’s inquest to establish the circumstances surrounding the toddler’s death.

In June, the High Court granted Eurapharma leave to challenge the proceedings and ordered a temporary suspension of the inquest pending the determination of its application.

In March, the Medical and Dental Practitioners Investigation Panel suspended the hospital’s medical director and two doctors after finding a prima facie case of medical negligence. The finding was not a final determination of liability.

The court’s latest decision clears the way for the inquest to proceed.

World.title: ADC, NDC, PDP decry attacks on opposition parties in Enugu
World.content:
‌The African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) have condemned attacks on opposition parties in Enugu State.

They warned that democracy in the state was heading towards anarchy, calling on security agencies and the federal government to intervene and protect opposition politicians and their supporters.

The parties made the condemnation at a joint press conference held at the Press Centre, Enugu, on Monday, following Saturday’s attacks on NDC members at two different locations in the state.

Narrating the incident, NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chinyeaka Ohaa, said he and his supporters were attacked on Saturday while returning from the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu.

Mr Ohaa said several of his supporters were injured, while vehicles were damaged and mobile phones belonging to some journalists and party members were seized during the incident.

“When I arrived from the airport on 10 October, I was attacked, and my members who came to welcome me were humiliated,” he said.

He alleged that security operatives prevented his supporters from accessing the airport and subsequently blocked his convoy at different locations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the attackers followed his convoy to the party’s campaign office where another attack occurred.

Previous attacks

Mr Ohaa said eight party supporters were injured during an attack a few months ago, including a woman who sustained a gunshot wound to her breast and a man who underwent surgery following injuries to his abdomen.

The NDC candidate urged the state government to investigate the incidents and ensure that those responsible were brought to justice.

Mr Ohaa also urged the state government to allow opposition parties to carry out their legitimate political activities without intimidation.

Similarly, the PDP governorship candidate in Enugu, Uche Nnaji, described the attacks as unacceptable and called for an end to political violence in the state.

Mr Nnaji said opposition parties had come together to express solidarity with the NDC and demanded adequate security for political activities.

“We believe in politics without bitterness. Politics is not a do-or-die affair, and nobody should be harassed or killed because of political differences.

“If you have done something for the state, you do not need to intimidate or kill people for them to see it. You only need to showcase your achievements,” he said.

Mr Nnaji called on security agencies, the federal government, and the international community to pay attention to the political situation in Enugu State.

Also speaking, the ADC governorship candidate in the state, Ocho Obodoeze, expressed solidarity with the NDC over the attacks.

Mr Obodoeze said political violence posed a threat to democracy and should be condemned irrespective of the political affiliation of those affected.

He said his party had suffered similar attacks during a thanksgiving event, when its supporters were chased away, and canopies and chairs were thrown away.

He alleged that the party had also received death threats, which were documented and reported to the State Security Service.

READ ALSO: How attacks on PDP in Enugu may affect Tinubu in 2027 Chieftain

Mr Obodoeze said the presence of security agencies at the airport should ordinarily guarantee the safety of citizens receiving political leaders and other visitors.

He urged the state government to investigate the allegations rather than dismiss opposition parties’ complaints.

Enugu govt denies involvement

The Enugu State Government, in a media briefing on Sunday, denied involvement in the attack.

The Secretary to the Enugu State Government, Chidiebere Onyia, said the airport incident was a matter between the NDC members and the Federal Airport Authority of Nigeria at Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu, because due approval was not given to the party—a claim the NDC has rejected.

(NAN)

World.title: EFCC arraigns Nigerian-American over alleged $320,000 vehicle import fraud
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned a Nigerian-American, Oluwatobi Adegoke, over an alleged vehicle import fraud involving more than $320,000.

Mr Adegoke was arraigned on 8 October before trial judge Olubunmi Abike-Fadipe of the Special Offences Court in Ikeja, Lagos, on one counts of stealing.

He denied EFCC’s allegations, by pleading not guilty to the charge.

According to a statement on Monday by EFCC, the agency arrested him in July over allegations that he was involved in a syndicate operating from the United States.

The commission alleged that Mr Adegoke advertised a 2024 Mercedes-Benz G63 AMG to prospective buyers in Nigeria while living in the US, claiming he could purchase and ship the vehicle to them. Two alleged victims allegedly paid a combined sum of more than $320,000.

The EFCC earlier announced his arrest in June, identifying him as Adegoke Oluwatobi Adams. Reports at the time said Ikechukwu Osita Ifeabunike allegedly paid $145,000 through an intermediary, while Godson Azubuike Amans allegedly paid $175,000 towards the vehicle purchase.

However, the charge read in court refers to $680,000 allegedly belonging to Mr Ifeabunike.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It accused Mr Adegoke of dishonestly converting the money after it was transferred to the account of his company, Omosco Auto Sales LLC, for the purchase of a 2022 G-Wagon from a person identified as Mr Robinson.

The EFCC’s statement did not explain the difference between the $320,000 cited in its account of the alleged fraud and the $680,000 stated in the charge. It also did not reconcile the different vehicle models mentioned.

After the defendant entered his plea, EFCC lawyer, Arazeem Adebayo, asked the court to remand him in a correctional centre and fix a date for trial.

Defence lawyer, Olalekan Abiodun, asked that his client be kept in EFCC custody pending the filing of a bail application. The commission said the court rejected the request.

Mrs Abike-Fadipe ordered that Mr Adegoke be remanded at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre in Lagos.

She adjourned the case until 13 January 2027 for trial.

World.title: FMC Abeokuta workers begin 72-hour warning strike
World.content:
Workers union at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Idi-Aba, Abeokuta, on Monday began a 72-hour warning strike over an alleged stabbing of a medical laboratory scientist by a patient’s relative.

The Chairman of the Medical and Health Workers’ Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), FMC Abeokuta, Abiodun Famuyiwa, disclosed this in an interview with NAN in Abeokuta.

Mr Famuyiwa said the strike involved workers in the centre, excluding doctors, following an alleged stabbing of the scientist while on duty on Sunday night.

“Mr Olasunkanmi Lawal, a medical laboratory scientist, was stabbed in two places, including the head, with an object, and he is now receiving treatment at the hospital.

“The incident has been reported to the police and referred to the appropriate authorities for further action,” he said.

He described the incident as an unacceptable act of violence against a healthcare worker performing his official duties.

He expressed concern over the safety of healthcare professionals in the hospital, saying that no worker should be subjected to physical attacks while providing essential medical services.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also demanded that the incident be investigated and the alleged assailant be prosecuted in accordance with the law.

The MHWUN chairman urged the management to review and strengthen existing arrangements, particularly in clinical and laboratory areas, emergency units, and other vulnerable locations.

He added that the warning strike was intended to express members’ displeasure, demand accountability, and compel the management to address their security concerns.

Meanwhile, the unions, operating under the Joint Action Committee (JAC), also announced the industrial action in a position letter dated 12 October and addressed to the Medical Director of the hospital.

The letter stated that the strike commenced at 11 a.m. on Monday and was scheduled to end at 8 a.m. on Thursday.

NAN reports that the letter was endorsed by representatives of the Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals (NUAHP), MHWUN, and the National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives (NANNM),

Others are the Senior Staff Association of Universities, Teaching Hospitals, Research and Allied Institutions (SSAUTHRIAI), and the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU).

The letter read: “This barbaric act of violence against a healthcare worker carrying out his professional responsibility is condemnable and must not be treated with levity.

‘We consider this incident a serious assault on the dignity, safety, and welfare of healthcare professionals who dedicate their time, knowledge, and energy to providing essential medical services to patients and the public.

“It is deeply disturbing that a facility established to preserve life and promote healing has become a place where healthcare workers may be subjected to physical attacks while discharging their lawful duties.

READ ALSO: FMC Abeokuta Health workers begin indefinite strike

“No healthcare worker deserves to be threatened, assaulted, or stabbed in the course of providing care.

“Disagreement, frustration, or dissatisfaction with any service rendered in the hospital cannot justify violence under any circumstance.”

It also stated that the incident was not merely an attack on the affected medical laboratory scientist, but an attack on the entire workforce of the centre.

“An injury to one member of our professional community is a matter of collective concern, and we cannot remain silent while the safety of our member is placed in jeopardy,” it stated.

(NAN)

World.title: Nigerian govt to invest more in technology, intelligence to tackle insecurity
World.content:
The Nigerian government says it will continue to invest in technology, intelligence and operational capabilities to tackle insecurity, acknowledging that serious security challenges persist in parts of the country despite reported successes by security forces.

The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, said this on Monday during a media chat with senior editors and journalists in Abuja.

Mr Idris defended the administration’s security efforts, saying President Bola Tinubu had strengthened the operational capabilities of the armed forces, intelligence services and other security agencies through improved coordination, equipment, logistics and support for frontline personnel.

He said security forces have recorded successes across several theatres of operation, including the killing of terrorist commanders and criminal kingpins, disruption of insurgent networks, rescue of hostages and dismantling of criminal enclaves.

He said intensified operations against crude oil theft, illegal refining and pipeline vandalism in the Niger Delta had also contributed to improved oil production and the protection of national revenues.

Despite these gains, the minister acknowledged that insecurity remained a serious concern in parts of the country.

“Every incident of terrorism, banditry, kidnapping or communal violence is a matter of grave concern to the President and the Federal Government,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We do not minimise the pain of affected families or the anxiety of communities still confronting these threats.”

Mr Idris assured Nigerians that the government would sustain its efforts to restore security across the country, adding that Mr Tinubu continued to demand results from security chiefs.

“Let me assure Nigerians that the federal government will neither relent nor retreat in its determination to secure every part of our country,” he said.

He said the government’s investments in personnel, technology, intelligence and operational capabilities were aimed at achieving lasting security.

“The security of Nigerians is not negotiable,” he said, adding that the government would continue to protect vulnerable communities and work towards a country where citizens could live, travel, farm, trade and work safely.

Minister urges states to deliver on responsibilities

Mr Idris also urged states and local governments to take greater responsibility for delivering essential services, including urban transport, education, primary healthcare and waste management.

He said the Tinubu administration had taken steps to strengthen states and local governments financially and constitutionally through increased fiscal transfers, efforts to secure local government autonomy, proposals for state police and electricity reforms that empower states to invest in and regulate the sector.

According to the minister, the president has consistently advocated true federalism throughout his political career, and his policies over the past three years have reflected that position.

However, Mr Idris said states and local governments must also step up to their responsibilities, particularly in providing services that directly affect citizens’ daily lives.

Citing a recent World Bank report, he said the combined capital expenditure of states rose by 151 per cent in real terms between 2023 and 2025, with significant increases in spending on transport, education, healthcare and social investment.

He urged Nigerians to hold all three tiers of government accountable for their respective responsibilities.

World.title: NAPTIP receives 105 Nigerians rescued from syndicates in Ghana
World.content:
The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) says it has rescued 105 Nigerians during an operation against cybercrime syndicates in Ghana, as authorities continue efforts to protect victims of exploitation and irregular migration.

In a statement issued on Monday, Vincent Adekoye, NAPTIP’s Head of Press and Public Relations Unit, said the operation was coordinated by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) following contact from Ghana’s Cyber Security Authority.

According to NAPTIP, Ghanaian authorities rescued 119 Nigerians during the operation. Of these, 105 have been repatriated to Nigeria, while the remaining 14 are still undergoing processing.

Several Nigerian security and law enforcement agencies were involved, including the Nigeria Immigration Service, Department of State Services, National Intelligence Agency, and the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons. The Nigerian High Commission in Ghana and other partners also participated.

NAPTIP Director-General Binta Bello, who received the returnees on behalf of the Nigerian government, assured them of their safety and said they would undergo profiling and reintegration procedures.

The agency said the process would help determine their individual circumstances and the assistance they require.

The development highlights the cross-border nature of trafficking and exploitation, a subject explored in recent PREMIUM TIMES investigations into how criminal networks exploit vulnerable Nigerians through deceptive promises of employment, education and better living conditions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that traffickers exploited Benue’s conflict to steal children and women, and that armed conflict, displacement and economic hardship in Benue State had created conditions that traffickers exploited to recruit women and girls and remove children from their families.

The investigation found that more than 300 children were allegedly taken from Yelewata, Daudu and Agban communities in Guma Local Government Area in 2024 through a purported Back-to-School programme. Parents were promised free education, food and accommodation for their children, with assurances that they would return home during Christmas and Easter holidays.

Instead, the children were allegedly moved through orphanage homes in Abuja and Nasarawa State before being distributed to other locations. NAPTIP said some were sold to prospective adopters under the guise of legal adoption.

The agency identified Anderson Archibong, Executive Secretary of the National Council of Child Rights Advocates of Nigeria (NACCRAN), as the alleged mastermind of the operation. NAPTIP said Archibong and other suspects have been arraigned in connection with the case.

The agency previously said it had rescued 105 children linked to the Benue operation, reuniting 101 with their families while four remained in its custody as efforts to trace their relatives continued.

A subsequent NAPTIP announcement reported that more than 180 children had been rescued in operations across five states, including children allegedly taken from conflict-affected communities under the guise of educational support.

The latest repatriation from Ghana involves a separate operation targeting cybercrime syndicates. NAPTIP’s statement did not specify whether any of the 105 returnees were identified as victims of human trafficking or whether they had been compelled to participate in cybercrime.

The agency said it would screen the returnees and provide support according to their individual circumstances.

Mrs Bello encouraged the returnees to remain calm as the government carried out the necessary procedures. NAPTIP said its engagement reflected its responsibility to protect their dignity, welfare, and safety.

The agency also thanked the Ghanaian authorities, particularly the Cyber Security Authority and Ghana Immigration Service, as well as the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency, for their operational support.

It commended ONSA, Nigerian security agencies and other partners for coordinating the operation.

NAPTIP urged Nigerians to exercise caution when considering employment, scholarships, and other opportunities abroad, particularly offers with unrealistic promises, vague job descriptions, or suspicious recruitment arrangements.

The agency said it would continue to strengthen cooperation with national and international partners to combat human trafficking and related forms of exploitation.

For families affected by trafficking in Benue, the latest development comes amid continuing efforts to trace missing children and prosecute those accused of exploiting displaced communities.

NAPTIP has said prolonged insecurity and the displacement of families have increased vulnerability to trafficking in Benue, which the agency previously identified as a leading source of trafficking cases in Nigeria.

The agency’s latest operation in Ghana underscores the importance of cross-border cooperation in identifying, rescuing, and assisting Nigerians caught in exploitative networks. However, the circumstances of the returnees and the nature of their involvement in the cybercrime operations remain unclear from the information released by NAPTIP.

World.title: AI, energy supply shock, mounting debts headline IMF/World Bank meetings in Bangkok
World.content:
Financial experts, government officials, central bank chiefs, heads of multilateral organisations and other participants are gathered this week in Bangkok, Thailand, for the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank scheduled to be held between October 12 and 18.

Participants are expected to deliberate on the disruptive potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the global economy, the widening war in the Middle East and its impact on the global economy, the global energy supply shock, mounting debts, and rising interest rates that pose daunting risks to global economic growth.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva says the Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre will host 18,000 people who were registered to attend the meetings, 4,000 more than the last off-site meetings held in Morocco in October 2023.

The IMF has made no significant change to its forecast of 3% global growth in 2026, and the body says some countries are expected to be downgraded because of war and reduced energy exports.

The meetings are also expected to address the growing public debt burden that has slowed growth and worsened inflation, as public debt remains at its highest level since World War Two and will exceed 100% of GDP before 2030, according to the IMF.

Emerging markets and low-income countries are particularly vulnerable, given high public debt levels that will have to be renegotiated at higher interest rates.

Equally important on the agenda is the precarity of platform-driven labour, amid AI-enabled automation and the changing future of work.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

On Monday, Ms Georgieva said Artificial Intelligence (AI) could affect about 40 per cent of jobs globally, urging governments to prepare workers for the changing labour market. She described AI as a “slow-moving tsunami” for the labour market, saying it could augment, downgrade or eliminate jobs.

IMF estimates show that AI could affect about 60 per cent of jobs in advanced economies and 23 per cent in low-income countries, reflecting the slower spread of AI rather than greater protection from its effects.

Bangkok

The Bangkok meetings are taking place amid disruptions and a war that has negatively affected energy supplies, especially via the Middle East.

Flights to Bangkok, the host city of this year’s off-site meetings, often route through the Middle East, creating immediate challenges for global travellers heading to Thailand’s capital.

On Sunday, there were attacks on Saudi airports, prompting disruptions to international travel.

The IMF and World Bank’s last off-site annual meetings took place in Morocco in 2023.

Nigeria’s participation

Already, Nigeria’s Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has arrived in Bangkok, Thailand, to lead the nation’s delegation to the meetings

A statement from the Federal Ministry of Finance said the annual gathering provides Nigeria with an opportunity to engage with international financial institutions and development partners on economic issues affecting the country and its development priorities.

Mr Oyedele’s presence at the meetings is equally expected to allow the Federal Government to present its economic priorities to development organisations and international partners. He is also expected to discuss how external cooperation can support domestic reform efforts.

The finance ministry website also says that, on the sidelines of the meetings, Nigeria will convene investors, project sponsors and public institutions around a curated pipeline of bankable opportunities across strategic sectors. The programme is focused on private-capital mobilisation, food security and infrastructure development. Another event focuses on investor and project-owner conversations at Fairmont Bangkok Sukhumvit.

PREMIUM TIMES newspaper is in Bangkok, Thailand’s capital, to report on the meetings and other policy decisions as they affect the global economy and Nigeria’s domestic affairs.

World.title: Top 10 African companies ranked among Forbes’ best employers in 2026
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

South Africa’s Nedbank has emerged as Africa’s highest-ranked company on Forbes’ World’s Best Employers 2026 list, placing 26th globally, while Nigeria’s Guaranty Trust Bank (GTBank) is the only Nigerian firm among the continent’s 10 highest-ranked entries.

The ranking, compiled by Forbes in partnership with Statista, features 900 companies headquartered in 52 countries, following a survey of more than 300,000 employees across over 50 countries.

Nine of Africa’s 10 highest-ranked companies are headquartered in South Africa, reflecting the country’s strong representation among large multinational employers.

GTBank ranks 277th globally and 7th in Africa, ahead of South African energy and chemicals company Sasol, healthcare group Mediclinic International and financial services firm Sanlam.

Here are the 10 highest-ranked African companies on Forbes’ World’s Best Employers 2026 list.

Nedbank — 26th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Banking and financial services

Nedbank is Africa’s highest-ranked company on the 2026 list, placing 26th globally. The South African banking group rose from 49th position in the 2025 edition, moving up 23 places to lead the continent’s entries.

The latest position earned by Nedbank puts it ahead of other African banking groups, including Standard Bank Group, Absa Group and FirstRand.

Standard Bank Group — 54th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Banking and financial services

Standard Bank Group ranks second among African companies with the best employers and 54th globally. The bank fell from 28th position in 2025, dropping 26 places in the latest edition.

Despite the decline, it remains one of Africa’s highest-ranked employers, alongside three other South African banking groups in the global top 105.

Absa Group — 98th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Banking and financial services

Absa Group ranks third among African companies and 98th worldwide. The South African financial services group recorded a slight decline from 97th position in the previous edition. Absa’s latest ranking significantly keeps it among the continent’s four highest-ranked employers, all of which are South African banking groups.

FirstRand — 104th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Banking and financial services

FirstRand ranks fourth among African companies and 104th globally. The financial services group is the parent company of banking brands including First National Bank and Rand Merchant Bank.

MTN Group — 133rd globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Telecommunications

MTN Group ranks fifth among African companies and 133rd globally. The telecommunications company rose 33 places from its 166th position in 2025 and retained its position as the world’s third-highest-ranked telecommunications employer.

MTN operates across multiple African markets, including Nigeria. Its ranking refers to the wider group rather than its Nigerian operations alone.

Investec — 197th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Banking and financial services

Investec ranks sixth among African companies and 197th globally. The international financial services group operates in banking, wealth management and investment services.

Guaranty Trust Bank — 277th globally

Country: Nigeria

Sector: Banking and financial services

Guaranty Trust Bank is the only Nigerian company among Africa’s 10 highest-ranked employers on the 2026 list.

The commercial bank ranks 277th globally, making it the seventh-highest-ranked African entry and its latest position places it ahead of Sasol, Mediclinic International and Sanlam in the continental ranking.

GTBank’s inclusion also gives Nigeria representation in a list otherwise dominated by South African companies.

Sasol — 298th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Energy and chemicals

Sasol ranks eighth among African companies and 298th globally. The South African energy and chemicals group operates across industries involving fuels and chemical products.

Sealing a place in the global 300 is significant as it makes the Energy company one of the continent’s highest-ranked employers outside the banking and telecommunications sectors.

Mediclinic International — 460th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Healthcare

Mediclinic International ranks ninth among African companies and 460th worldwide. The healthcare group operates hospitals and provides specialist medical services.

Sanlam — 470th globally

Country: South Africa

Sector: Insurance and financial services

Sanlam completes the African top 10, ranking 470th globally. The South African financial services group has interests in insurance, investments, retirement savings and wealth management. Its placement makes it the 10th-highest-ranked African company in the 2026 list.
