World.title: Houthi official warns of ‘swift, painful response’ if US enters Yemen war
World.content:
Yemen’s Houthi armed forces patrol as Yemeni prisoners loyal to the Houthi authorities arrive in the capital Sanaa on September 12, 2026, after being released on the west coast where he and others were being held by Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces. Some 210 prisoners were released following a week-long offensive, in which the Iran-backed Houthis on September 11, 2026, captured Yemen’s Red Sea coast from the internationally recognised government, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed amid the US-Iran war. (Photo by Mohammed HUWAIS / AFP)

A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a “painful response” if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington’s help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks.

Yemen’s civil war — in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis — reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.

The Houthis quickly began targeting Saudi oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs, including with a string of lethal strikes on Riyadh’s airport, rocking the world’s top oil exporter.

Blasts resounded over the capital again on Monday night, with the Saudi coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile.

Following an attack Saturday at the airport that killed 13 people, US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom.

“If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told AFP in an interview.

He also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”.

Saturday’s strike on King Khalid International Airport was the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, and also left hundreds wounded.

Trump said the attack was “not acceptable” and that he would be speaking to the kingdom’s de facto leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, telling reporters the US was “going to look at” the possibility of joining Saudi strikes.

Four people died in earlier strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh’s outskirts on Monday.

– ‘Serious’ response –

Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.

Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told a conference in Riyadh on Monday that the recent events had “tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience”.

“The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”

CCTV footage of Saturday’s attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden blast tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.

The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats.

In the evening, mobile phones received a loud government alert warning of a “hostile aerial threat” before the announcement of the interception.

It was the first use of the phone alert system in Riyadh in weeks, with no official reason given for the lack of messaging during the attacks targeting the capital in recent days.

– Flights suspended –

The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said US government employees must obtain its authorisation before using any airport in the kingdom, and urged US citizens to “take extreme caution” if they chose to do so.

The mission also said “American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events” in Saudi Arabia.

The UAE’s national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week, and also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah.

Bahrain’s national carrier Gulf Air said it too was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday.

US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh, scheduled for October 23.

Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.

Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University, said that despite some success, “Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves”.

Riyadh leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”.

The long-running Yemeni civil war has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.

UN rights chief Volker Turk said he was “appalled by the repeated attacks” on Saudi Arabia, but urged both sides to back down, adding “continued fighting will only unleash further misery with no end in sight”.

AFP

World.title: Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway progressing as planned – FG
World.content:
David Umahi

The Federal Government says construction of the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is progressing as planned, dismissing reports that the project had been abandoned for the East-West Road.

Sen.​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‍⁠​​‍‌​ David Umahi, Minister of Works, stated this while briefing newsmen on Monday at the State House in Abuja.

Umahi said construction is ongoing along various sections of the highway, adding that the project remained intact and was being implemented as designed.

“The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is moving and moving even faster than envisaged. Don’t forget that Section One, covering 147.47 kilometres, is being fully constructed in Lagos,” he said.

The minister said Section Two, covering 55 kilometres, was expected to be ready by mid-November.

He said work is ongoing on Sections Three A and Three B, covering about 75 kilometres in Akwa Ibom and Cross River states, with progress exceeding 40 per cent.

Umahi added that construction is ongoing on Sections Four A and Four B, covering 65 kilometres across Ogun and Ondo states.

He said work had also commenced on Section Five, covering 62.5 kilometres in Akwa Ibom, with more than 20 per cent progress recorded within less than three months.

The minister explained that the ministry is seeking President Bola Tinubu’s approval to incorporate about 400 kilometres of the East-West Road into the ongoing infrastructure development programme.

He said the proposed intervention would cover sections linking Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom and Cross River states.

Umahi said the East-West Road required attention because some sections had suffered damage from flooding, citing affected portions in Delta and Edo.

He stressed that the proposed work on the East-West Road would complement, rather than replace, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

“Nobody has abandoned the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. We have designers and surveyors working along the route, including in Edo, Delta, Bayelsa and Rivers,” he said.

Umahi said the Federal Government is undertaking surveys along the route to ensure the project’s continued development and integration with other infrastructure projects in the Niger Delta.

He added that the highway remained part of the Federal Government’s legacy infrastructure projects and that its alignment would not be altered.

“The 750-kilometre coastal highway is intact and cannot be changed. Nobody has the power to change it because it is already designed and ongoing,” he said.

(NAN)

World.title: Tinubu’s N60 fuel discount was a ‘stunt’ — Makinde campaign
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

The Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of using its N60 per litre petrol discount as a political stunt to deflect public anger rather than ease Nigerians’ economic hardship.

The campaign organisation said the reported increase in petrol prices from N1,370 to N1,410 per litre at filling stations in Abuja and other parts of the country had reinforced its earlier warning that the discount was no solution to the rising cost of living.

In a statement by its Director of Communications, Richard Ihediwa, the organisation accused the administration of using propaganda to project an image of compassion while Nigerians continued to bear the burden of economic hardship.

“The latest development also strengthens our position that no amount of propaganda can conceal the consequences of policies, whose promised benefits are not reflected in the daily lives of ordinary Nigerians,” it said.

The organisation also faulted the government’s economic reform narrative, arguing that the promise of bold reforms had become an excuse for imposing greater hardship on citizens.

“Nigerians cannot continue to be confronted with the hollow slogan of ‘bold economic reforms,’ which has become a euphemism for transferring the crushing burden of economic hardship onto citizens already struggling to survive,” the campaign organisation said.

It called for a fundamental rethink of the policies driving the hardship, warning that temporary concessions would remain inadequate without changes to the country’s economic direction.

Turning its criticism into a political argument, the organisation presented the Makinde/Daura ticket as an alternative to the Tinubu administration, citing its RESET NIGERIA Agenda, which it said was anchored on responsible economic management, transparent resource governance and productive investment.

“Nigeria needs a complete RESET under a Makinde Presidency and not this propaganda-driven administration that have failed in all ramifications,” Ihediwa said.

World.title: Meet Nigeria’s longest-serving senators
World.content:
Senate setting

By Adegboyega Adeleye

As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections, the careers of its longest-serving senators offer a look at the lawmakers whose years in the upper chamber have been shaped by electoral victories, political shifts and returns to office.

Some have served for several terms, building lengthy records in the Senate, while others have had breaks in their legislative careers before returning to the chamber.

Their years of service reflect the different paths they have taken to remain in the Senate since Nigeria’s return to democracy in 1999.

Here is a look at Nigeria’s longest-serving senators.

Ahmad Lawan (19 years in the Senate)

Party: All Progressives Congress (APC).

Ahmad Lawan, who represents Yobe North Senatorial District, began his federal legislative career in 1999 when he was elected to the House of Representatives to represent Bade/Jakusko Federal Constituency in Yobe State.

He served in the lower chamber until 2007, when he transitioned to the Senate. He has represented Yobe North since then and served as President of the Senate from 2019 to 2023.

Lawan’s 27-year legislative career spans both chambers, while his Senate tenure began in 2007. The former senate president remains one of the lawmakers who have served in the National Assembly since the beginning of the Fourth Republic.

Ali Ndume (15 years in the Senate)

Party: All Progressives Congress (APC).

Ali Ndume.

Ali Ndume, who represents Borno South Senatorial District, entered the National Assembly in 2003 as a member of the House of Representatives, representing Chibok/Damboa/Gwoza Federal Constituency in Borno State.

He served in the House until 2011, when he was elected to the Senate. Since then, he has won successive elections to represent Borno South and held leadership positions, including Senate Majority Leader and Senate Chief Whip.

Ndume’s federal legislative career spans both chambers. He was previously affiliated with the All Nigeria Peoples Party and the Peoples Democratic Party before joining the APC.

Enyinnaya Abaribe (19 years in the Senate — since 2007)

Party: Labour Party (LP)

Sen. Enyinnaya Abaribe

Enyinnaya Abaribe has represented Abia South Senatorial District since 2007, when he was elected to the Senate on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party.

Before joining the National Assembly, Abaribe served as deputy governor of Abia State from 1999 to 2003 under Governor Orji Uzor Kalu.

He won successive elections to retain his Senate seat and served as Senate Minority Leader during the Ninth National Assembly. He left the PDP and joined the All Progressives Grand Alliance in 2022 before moving to the African Democratic Congress in March 2026. He subsequently joined the Labour Party in May 2026.

Unlike lawmakers who moved from the House of Representatives to the Senate, Abaribe’s federal legislative career began in the upper chamber as his service in the Senate dates to 2007.

Adamu Aliero (about 12 years in the Senate)

Party: All Progressives Congress (APC)

Adamu Aliero, who represents Kebbi Central Senatorial District, first entered the Senate in 2007 after serving two terms as governor of Kebbi State from 1999 to 2007.

His initial Senate tenure ended in 2008 when he was appointed Minister of the Federal Capital Territory. He returned to the Senate in 2015 and won re-election in 2019 and 2023.

Aliero’s legislative career has therefore not been continuous since 2007. He served in the Senate from 2007 to 2008 before returning in 2015, accumulating approximately 12 years in the chamber across the two periods.

He won his 2023 Senate seat on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party but defected to the APC in May 2025. The Senate formally announced the defection during plenary.

Solomon Olamilekan Adeola (11 years in the Senate)

Party: All Progressives Congress (APC)

Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, represents Ogun West Senatorial District. He began his federal legislative career in 2011, when he was elected to the House of Representatives to represent Alimosho Federal Constituency in Lagos State on the platform of the defunct Action Congress of Nigeria.

Adeola served in the House until 2015, when he won election to the Senate representing Lagos West. He retained the Lagos West seat for two terms before winning the Ogun West senatorial seat in 2023.

His legislative career spans both chambers and two senatorial districts. His National Assembly service dates to 2011, while his Senate tenure began in 2015.

Danjuma Goje (15 years in the Senate)

Party: All Progressives Congress (APC)

Goje was elected to the Senate in 2011 and won re-election in 2015, 2019 and 2023. His federal legislative career began in the Senate rather than the House of Representatives.

He initially contested for the Senate on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party before moving to the APC. He remains an APC senator representing Gombe Central.

World.title: IPO: Dangote Petroleum Refinery extends offer period by two weeks
World.content:
By Peter Egwuatu

Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE (DPRP) has announced the extension of the application period for its Initial Public Offering (IPO) by two weeks, following approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), amid what has become one of the most significant capital market offerings in Nigerian and African history.

The IPO, which consists of 4,100,000,000 ordinary shares of US$0.000013 each at N525.00 per share, opened on Monday, September 14, 2026, and was originally scheduled to close on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The application period will now remain open until Tuesday, October 27, 2026.

The extension follows exceptionally strong interest from a broad spectrum of eligible investors across Africa and other international markets. Since the launch of the offer, investor participation has underscored the growing confidence in Dangote Refinery’s long-term growth prospects and its strategic role in transforming Africa’s energy landscape.

In a chat with media men in the Refinery, President of Dangote Group, Aliko Dangote said: The IPO is going very well. We will extend the closing date because we want more of our African brothers and sisters to participate. Following our discussions with the Nairobi Stock Exchange, we have identified what we believe is the best way to facilitate participation. We are now trying to replicate that arrangement with other African exchanges to ensure wider participation…But when it comes to the amount of money we originally intended to raise, we have already received subscriptions amounting to more than three or four times that figure…So, it is not about the amount of money. It is about the number of people who will have the opportunity to participate in this offer. That means quite a lot to us.”

The company said, the additional two-week period will support ongoing market-access initiatives across African jurisdictions, including the expansion of distribution channels and the rollout of unsponsored depository receipt programmes designed to facilitate seamless cross-border investment.

It will also provide more time for prospective investors to complete account-opening procedures, identity verification processes, and other regulatory requirements necessary for participation in the offer.

Speaking on the extension, David Bird, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE, said: “We welcome the SEC’s approval of the extension, which will give more investors across Africa the opportunity to participate in the Offer. From the outset, our ambition has been to enable as many people as possible to participate in the IPO and share in DPRP’s future growth. The additional time will help us extend that opportunity to more investors across Africa.”

World.title: IPOB rejects report on resumption of sit-at-home
World.content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

NNEWI — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has rejected an alleged police intelligence report claiming that the group and its Eastern Security Network (ESN) planned to resume enforcement of Monday sit-at-home orders in the South-East.

The group, in a statement issued by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Emma Powerful, said it had no plan to enforce a sit-at-home order from October 12, 2026.

The statement was a response to an alleged police intelligence report dated October 9, 2026, which reportedly raised concerns about a possible resumption of sit-at-home enforcement in the region.

IPOB said it did not issue any directive to its members or the ESN to enforce the order, maintaining that its position on the matter remained unchanged.

“There is no voice note. There is no order from IPOB or ESN to resume any sit-at-home. There is no plan by this movement to enforce anything on the people of the South-East or Imo State,” the statement said.

The group also called on the Nigeria Police Force to provide verifiable evidence for the allegations contained in the reported intelligence document, including the basis for linking the alleged message to IPOB or ESN.

IPOB said its activities were focused on its stated objective of Biafran self-determination through peaceful means.

The group further reiterated its position on the forthcoming elections, saying it intended to boycott them.

IPOB also called on the Federal Government to give greater attention to the economic challenges facing Nigerians, including hunger and unemployment.

It urged the authorities to prioritise measures that would ease hardship and address the concerns of citizens.

The statement did not include a response from the police on the reported intelligence document or the allegations attributed to it.

World.title: Accord Atiku respect due to him –  APC tells members
World.content:
Atiku Abubakar

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has urged its members to accord former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar the respect due to his former office and status as a presidential candidate, despite accusing him of disrespecting President Bola Tinubu.

The council’s directive followed public reactions to Atiku’s decision to address Tinubu as “Bola”, which it described as unbecoming of a former vice-president and a presidential aspirant.

In a statement issued on Monday, the council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake, said party leaders, spokespersons, members and support groups should continue to show Atiku the courtesies due to him, notwithstanding their disagreement with his conduct.

“Without any regard to his personal choice to disrespect the office he is aspiring to occupy, the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has implored all party leaders, spokespersons, party members and support groups to accord all the respect, courtesies and regard due to Alhaji Atiku Abubakar as former Vice President of Nigeria and a Presidential candidate,” the statement said.

The council faulted Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, for what it described as a lack of decorum in addressing the President.

It also accused him of allowing political animosity and ambition to influence his public conduct since losing the 2023 presidential election.

The APC council, however, said it would not follow what it characterised as Atiku’s approach to political engagement.

It added that its campaign would focus on issues affecting Nigerians, including the party’s programmes, Tinubu’s record in office and what it described as the administration’s efforts to move the country from reforms to prosperity ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: Budo-Osho, Tanke, Ilorin Land Protest: Developer Claims Title Over Disputed Land
World.content:
The dispute between Kwara State residents and Sammya Nigeria Limited, an estate developer, over a piece of land in Budo-Osho, Tanke area of Ilorin, the capital of Kwara State, has taken a different dimension.

Some landowners in Kwara State recently protested at the Kwara State Government House and the state’s Bureau of Land over an alleged takeover of their properties by Sammya Nigeria Limited, a company they accused of claiming ownership of a large expanse of land and demolishing buildings belonging to residents.

However, Sammya Nigeria Limited, while reacting to the development on Monday, said the information circulating on social media alleging that buildings were demolished at Budo-Osho, Tanke, Ilorin, on the orders of the Kwara State Government was untrue.

Sammya Nigeria Limited, in a statement, said it acquired the land from the Kwara State Government in 2018 and stated that it holds three Certificates of Occupancy (C of O) covering three locations: Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3.

The General Manager of Sammya Nigeria Limited, Olatunji Idowu, while explaining the events leading to the protest by the Kwara community, said approximately two months ago, when the company was preparing to commence development work in Phases 2 and 3, it approached the Bureau of Lands, the government agency responsible for land administration in Kwara State, to identify and mark structures encroaching on its titled land.

He said the Bureau of Lands carried out the exercise and submitted a land encroachment report to their office.

“Following this exercise, some individuals who allegedly occupied portions of the titled land without proof of ownership were informed that they had encroached on legally titled property.

“Two days later, these individuals reportedly attempted to disrupt our construction activities. Consequently, we submitted a petition to the Commissioner of Police, Kwara State Police Command, and invited community leaders, including Akorede and the Magaji of Tapa, to address the situation.

“They were advised not to disrupt our operations and were directed to channel any grievances through the appropriate government authorities rather than confronting the developers.

“When we resumed work on Friday of the previous week, some individuals reportedly went to the Kwara State Government House to protest, alleging that the developer was taking over their properties and demolishing their buildings.

“According to our account, the government officials who attended to them contacted the relevant land authority, which explained that the individuals had encroached on titled land.

“Subsequently, the individuals returned to the site to disrupt our operations. However, security personnel present at the location prevented them from doing so.

“On Saturday, when no construction work was scheduled, the same individuals allegedly returned to the site and began destroying sections of our perimeter fence,” Idowu said.

Idowu explained further that it was important to clarify that the demolition exercise was not carried out on the orders of the Kwara State Government.

“We are the developers of the estate and have obtained approval for the estate layout.

“The structures affected were those obstructing the planned roads within the estate and situated on our titled property. As part of the approved development, roads must be opened and obstructions within their alignments removed,” Idowu explained.

He further said, “Some buildings in the area remain standing because they were not affected by the road alignment.

“Therefore, the claim that the Kwara State Government ordered the demolition of residents’ buildings is misleading and does not reflect our account of the circumstances surrounding the incident,” he said.

He said Sammya Nigeria Limited had submitted a further petition to the Commissioner of Police, Kwara State Police Command, requesting an investigation into the incident.

Idowu further alleged that, “last month, the leaders of the land grabbers in person of Magaji Akorede and Magaji Tapa were invited to the State Police Command, Ilorin, after our petition to the Commissioner of Police, not to disrupt our activities on the site again. The instructions was not complied with, they came on 10th and 11th October and destroyed our Fence and carted away other valuables”.

“We also intend to seek appropriate action against those responsible for damaging our property. We have the relevant land ownership documents, photographs, and video recordings to support our position and assist the police in their investigation,” he said.

“Our position is that the incident arose from alleged encroachment on our titled land and the obstruction of approved development activities, rather than from any demolition order issued by the Kwara State Government.

“We remain committed to developing the estate in accordance with the approved layout and to resolving any genuine disputes through the appropriate legal and governmental channels,” Idowu explained.

Idowu said by obtaining the Certificate of Occupancy (C of O) from the Kwara State Government by Sammya Nigeria Limited, it had met the constitutional requirement for owning land anywhere in Nigeria.

Efforts to get the views of the Kwara residents (protesters) proved abortive, as our reporter could not identify any of their leaders or obtain their contacts.

World.title: Everything You Thought You Knew About Milk
World.content:
Tito Ipinmoye

If you grew up in Nigeria in the 90s or early 2000s, chances are you didn’t learn about milk from a science class. You learnt about it from television. Back then, adverts were part of our childhood. We didn’t reach for a remote every time the commercials came on. We sang the jingles, quoted the catchphrases and years later, many of us can still remember them word for word.

For me, one advert stands above the rest. It followed a young Kanu Nwankwo as he dribbled a football through the dusty streets of Owerri on an errand for his mother. He left home with nothing but a football at his feet, dribbling all the way to the market. Just as a tin of milk slipped from the market woman’s hands, he flicked it back into the air with effortless skill. She smiled and said: “Papilo, I know say one day you go make us proud.”

As children, we believed her. Not because we understood marketing, but because those adverts made us believe that greatness could begin anywhere. They told us that a boy from Owerri, Nigeria could become one of Africa’s greatest footballers. They told us that ordinary children with big dreams could grow into extraordinary adults.

And somewhere between that advert and my mum pouring milk into my breakfast cereal every morning before school, I came to believe two things. The first was that milk helped build strong bones and teeth. The second was that maybe, just maybe, I could become whoever I dreamed of becoming.

Years later, after becoming a dietitian, I realised that my childhood understanding wasn’t wrong, it was simply incomplete. Today, conversations about milk have become surprisingly complicated. Social media is filled with conflicting opinions. Some people insist milk is only for children. Others believe it causes weight gain. Some assume all milk is the same, while others believe dairy milk and non-dairy offer identical nutrition.

As nutrition professionals, we know that the truth is rarely found in headlines or viral videos. It is found in evidence. So, let’s separate what we know about milk from what we only think we know.

What Exactly Is Milk?

From a scientific perspective, milk is the natural nutrient-rich fluid produced by mammals to nourish their young during the earliest stages of life. For humans, cow’s milk is the most widely consumed form of dairy milk and has been part of diets around the world for generations. But from a nutrition perspective, milk is much more than its definition. It is a naturally nutrient-dense food that provides a unique combination of high-quality protein, calcium, phosphorus, vitamin B12, riboflavin and other essential nutrients that work together to support growth, bone health, muscle function, energy production and overall wellbeing throughout life.

Unlike many foods that contribute just one or two key nutrients, milk delivers several essential nutrients in one convenient food. This is one of the reasons it has remained a staple in many cultures and continues to play an important role in healthy eating patterns across different stages of life. Yet despite these nutritional benefits, milk remains one of the most misunderstood foods on our tables.

Over the years, I’ve heard people say that milk is only for children, that it causes weight gain or that all milk products are the same. Social media has only amplified these conversations, making it increasingly difficult to separate evidence from opinion. So, let’s look at some of the most common myths about milk and what science tells us.

Why Milk Matters

One of the things I have learned after years of working as a dietitian is that conversations about milk often focus on just one nutrient: calcium. Yes, milk is well known for supporting strong bones and healthy teeth, but that’s only one part of the story. Milk provides a unique combination of nutrients that work together to support the body in different ways. Rather than contributing just one benefit, it supplies several essential nutrients in a single food, each playing its own role in maintaining good health.

High-quality protein helps build and repair muscles, organs and other body tissues. It’s essential for growth in children and helps adults maintain muscle mass throughout life.

Calcium and phosphorus work together to support strong bones and healthy teeth. These nutrients are especially important during childhood and adolescence, when bones are developing rapidly, but they also remain important throughout adulthood to help maintain bone health.

Vitamin B12 plays an essential role in the production of healthy red blood cells and supports the normal functioning of the nervous system. Riboflavin (vitamin B2) helps the body convert the food we eat into the energy we need for everyday activities. Many milk products are also fortified with vitamins A and D. Vitamin A supports healthy vision and the normal functioning of the immune system, while vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium effectively, making it an important partner in maintaining strong bones.

What makes milk unique isn’t that it contains one remarkable nutrient. It’s that it brings many important nutrients together in one food. That combination is one of the reasons milk has remained part of healthy dietary patterns across different cultures and generations. A glass of milk doesn’t provide just one nutrient. It provides a package of nutrients working together to support growth, development and overall wellbeing.

Myth 1: ‘Milk Is Only for Children’

One of the most common misconceptions I hear is that milk is something we eventually outgrow, that once we become adults, it no longer has a place in our diet. I understand where that idea comes from. Many of us first encountered milk as children. It was stirred into our morning pap, added to cereal before school or mixed into a warm cup of tea on rainy days. Over time, it’s easy to begin thinking of milk as a “children’s food”. But our bodies tell a different story.

While our nutritional needs change throughout life, they never stop. In fact, the nutrients milk provides continue to support us in different ways as we grow older. For children, milk contributes high-quality protein, calcium and other essential nutrients that support healthy growth and the development of strong bones and teeth. During the teenage years, when growth accelerates and nutritional demands increase, these nutrients remain just as important.

As adults, the focus shifts. Growth may slow, but maintaining muscle mass, preserving bone health and meeting our daily nutrient needs become priorities. The high-quality protein, calcium and other vitamins and minerals found in milk continue to contribute to those goals as part of a balanced diet.

For older adults, maintaining muscle strength and bone health becomes increasingly important. Adequate protein helps preserve muscle as we age, while calcium and vitamin D, where milk is fortified with vitamin D, continue to support healthy bones. In other words, milk doesn’t stop being relevant because we grow older, its role simply changes. The nutrients remain valuable. What changes is how our bodies use them at different stages of life. Perhaps that’s a better way to think about it.

Milk grows with us, not because every person must drink milk every day, but because the nutrients it provides continue to support health from childhood through older adulthood as part of a healthy, balanced diet.

Myth 2: ‘Milk Causes Weight Gain’

If you’ve spent any time on social media, you’ve probably come across someone confidently declaring that milk is “too fattening” or should be avoided if you’re trying to manage your weight. It’s a message that’s repeated so often that many people now accept it as fact. The reality, however, is much less dramatic. No single food causes weight gain on its own. Weight gain occurs when, over time, we consistently consume more energy than our bodies use. Overall dietary patterns, portion sizes, physical activity, sleep and other lifestyle factors all play a role. This is why it’s important to understand the different dairy milk options available rather than assuming they all have the same nutritional profile.

Full Cream Milk naturally contains milk fat and provides high-quality protein, calcium and a range of essential vitamins and minerals. It can be enjoyed as part of a healthy, balanced diet by individuals and families whose nutritional needs and preferences align with this type of dairy milk.

Filled Milk, on the other hand, is a dairy milk product in which part or all of the natural milk fat has been replaced with vegetable oils. While its fat composition differs from that of Full Cream Milk, it continues to provide important nutrients such as protein and calcium, giving consumers another dairy milk option to suit different nutritional needs and preferences. The important question, therefore, isn’t whether milk is “good” or “bad.” It’s whether the product you choose fits your overall dietary pattern, lifestyle and nutritional needs. Nutrition is rarely about eliminating one food, it is about building balanced eating habits over time.

Myth 3: ‘All Milk Is the Same’

At first glance, it’s easy to see why many people believe all milk is the same. Walk into any supermarket and you’ll find shelves lined with products that look similar, often displayed side by side. But while they may all be found in the same aisle, they are not all the same. One of the biggest misconceptions I encounter is the belief that every white powder added to tea, coffee or cereal is simply “milk.” These products are designed for different purposes, and understanding those differences is an important part of making informed nutrition decisions.

Broadly speaking, consumers will come across three main categories: Dairy milk, such as Full Cream Milk and Filled Milk, which provide high-quality protein, calcium and other essential nutrients. Creamers, which are designed primarily to add creaminess, texture and flavour to beverages such as tea and coffee. They serve a different purpose from dairy milk and do not provide the same nutritional profile. Ultimately, the best choice begins with understanding what each product is intended to do. When we know the difference between dairy milk, and creamers, we can choose the product that best fits our nutritional needs instead of assuming they are all nutritionally equivalent.

Final Thoughts

Whenever I think about milk, I don’t think first about football. I think about the words of a mother to a young boy: “Papilo, I know say one day you go make us proud.” As children, we saw a story about dreams. Looking back, I realize that the advert gave us more than nostalgia. It sparked a conversation about nutrition that many of us are still having today.

The difference is that, as adults and for me, as a dietitian we now have the opportunity to replace assumptions with evidence. We can look beyond the stories we grew up with and make informed choices based on nutrition science. The stories that shaped our childhood sparked our curiosity. Science helps us make informed choices. And that’s something worth passing on to the next generation.

* Ipinmoye is the author of ‘A Dietitian’s Perspective on Why Milk Still Deserves a Place at the Table.’

World.title: Akwa Ibom Ex-agitators Pass Vote of Confidence on Otuaro, Reaffirm Support for Tinubu, NSA Ribadu
World.content:
Akwa Ibom Ex-Militants Forum has passed a vote of confidence on the Special Adviser to the President on Niger Delta Affairs, Dr. Dennis Brutu Otuaro, while reaffirming its support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu.

The Forum, in a statement jointly signed by its President, Elder Imoh S. Okoko, Secretary, Sunny Affiah, and other leaders including Ekpo Ekpo, Henry Okon Etete, Elder Udom Ebetor and Udo Bassey, expressed its unwavering support for Otuaro and strongly condemned recent calls by certain individuals and groups for his removal from office.

The group said as stakeholders and beneficiaries of the Niger Delta peace process, they recognised the critical role of the Presidential Amnesty Programme (PAP) in sustaining peace, rehabilitation, reintegration, human-capital development and economic empowerment across the region.

The Forum also condemned the use of ethnic sentiment, sectional interests and personal grievances to undermine the leadership of PAP, emphasizing that its position is directed at individuals and interest groups and not against the Ijaw ethnic nationality or any other ethnic group.

The Ex-militants further called for all genuine allegations concerning PAP to be subjected to transparent investigation and due process, while commending Otuaro’s emphasis on education, professional training, skills acquisition, empowerment and sustainable reintegration.

It urged the Federal Government to allow Otuaro to continue implementing his mandate and to support initiatives that promote long-term peace and economic development.

The group reaffirmed its support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his Renewed Hope Agenda, expressing confidence in the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, and his efforts toward strengthening Nigeria’s national security architecture and maintaining peace and stability in the Niger Delta.

The Forum said the success of the Presidential Amnesty Programme should ultimately be measured by the peace it preserves, lives it transforms, young people it educates and the sustainable future it creates for the Niger Delta, appealing to all stakeholders to place peace above politics and the collective future of the region above ethnic and sectional considerations.

“Following careful consideration of developments within PAP, the Akwa Ibom Ex-Militants Forum hereby passes a resounding Vote of Confidence in Dr. Dennis Brutu Otuaro as the Special Adviser to the President on Niger Delta Affairs; rejects and condemns calls for his removal where such calls are not supported by credible, verifiable and properly established evidence; condemns the use of ethnic sentiment, sectional interests and personal grievances to undermine the leadership of PAP; emphasises that our position is directed at individuals and interest groups and not against the Ijaw ethnic nationality or any other ethnic group; calls for all genuine allegations concerning PAP to be subjected to transparent investigation and due process; commends Dr. Otuaro’s emphasis on education, professional training, skills acquisition, empowerment and sustainable reintegration; urges the Federal Government to allow Dr. Otuaro’s to continue implementing his mandate and to support initiatives that promote long-term peace and economic development.

“The Forum also reaffirms its support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his administration; expresses confidence in the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, and his efforts toward strengthening Nigeria’s national security architecture.

“The Akwa Ibom Ex-Militants Forum believes that the success of the Presidential Amnesty Programme should ultimately be measured by the peace it preserves, lives it transforms, young people it educates, skills it develops and the sustainable future it creates for the Niger Delta. We therefore appeal to all stakeholders to place peace above politics, development above personal interests and the collective future of the Niger Delta above ethnic and sectional considerations. The Niger Delta cannot afford another cycle of instability.

“We call on the Federal Government to retain Dr. Dennis Brutu Otuaro as the Special Adviser to the President on Niger Delta Affairs and provide him with the necessary support to discharge his mandate effectively”, the statement read in parts

World.title: EU Envoy Raises Alarm over 129m Global Out-of-School Girls, 12m Child Marriages Annually
World.content:
* As Dutse school wins NILDS-EU debate, takes home N1m

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Head of the European Union (EU) Delegation to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Ambassador Gautier Mignot, has raised the alarm over the scale of educational exclusion and child marriage worldwide.

He disclosed that approximately 129 million girls remain out of school, while about 12 million are affected by early and forced marriage annually.

Mignot warned that at the current rate of progress, ending child marriage could take 300 years, citing assessments by the United Nations.

He called for targeted investments and interventions to tackle the structural inequalities that expose girls to early marriage and deny them access to education.

The envoy spoke on Monday at the grand finale of the 2026 National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS)-EU inter-secondary school debate held at the NILDS headquarters in Abuja to commemorate the International Day of the Girl Child.

Government Day Secondary School, Dutse, Abuja, emerged overall winner of the competition, securing 89 per cent and taking home the grand prize of N1 million.

The debate, which focused on the motion, ‘Empowering the Girl Child Is More Effective Than Punishing Offenders in Ending Child Marriage,’ brought together four secondary schools to examine the measures required to eliminate the harmful practice.

Government Day Secondary School, Dutse, which argued in favour of punishing offenders, defeated Government Science Secondary School, Maitama; Baptist High School, Kubwa; and Ambassador Global Academy, Kwali.

Government Science Secondary School, Maitama, came second with 76 per cent and received N500,000, while Ambassador Global Academy, Kwali, finished third with N250,000. Baptist High School, Kubwa, came fourth and received N100,000.

Speaking at the event, Mignot said the EU’s Gender Action Plan III was designed to advance gender equality through international partnerships, with at least 85 per cent of EU-funded projects expected to incorporate gender considerations.

According to him, the EU supports programmes addressing gender-based violence, adolescent reproductive health and girls’ education, recognising gender equality as an essential component of societal development.

He described the debate as an opportunity to strengthen advocacy, confidence and leadership skills among young people, particularly girls, while encouraging them to pursue equal opportunities.

The envoy also pledged that the winning team would visit the EU Delegation to learn about its activities and deepen its understanding of the European bloc’s development and gender-equality initiatives.

Meanwhile, the Director-General of NILDS, Prof. Abubakar Sulaiman, called on governments at all levels to increase investment in public education, saying the performances of the students demonstrated the capacity of public schools to produce outstanding academic results despite funding challenges.

He commended the participants for their intelligence, confidence and strong argumentative skills, noting that the competition had demonstrated the intellectual abilities and potential of students from different backgrounds.

“The impressive performances of these students show that public schools are capable of producing outstanding students despite challenges associated with inadequate investment in education.

“The children of the less privileged are gifted, and what we tend to assume is not always the reality,” he said.

Sulaiman said students from public schools had also distinguished themselves in the institute’s quiz competitions over the past 11 years, expressing optimism that sustained investment would help them develop their abilities and compete favourably with their counterparts elsewhere.

He urged governments to provide the necessary resources to strengthen public education and ensure that students from disadvantaged backgrounds had access to opportunities to realise their potential.

The NILDS director-general also stressed the need to empower girls through education, arguing that the country’s future depended significantly on providing women and girls with opportunities to contribute meaningfully to society.

He called on government institutions, private organisations, development partners and the media to support initiatives that promote girls’ education and protect their rights.

Sulaiman specifically urged the media to highlight the achievements of female students and sustain advocacy against harmful practices that undermine their development.

He said NILDS had supported legislative and policy initiatives aimed at addressing female genital mutilation, gender-based violence and early marriage.

According to him, the institute is working with UN Women, civil society organisations, non-governmental organisations and development partners to advance the protection of girls’ rights and promote awareness of policies and legislation designed to improve their welfare.

In her reaction, Grace Onuoha, lead speaker of the winning Government Day Secondary School, Dutse team, expressed delight at the school’s performance.

She pledged to sensitise her classmates and friends of the dangers of child marriage and encourage girls to speak out against abuse.

The competition brought together students from Government Day Secondary School, Dutse; Government Science Secondary School, Maitama; Baptist High School, Kubwa; and Ambassador Global Academy, Kwali, to examine the roles of education, accountability and legal enforcement in ending child marriage.

World.title: 2027: Kwara APC Guber Candidate, Danladi,  Unveils 3-point Agenda
World.content:
* Lists security, citizen empowerment, social welfar Hammed Shittu in Ilorin



The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara State, Hon. Saliu Yakubu Danladi, has unveiled a three-point agenda that will form the thrust of his administration in the first year if given the chance to lead the state in the forthcoming elections.

Danladi, who is the Speaker of the state House of Assembly, listed security, citizen empowerment and social welfare as the three key areas he will prioritize to make life easier for Kwarans.



Danladi made the disclosure in an interview with newsmen in Ilorin, the state capital, on Monday on his programmes for the residents of the state if given the chance to lead the state come 2027.

He said no meaningful development can take place in an atmosphere devoid of peace and adequate security.

“Without peace, it is difficult to bring development to the state,” he said.

He explained that his administration would build on the successes of the incumbent Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq, while intensifying efforts in sectors where more work is still required.

On citizen empowerment, Danladi noted that a society that fails to empower its people will remain stagnant, stressing that productivity of the citizenry is central to the state’s development.

He added that his third priority would be the implementation of people-oriented projects and initiatives centred on social welfare, particularly in education, health and agriculture, which he described as critical drivers of Kwara’s progress.

The APC candidate also disclosed plans to create a conducive environment to attract investors and drive industrialization, with the aim of moving Kwara away from its civil-service-dependent status.

He acknowledged that the narrative has started changing in the last seven years under the present administration and pledged to further boost investment in agriculture and other productive sectors.

Danladi, who became Speaker at the age of 33 and has led the 24-member Assembly for over seven years, said his long and rancour-free leadership of the legislature is proof of his competence and capacity to govern the state.

World.title: Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria to Be Unveiled in Abuja Weekend
World.content:
Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria will be officially unveiled in Abuja this weekend as part of efforts to expand the Nigerian fan base of the current Premier League champions.

According to a press release issued by the club on Monday, arrangements have been concluded for the official launch and unveiling of the group, described as a unique innovation by Nigerian devotees of Arsenal Football Club.

The club’s National President, Mr Charles Ojugbana, said the organisation was drawing inspiration from the exploits of Arsenal players of Nigerian descent, past and present, including Kanu Nwankwo, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze.

The day will end with the formal unveiling of the club at an event expected to be attended by eminent personalities from different walks of life, including captains of industries and popular Nigerian celebrities who support Arsenal Football Club.

Those expected at the event include Dr Bukola Saraki, HRH Emir Sanusi Lamido Sanusi, Senator Dino Melaye and Arsenal legend Kanu Nwankwo.

The statement said Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria operates a governance structure comprising a Board of Trustees, a National Executive Committee (NEC) and a General Assembly of members, which serves as its highest decision-making body.

It added that the club runs a digital membership database to ensure seamless administration and management.

The club also listed the creation of massive awareness for children with Down syndrome as one of its activities for next year. The initiative is designed to coincide with the commemoration of World Down Syndrome Day in March 2027.

World.title: Katsina Scholarship Board Refunds N86m Unclaimed Bursary to State Coffers
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Katsina State Scholarship Board has refunded N86 million unclaimed bursary funds to the state government following the introduction of improved digital verification and accountability measures by the state government.

The Executive Secretary of the Board, Dr. Aminu Salisu Tsauri, disclosed this on Monday during the flag-off of bursary payments for the 2025/2026 academic session by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda at the state-owned Institute of Technology and Management.

He said the recovery of the unclaimed funds was made possible through improved digital verification processes aimed at ensuring that public funds reach only eligible beneficiaries.

He added that the state scholarship board had screened 14,925 new applicants for bursary payments, with disbursement expected before the end of 2026.

He said: “The Katsina State Scholarship Board has returned N86 million unclaimed funds to the state government’s coffers through improved digital verification. 14,925 new applicants have been screened for payment before the end of 2026.”

Flagging off the exercise, Governor Radda said his administration has increased bursary allowances by 100 per cent and commenced the disbursement of N689.79 million to 19,318 verified students across 97 institutions for the 2025/2026 academic session.

He explained that the review ends 18 years of stagnant bursary rates since 2007 and will ease the financial burden on students and parents across the state.

He announced a 150 per cent increase for Veterinary Medicine students in 300 and 400 levels, 200 per cent for those in 500 and 600 levels, and N500,000 each for 56 Katsina indigenes at the Nigerian Law School, totaling N28 million.

On foreign scholarships, Radda said the state is sponsoring 118 students — 41 studying Medicine in Egypt, 10 in Ethiopia, 33 studying Artificial Intelligence and 34 Bioengineering in China — with an upkeep commitment exceeding N1.7 billion, plus tuition, accommodation and health insurance.

He said total bursary payments and student awards by his administration now exceed N3.29 billion, from over N2.6 billion previously disbursed.

Radda also unveiled a new local scholarship scheme for 1,700 students – 50 best performing NECO and WAEC students from each of the 34 LGAs – to study Nursing, Engineering, ICT, Agriculture and Education in state-owned institutions.

He charged the Scholarship Board to sustain transparency, verification and accountability in managing public funds.

World.title: NDC Chairman Alleges Forgery in Plateau Guber Substitution, Demands Police Probe
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The Plateau State Chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Comrade Solomon Ndam, has accused unnamed party actors of forging an Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) substitution document in a bid to unlawfully replace the party’s governorship candidate ahead of the 2027 elections.

Addressing journalists in Jos on Monday, Ndam said he was duly elected the party’s governorship candidate in May 2026 but later withdrew from the race to respect the state’s zoning arrangement to pave the way for a fresh primary.

According to him, Mr. Alfred Ali Dapal emerged as the party’s candidate during a substitution primary conducted on September 15, 2026, and was the only person with whom he executed the required substitution documents.

Ndam alleged that a separate INEC Form EC11B later surfaced bearing his name and photograph but containing a signature he described as forged and unknown to him, allegedly to facilitate the nomination of Jonathan Sunday Akuns.

“I am alive and healthy. The signature on that document is not mine. The only Form EC11B I signed was with Engr. Alfred Dapal,” he said.

The NDC chairman maintained that candidate substitution without the consent of a withdrawing candidate could only occur in the event of death, stressing that no such circumstance existed in his case.

He called on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) and the Plateau State Police Command to investigate the alleged forgery and ensure those responsible are arrested and prosecuted.

Ndam also disclosed that he had briefed his lawyers and was considering a formal petition to the police if no action was taken.

He urged party members across the state to remain calm and continue supporting the NDC, insisting that due process and the rule of law must prevail in resolving the dispute over the party’s governorship ticket.

World.title: Planning a coastal trip? Here’s what Tuesday’s tides look like
World.content:
Tuesday’s high and low tide times for eight coastal locations across South Africa. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities, as spring tides bring changes to water levels along South Africa’s coastline.

However, tides are only part of the picture. Wind, waves and swell and the shape of the seabed can also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual, changing conditions along the coast.



The most recent spring tide coincided with the new moon on Saturday, 10 October. The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing, fishing and other coastal activities. Higher tides can cover rocks and reefs, while lower tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: ‘Orlando Pirates won’t win a trophy’ – Tso makes bold prediction
World.content:
Orlando Pirates legend Benedict ‘Tso’ Vilakazi has cast doubt on his former club’s chances of winning silverware this season following their MTN8 final defeat to Mamelodi Sundowns.

The Buccaneers suffered a 2-0 loss to the Brazilians, who claimed their first MTN8 title in five years.

Pirates enjoyed a successful campaign last season, winning a treble, but their hopes of defending their trophies have already suffered a setback.



With Sundowns showing impressive form, the Soweto giants face a tough challenge in their pursuit of more silverware.

Vilakazi, who has previously praised Abdeslam Ouaddou’s team, believes Pirates will struggle to win trophies this season, particularly if they come up against Sundowns in cup competitions.

“Orlando Pirates won’t win a trophy this season. My reason is I’ve watched Sundowns this season, especially their past two games against the champions of Saudi Arabia (Asia) and against Orlando Pirates in the MTN8 final. I don’t see any team stopping Pirates except for Sundowns,” he said on the Omniaudio Africa podcast.



Tso Vilakazi backs Sundowns to dominate over Orlando Pirates

Vilakazi went further, predicting that Sundowns would have the upper hand if the two teams meet again in a cup final.

“If Pirates play Sundowns, they will lose. I see Sundowns taking everything this season. If they play the way they are playing now, I don’t see anyone stopping them, including Pirates.

“I love Pirates with all of my heart and it is my home, but looking at Sundowns’ performance, they look unstoppable,” he added.



Orlando Pirates will now have to regroup after their MTN8 disappointment as they turn their attention to the remaining competitions.

Meanwhile, Sundowns will look to build on their cup success as they pursue further honours this season.

Will the Buccaneers end the season empty-handed?

World.title: SK Khoza delivers a riveting debut on ‘The Four of Us’ [video]
World.content:
Sthembiso SK Khoza has finally made his highly anticipated debut on e.tv’s The Four of Us, where he delivers a riveting debut as Hitman.

The telenovela, which replaced the long-running soap opera Scandal! in June 2026, is produced by the renowned Tshedza Pictures.

It boasts a star-studded cast including Sindi Dlathu, The Polygamist’s Sdumo Mtshali, Dumisani Dlamini, Thembinkosi Mthembu.



PAPI AND VLADIMIR RECONNECT

On Thursday evening, Papi received an unexpected visit from Vladimir, an old acquaintance flanked by two heavily armed bodyguards.

Vladimir had heard through the grapevine that Papi’s business was struggling, leading him to suggest taking down the “problematic” Hitman by stealing his brand-new bakkies.

However, Vladimir isn’t entirely genuine, as he expects a cut of the car sales, a condition Papi agrees to.

VLADIMIR’S NOT-SO-TRUSTED SPY

Vladimir’s “trusted” inside man within Hitman’s camp, Cobra, tipped him off that the camp recently hijacked a truck carrying new bakkies.

Vladimir then suggests to Papi that they steal the vehicles during the weekend, since Hitman will be at home in Bergville for an ancestral ceremony, which means his warehouse will be left unguarded.

SK KHOZA DELIVERS RIVETING DEBUT

A first look at Hitman already paints a dangerous picture of him. He is seen kicking and punching Cobra after discovering that he is Vladimir’s spy.



“So, you thought I didn’t know that you were Vladimir’s spy? That you’ve been following me around and snitching?” he asks.

Hitman then instructs his ally to contact MaNgwaneni back home and call off the traditional ceremony. Instead of killing Cobra, Hitman decides to use him as bail to get back at Papi and Vladimir.

Believing the warehouse is empty, Papi, Vladimir and their crew walk right into Hitman’s trap. When they realise the bakkies are not there, they immediately suspect there’s a traitor among them.

Thereafter, Hitman and his crew storm in and shoot Cobra, their spy. A deadly shootout soon erupts but comes to a halt when Hitman takes Papi’s brother-in-law hostage.

Confronted by his former protégé, Papi is forced to surrender and drop his gun.

Hitman then asks, “How do you feel right now? Your right-hand man, whom you taught everything, is about to kill you. I’m going to kill you today. How do you feel?”

Hitman then shoots Papi in the chest, but did he die?

World.title: The cheapest two-week beach holiday in South Africa
World.content:
Flights from OR Tambo and accommodation for R400 per person. Image: Wikimedia Commons

South Africans waiting until the last minute to book can still get a family holiday for under R450 per person per night.

If you’re in this group and want to have fun with your family, this is the cheapest two-week beach holiday for a family of four.

The price includes accommodation and flights from OR Tambo.



The Cheapest Destination for 14 Nights

If you want to enjoy a two-week break with your family, you can get 14 nights and flights for a family of four for R24 600 in Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth).

That works out to R439 per person per night, including flights. Without flights, it’s only R245 per person per night.

For flights, you can travel for as little as R10 859 for two adults and two children from OR Tambo International Airport to Port Elizabeth International Airport (PLZ).

The ticket prices include one checked bag per passenger.

But the flight can be cheaper. If you only include checked bags for two passengers and share luggage, the flight drops to R9 939.52.

Typically, the difference between checked luggage and no checked luggage is R230, R460 in total for return flights.



You’ll save R920 if two passengers don’t have checked bags.

Then, once in Gqeberha, travellers can get accommodation starting at R13 732 for 14 nights. This will be self-catering accommodation in a holiday home.

Accommodation in Gqeberha is limited. Many affordable bookings have already been taken.

However, if you can’t book the same accommodation for the full 14 nights, split your accommodation dates.

The cheapest flight departing from OR Tambo to Gqeberha in December is R1026.44. This excludes a checked bag.

For a checked bag, the price climbs to R1 256.44.

Departure Dates With Checked Bags Without Checked Bags 1 December 2026 R1 256.44 R1 026.44 2 – 4 December 2026 R1 357.44 R1 127.44 5 – 9 December 2026 R1 430.44 R1 660.44 29 -31 December 2026 R1 357.44 R1 127.44

The most expensive return flights in December are between 23 and 27 December.

In January, return flights are most expensive until the Sunday before the start of the school term.

Once the school term starts, prices return to normal.

If you return during peak periods, expect to spend up to R14 900 on flights.

But if you travel after school starts, the cost of flights drops by 27%.

Return Dates With Checked Bags Without Checked Bags 14 – 16 December 2026 R1 357.44 R1 127.44 17 -22 December 2026 R1 559.45 R1 329.45 28 – 30 December 2026 R1 733.44 R1 963.44 12 – 15 January 2027 R1 357.44 R1 127.44

Why is Port Elizabeth Cheapest?

The distance between OR Tambo and Gqeberha is roughly double the distance from OR Tambo to King Shaka International.

Despite this, flights to Gqeberha are 22% cheaper than Durban.

That’s because demand to fly from OR Tambo to King Shaka International Airport is higher than demand to fly from OR Tambo to Gqeberha.

The plane is scheduled to fly anyway.

So, to guarantee the plane reaches capacity, airlines offer cheaper seats.

It’s the same reason flights become cheaper when you book them closer to your travel date. Airlines need to fill up seats.

The price also depends on the days you’re travelling.

Flights to Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport drop from their peak by 58% when you travel after Christmas.

The cheapest dates to depart OR Tambo are at the beginning of or the end of December. Then, to depart Gqeberha, it’s cheapest on 14 January 2027.

That’s one day after the first day of term.

World.title: ‘We need R5 000 this time’: Pensioners’ demand sparks debate
World.content:
The call for a R5 000 SASSA Older Persons Grant has opened a wider debate among South Africans about how government could afford it, and who might lose out.

The discussion played out on The South African’s Facebook page, where pensioners, caregivers and critics weighed in.

Pensioners say the time has come

Frans Matsekela made the demand in just five words.



“We need R5 000 this time,” Matsekela wrote.

His use of “this time” suggests a growing impatience among older grant recipients, many of whom feel annual increases have failed to keep up with food, electricity and transport costs.

Thuli Nzimande added that pensioners should not see deductions or reductions of any kind. “Elderly pensioners must get full amount no matter what,” Nzimande wrote.



A R5,000 grant would be more than double the current Older Persons Grant, a major cost given the millions of pensioners SASSA supports each month.

Calls to take from children’s grants

Some commenters had a clear answer on funding. Wade Hendricks suggested limiting support for children to pay for older and disabled South Africans.

“Limit grant to one child and cut the R370 and redirect funds to increase pensioners and disabilities pay,” Hendricks wrote.



Jay Mtungwa went much further, rejecting grants altogether in favour of job creation. “Cancel the whole damn grant thingy, better to put it into employment,” Mtungwa wrote, arguing that adult children should support their elderly parents.

Their views highlight a tension between generations, as pensioners and caregivers compete for limited social spending.

Seniors outside the system

Genover Govender warned that the debate should not ignore older South Africans who receive nothing at all.



“Consider those seniors that are not getting Sassa at all as well,” Govender wrote.

Her comment points to elderly people who fail the means test, are stuck in lengthy application processes, or have never applied. A higher grant would not help them unless they can access the system first.

Economists have long warned that social grants already take up a significant share of the national budget, limiting room for large increases without new revenue or cuts elsewhere.



SASSA has not announced any plan to raise the Older Persons Grant to R5 000. Grant amounts are set during the annual national budget, and pensioners should rely only on official SASSA channels for confirmed increases.

Former police lieutenant-general⁠ Shadrack Sibiya has resigned from SAPS⁠ after disciplinary proceedings began. He faces six criminal charges, including allegations of rape, sexual grooming, human trafficking and negligent handling of a firearm.

There is a development in the murder investigation involving ⁠Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo⁠. A suspect has been arrested in connection with property believed to belong to the 38-year-old, who was murdered in Kempton Park on 12 September. Investigations continue.

⁠Oil prices have fallen,⁠ and many stock markets have risen after ⁠US President Donald Trump⁠ announced what he called an energy⁠ ceasefire⁠ between ⁠Russia and Ukraine⁠. The announcement has not been confirmed by Moscow.

World.title: Zuma’s visibility key to MK Party’s election push - Election analyst
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – The Umkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP) could face a challenge if its leader, Jacob Zuma, remains in hospital and is unable to partake in the campaign trail ahead of the 2026 local elections set for 4 November.

This is the view of election analyst Wayne Sussman, who said Zuma’s visibility will be crucial in the coming weeks to build on the gains it made in the May 2024 elections.

“Umkhonto We Sizwe is on the cusp of achieving something very significant in provinces like KwaZulu-Natal, but if he's not at the helm, if his health continues to deteriorate, that could have a very seismic impact on Umkhonto weSizwe's performance and indeed on the results come the day after this election," he said.

According to Sussman, Zuma is one of the "most charismatic politicians with incredible brand recognition and name recognition and has that ability at a manifesto launch to lift the spirit of his activists".

And while Sussman recognises that Zuma’s son, Duduzane Zuma, holds a senior position in the MKP as the first deputy president, he said it would be worrisome for Zuma not to be visible during this crucial time.

READ | Zuma's hospitalisation raises questions over MK Party's election campaign

Zuma remains in Netcare St Anne’s Hospital in Pietermaritzburg.

The Presidency has confirmed that the surgeon general is overseeing his medical care.

The 84-year-old was admitted last week after the MKP called a routine check-up.

It's unclear if Zuma will attend campaign events, including his party’s manifesto launch in Mbombela on Sunday.

He's also due to appear before the TRC Cases Inquiry next Thursday.

READ |Zuma remains in hospital ahead of MK Party manifesto launch

World.title: 'History not in the side of ANC' - Election expert amid IEC vs ANC ConCourt legal battle
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - An election analyst has pointed out that legal precedent goes against the ANC.

This is as the party is now waiting to see whether a Constitutional Court ruling will allow the submission of 181 candidates after the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) deadline.

According to Wayne Sussman, the National Freedom Party failed to submit its candidate list in the 2016 local government elections; as a result, the IEC did not allow them to run in the elections, seeing them lose an overwhelming number of councillors in KwaZulu-Natal.

“So historical precedent is not on the ANC side and the IEC has been quite categorical about that. Of course, the court has to make its determination and its decision, but history is not on the ANC side,” Sussman added.

The IEC has stuck to its guns in front of the Concourt.

They argue that the ANC never completed the candidate submission process and thus didn't adhere to the deadline.

They also argue that the same system has been in place for the past few elections and ask what would've changed now.

The ANC has argued that the IEC was in possession of their draft list of candidates for six municipalities and that the Submit as Final button was not a legal obligation.

Judgment has been reserved.
