World.title: Discount retailer Boxer announces profits and a new CEO
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Boxer’s growth story continues.

In interim results released on Monday, the discount retailer said Justin Galloway will succeed Marek Masojada.

Boxer has expanded rapidly in recent years, boosting its parent company, Pick n Pay, which retains a large stake.

When Masojada joined in the early 1990s, Boxer had just five stores.

Over 30 years later, he leaves after helping grow the network to 600 stores. Headline earnings per share rose 9.2% in the six months to August.

This growth comes despite lower food prices following a record harvest in South Africa.

READ | Boxer muscles through tough retail environment

Talking to eNCA, Masojada described the journey over the 30-odd years as a privilege to have been part of the growth, working alongside a ‘great team’

“There is a lot of mixed feelings, but what I will say is that the job's not done. I remain in place until the end of our financial year, and obviously we're all going to be working extremely hard to deliver a year-end result after the satisfactory result," he said.

In his conversation with eNCA, Masojada took the time to reflect on the food prices, which were lower than a year ago.

READ | What determines prices? SAHRC probe into SA food system moves to second leg

He said that while having lower prices is great for the consumer, for any retailer having consistent deflation in the market, it does present challenges in terms of getting rand growth through the tills.

But despite that deflation, there is strong promotional activity which many retailers put out into the market to keep themselves and the value proposition active in the consumer’s mind.

World.title: SAPS deems Sibiya’s resignation as a 'dishonourable discharge'
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Shadrack Sibiya's departure from the South African Police Service (SAPS) has been regarded as a dishonourable discharge.

According to police spokesperson Athlenda Mathe, this is because the top cop resigned while facing an ongoing disciplinary case.

His legal team tendered his resignation immediately after his disciplinary proceeding began on Monday.

As such, police confirmed that his employment was terminated with immediate effect on 12 October.

READ | Shadrack Sibiya resigns from SAPS

Sibiya’s resignation brings an end to his employment with the police under a dark cloud.

Sibiya still faces criminal charges before the Randburg Magistrate’s Court relating to rape, trafficking in persons and sexual grooming of a child.

Sibiya was arrested on 21 September for the alleged rape of an 18-year-old and alleged sexual grooming of a 16-year-old.

He has denied the allegations.

He alleges the charges against him are trumped up and says the victims are not vulnerable, nor have they been sexually exploited.

READ | Sibiya admits sex with 18-year-old but calls charges 'trumped up'

Sibiya also faces an additional charge related to a firearm that was allegedly found in his vehicle on 21 September, the day he was arrested.

Separately, testimonies before the Madlanga Commission have implicated Sibiya in corruption and interference with police operations allegations.

These include receiving impalas from alleged crime boss Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matlala, as well as recalling and keeping all active 121 case dockets from the Political Killings Task Team.

Sibiya joined the SAPS on 1 June 1988.

World.title: 'Just the start of the momentum' - Cameron on Sibiya's resignation
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Criminal investigations against disgraced former top cop Shadrack Sibiya are unlikely to come to a halt.

This is the view of the Chairperson of the Portfolio Committee on Police, Ian Cameron, as he reacts to the resignation of the now-former Deputy National Police Commissioner.

According to Cameron, allegations against Sibiya that have emerged both at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry and the Ad Hoc Committee are far-reaching and point to what he calls ‘a desperate need for further criminal investigations'.

“This is just the start of the momentum. The problem with Mr Sibiya is that the can of worms that has been opened around him, and him playing such a central figure kind of role throughout this whole ordeal, makes it very difficult to get away from," he said.

Sibiya resigned while facing an ongoing disciplinary case.

READ | Shadrack Sibiya resigns from SAPS

It was his legal team who tendered his resignation immediately after his disciplinary proceeding began on Monday.

As such, police confirmed that his employment was terminated with immediate effect on 12 October.

READ | SAPS deems Sibiya’s resignation as a 'dishonourable discharge'

Sibiya’s resignation brings an end to his employment with the police under a dark cloud.

With allegations of rape, trafficking in persons and sexual grooming of a child hanging over him, Sibiya has also been clouded by allegations of corruption and interference with police operations.

Cameron said he suspects that Sibiya may have been anticipating an unfavourable outcome from the disciplinary hearing against him.

World.title: State alleges funeral policy claim at heart of four-month-old baby's murder plot
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A so-called pastor and his two wives have appeared before the Atteridgeville Magistrate’s Court on Monday in connection with the murder of a four-month-old baby.

Gauteng National Prosecuting Authority spokesperson Lumka Mahanjana alleges that the three accused had taken out a funeral policy on the child and were planning to claim against the baby's death.

“That was their motive, to kill the victim,” she said.

According to Mahanjana, all three suspects before the court face differing charges.

One of the wives, accused number two, faces charges of conspiracy to commit murder and fraud.

READ | So-called pastor and two wives appear in court over baby's death

The other wife, alongside the pastor, faces similar charges, including premeditated murder, kidnapping, murder, human trafficking and robbery with aggravating circumstances.

The matter will be back in court on 16 October for bail and legal aid.

“You must understand that today the legal aid was not in court, hence why we could not proceed with the matter,” she added.

Police say the man and his two wives accompanied the 43-year-old woman and her baby to the Hennops River in Pretoria last week for a ritual.

The man allegedly went ahead with the woman, leaving the infant in the care of his wives.

READ: Manhunt launched for pastor after baby found dead in Atteridgeville

Police believe the woman was raped before she managed to escape.

The baby’s body was later discovered in a shallow grave near the river.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Kalonzo to Ruto: You have no numbers
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka speaks during launch of economic empowerment equipment distribution at Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos town on October 9, 2026. [John Muia, Standard]

The united opposition will deal President William Ruto a humiliating defeat in next year’s general election, Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka has predicted.

Speaking Friday in his Ukambani backyard during an empowerment equipment handover ceremony hosted by Governor Wavinya Ndeti at the Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos, Kalonzo declared the opposition will defeat Ruto at the ballot ‘no matter what magic he (Ruto) deploys.

“Ruto has been cornered. We have heard him suggesting that they will import foreigners from neighboring countries to vote for him but even so, he will not secure the numbers. We in the united opposition have committed to produce a single candidate that will face Ruto at the ballot,” Kalonzo said.

Recognizing the need to consolidate his lower Eastern vote bloc, Kalonzo rallied the Akamba community to come out in huge numbers to register as voters in the upcoming voter listing initiative by the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC).

“It is the time to redeem this country. The IEBC will as from next month undertake the final leg of voter registration and I urge all eligible voters to apply for national identity cards and register as voters,” he said, vowing he will defeat Ruto in Luo Nyanza.

Kalonzo called out Ruto over what he termed as the president’s habit of making empty promises to Kenyans. “The other day I heard Ruto promising thousands of dams across the country. He should come for benchmarking in Machakos. Retired President Mwai Kibaki and I secured African Development Bank (ADB) funding for the construction of Yatta Dam and now he has ten months left in office. When will he build?” he posed.

Former Attorney General Justin Muturi, who flanked Kalonzo, declared time was fast running out for the opposition to identify and name its presidential flag bearer for the next year’s general election.

The DP party leader, who has gone public declaring his choice of Kalonzo as the presidential ticket bearer for the opposition expressed his frustrations for the opposition’s dillydallying in naming its flag bearer.

“We (the opposition) are tired of singing one song for years that we will produce and name one person to face Ruto. When you see us here another day, do not entertain such kind of talk. Demand that it is Kalonzo for State House,” said Muturi.

During the ceremony, Governor Wavinya Ndeti unveiled assorted empowerment equipment targeting about 6000 beneficiaries across the county.

Addressing residents during the forum, Wavinya jeered at UDA-allied politicians who have been dishing out cash handouts to residents, terming it untenable.

“It is time to demonstrate to those who are approaching our people with cheap hand-outs that when the people of Machakos are given the tools to work, they produce real wealth. My commitment is that I will continue allocating resources to asset-based empowerment until every household in Machakos enjoys economic dignity,” Wavinya said.

World.title: Revealed: 84 Kenyans killed, 52 missing in Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi. [File,Standard]

The government has records of 354 Kenyans linked to the Russia-Ukraine war, including 84 classified as killed or missing in action and five being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine.

Prime Cabinet Secretary and Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi gave the updated figures in a response to Parliament on the recruitment of Kenyans into the Russian military and the detention of Kenyans in Ukraine on Thursday, October 8.

The records show that 77 Kenyans remain on the front lines, 38 are in camps, 52 have an unknown or unclassified location and 34 are hospitalised.

Another 62 Kenyans have been repatriated, while one is in detention and another has completed a military contract.

The government said Russia has stopped the enlistment of additional Kenyans after Kenya secured the country’s placement on Russia’s ‘Stop List’ during Mudavadi’s visit to Moscow in March.

“The Embassy of Kenya in Moscow has since confirmed that no additional Kenyan nationals have been enlisted in the Special Military Operation following the implementation of the Stop List,” Mudavadi said.

Russian authorities have told Kenya that requests to terminate military contracts will be considered on a case-by-case basis by individual military unit commanders.

Mudavadi said Kenya continues to engage Russian authorities and affected families over the burial, cremation or repatriation of remains after Russia said its Defence Ministry could not meet the cost of repatriating the remains of deceased Kenyans.

Five Kenyans held in Ukraine

Five Kenyan nationals are currently being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine, according to information sent to Kenya by the Ukrainian Embassy in Vienna on September 3.

The government identified them as Evans Kibet, detained since May 2025; Willi Muniu Macharia, detained since November 2025; Haron Kibet Pachenge, detained since March 2026; Joseph, detained since April 2026; and Francis Ndarua Ndungu.

Kenya’s Honorary Consul in Ukraine visited the Zakhid 1 prisoner-of-war camp and reported that the detainees were being held in humane conditions, had access to medical services and were being treated under rules governing prisoners of war.

The government also said Ukraine was holding the remains of four other Kenyans.

They are Simon Gitau, Clinton Nyapara Mogesa, Dennis Bagaka Obwori and Eric Mwangi Nyambura.

Kenya is seeking the release and repatriation of the affected Kenyans through diplomatic channels, including engagement with Ukraine and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

The government wants Kenyans held as prisoners of war to be considered as possible victims of international human trafficking.

Mudavadi said many of the affected Kenyans reported that recruiters lured them with promises of employment before they ended up in military service.

The government says the circumstances surrounding their recruitment could fit the definition of trafficking under Article 3(a) of the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, also known as the Palermo Protocol.

It wants the issue considered during negotiations over their repatriation so the Kenyans can access assistance available to trafficking victims.

President William Ruto has also raised the matter directly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a telephone conversation, according to the government.

Kenya has further received approval from Kyiv for its ambassador to Ukraine, with the government saying this will improve its ability to respond to cases involving Kenyans in the country.

The State Department for Diaspora Affairs said families should report cases to the government as soon as communication with relatives in Russia is disrupted.

Once a family reports a case, the department collects identification details, travel information and next-of-kin contacts before referring the case to the Kenyan Embassy in Moscow for verification.

The government has also facilitated the return of 62 Kenyans who had been involved in Russia’s military operations.

It has provided affected families with updates from diplomatic missions, information on compensation processes, psychosocial support and guidance on the repatriation or burial of remains.

The government said it is also expanding measures to prevent deceptive recruitment by providing pre-departure information, urging Kenyans to verify recruitment agencies and employment offers and strengthening emergency assistance through Kenyan diplomatic missions.

The scale of the recruitment first emerged publicly in February when Parliament was told that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been recruited to fight for Russia.

The National Intelligence Service report presented to lawmakers said recruiters targeted former security personnel and civilians with promises of lucrative employment, salaries and bonuses.

The figures at the time included 89 Kenyans on the frontline, 39 hospitalised, 28 missing in action, 35 in camps or bases, 30 repatriated, one detained and one who had completed a contract.

The government then stepped up diplomatic efforts. In March, Kenya announced an agreement with Russia to stop further enlistment of Kenyans into its military operations and to facilitate consular support and voluntary disengagement for Kenyans already serving.

The issue remains unresolved for many families. More than 30 families affected by the recruitment were reported this week to be seeking a meeting with President Ruto before Kenya's delegation travels to Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit, demanding answers on missing relatives, repatriation of survivors and the return of remains.

World.title: Wajir patient isolated over suspected viral haemorrhagic fever
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home. [File, Standard]

A 20-year-old man in Habaswein, Wajir County, has been isolated after presenting with symptoms consistent with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever, following recent travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home, where he is being treated after developing fever, headache and cough. He was also found to have severe anaemia, with a haemoglobin level of 4g/dL.

According to a disease surveillance report filed at Habaswein Police Station, the patient told health officials that he had recently travelled to the DRC, where he worked as a “tan boy” on a cargo truck or trailer.

He reportedly developed fever and headache while still in the DRC on September 2, 2026, before traveling by trailer to Uganda, where he stayed for about five days and sought medical attention.

The report states that he was treated with antibiotics in Uganda before travelling by trailer to Malaba. From Malaba, he travelled by motorcycle to a relative's residence, where he stayed for approximately five days.

He later travelled by trailer to Nairobi and proceeded by bus to Isiolo, where he stayed for about 10 days before travelling to Habaswein by Probox vehicle. He arrived in the town around September 20.

Upon arrival, the patient sought treatment at Hilac Medical Clinic, where he was managed for pneumonia and septicaemia for about three days.

However, his condition did not improve and he was subsequently transferred to Albadar Nursing Home, where he remains admitted.

The report adds that the patient is receiving intravenous Augmentin and paracetamol and has been transfused with two units of whole blood.

“Despite the above interventions, the patient remains clinically unwell and sick-looking,” the report states.

Authorities have since placed the patient in isolation as investigations continue to establish the cause of his illness.

“Sample collection has been completed, and the specimen will be shipped to National Public Health Laboratories tonight,” the report states.

World.title: Complainant letters cannot be used to initiate judge's removal, court rules
World.content:
Chief Justice Martha Koome. [File]

A letter addressed to the Chief Justice seeking administrative intervention cannot form the basis for removing a judge, the Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) has ruled.

Delivering a unanimous judgment in a case filed by Environment and Land Court Judge Anthony Ombwayo, a three-judge ELRC bench comprising Justices Jemimah Keli, Onesmus Makau, and Dr. Jacob Gikeri ruled that a letter written to the Chief Justice cannot simply be forwarded to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and treated as a petition for removal.

World.title: Trump really wants to make ‘super intelligence’ happen. Is it going to happen?
World.content:
Unable to convince Americans to embrace the AI data centers they hate, President Donald Trump is instead exercising the one power he believes is absolute in the presidency: a rebrand.

But unlike Lake America, the Gulf of America, military bases or a mountain, this change is about altering public opinion rather than scoring political points.

Trump first told fellow world leaders at the United Nations last month that “use of the word artificial makes intelligence fake, it makes it sound fake.”

It’s not fake, Trump says; it’s amazing

After Trump signed an executive order in late September, the US government has been changing official documents and websites. Cabinet secretaries and other aides immediately used the new term.

Elon Musk said on X that he would change the name of his company from SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, although that particular change has not yet occurred.

Trump has refused to answer questions that use the old term. He told supporters at a campaign rally in Nebraska that he would henceforth repurpose “artificial” — an “ugly” word, he said — for the news media.

AI is for ‘THE ENEMY’

On Thursday, the president said on social media that anyone who uses the term artificial intelligence instead of super intelligence will be viewed by his White House as “THE ENEMY!”

All of this might feel very much like Trump’s “weave” — the mental meanderings of Trump’s public statements — but it has also been fascinating to watch the infrastructure of the federal government respond to what many Americans might write off as a semantic distinction.

Renaming things is within Trump’s power

There are things that are out of Trump’s power — passing spending bills, renaming the Kennedy Center, ending his war against Iran — but he has shown that presidents have power to change names.

It’s also evidence he knows the unpopularity of data centers and concerns about AI in general at a time when he is a major booster of AI.

Will a rebrand be effective?

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has long pushed to view AI as superintelligence. In August, he published a 6,000-word treatise about how Meta would approach AI. In rose assessments of the future, he referred to the promise of superintelligence. When he referred to AI, it was usually in reference to what he argued were unfounded worries. Zuckerberg said Meta will be committed to an open source model that provides for superintelligent agents working on behalf of every individuals.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Politico’s “Decoded” podcast there are no plans to change the name of his company to OpenSI. But he did say that people in the industry have been using the term superintelligence for a while.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman listens to a speaker at the United Nations Security Council, during a session on artificial intelligence, on September 23. Brendan McDermid/Reuters

It might be a better term, ultimately, than artificial intelligence, but “still sort of understates the magnitude of what I think is happening,” Altman said.

Altman predicted people would still use the term AI and questioned whether Trump’s rebrand would accomplish its goal of changing people’s opinions of AI.

“Does superintelligence sound obviously less scary to people than artificial intelligence?” Altman wondered. Time will tell.

Superintelligence is a separate concept

What is definitely true is that the concept of superintelligence, while it sounds better in Trump’s view, is arguably distinct from AI and should be no less intimidating to Americans.

The term artificial intelligence has its roots in the 1950s, when a group of Dartmouth professors held a summertime conference “on the basis of the conjecture that every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it.”

Superintelligence, at least academically, seems more like the next step of artificial intelligence, or artificial generative intelligence. That happens when the machines learn.

The Oxford philosopher Nick Bostrom has written extensively about superintelligence, including in the 2014 book “Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies.”

Here’s how Bostrum first defined superintelligence in a 1997 essay:

By a “superintelligence” we mean an intellect that is much smarter than the best human brains in practically every field, including scientific creativity, general wisdom and social skills. This definition leaves open how the superintelligence is implemented: it could be a digital computer, an ensemble of networked computers, cultured cortical tissue or what have you. It also leaves open whether the superintelligence is conscious and has subjective experiences.

Asked how he views Trump’s rebrand, Bostrum said that from a technical perspective AI has traditionally “been this wide umbrella term that refers to every form of intelligent information processing in machines.”

We’re talking everything from the Google searches and email spam filters, the current crop of AIs and “hypothetical future more powerful ones.”

“If the idea is to use the new word superintelligence to cover all of that, it’s a little bit of a stretch, maybe, to call my spam filter a superintelligence,” Bostrum told CNN.

In the theoretical evolution of AI, what comes next, he said is AGI, or artificial general intelligence, which refers to a system that has the same kind of learning and reasoning as humans, something Atman says might already have occurred.

“Superintelligence was reserved for this sort of hypothetical future form of artificial intelligence that not only matched but radically exceeded humans across all cognitive domain,” according to Bostrum.

That is exactly the thing that frightens the AI “doomers.” But it is incomprehensible to Trump that the machines could outwit him.

Trump moves to control the narrative

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” Trump wrote in September, arguing against any sort of AI regulation.

President Donald Trump in the Oval Office of the White House on October 7. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images

Bostrum has written both about potential pitfalls of superintelligence as well as the enormous potential to improve and extend human life. But by changing the name, Trump seems to just want to control the narrative.

Bostrum doesn’t necessarily think it’s a bad idea.

“It’s not up to me to decide how English language should be used,” he said. “I mean, it’s good for my book sales, I guess.”

He does see the rhetorical argument for a new term: It’s harder to argue against super intelligence than artificial intelligence.

“If you define superintelligence as we already have superintelligence and it hasn’t caused any catastrophe yet, then what’s the big deal? And you then would need to introduce some new term to refer to this like hypothetical future capability that’s even more powerful.”

Trump knows a thing or two about saying things so much that they take hold in the public. He rarely speaks in public without repeating the same talking points about “fake” news, the “radical left” Democrats, or about how wonderful his own leadership has been, regardless of what the facts are.

At the UN, Trump compared his rebrand to the evolution of “global warming,” which he said was “reborn to climate change because the planet was cooling, not warming, and nobody was dead.”

That’s not exactly what happened, as anyone paying attention to the warming climate in recent years can pretty easily confirm.

World.title: At least 72 Sudanese artisanal miners killed in strike, rights monitor says
World.content:
Reuters — At least 72 artisanal miners were killed in an airstrike in northern Sudan on Saturday, rights monitor Emergency Lawyers ‌said on Sunday, in the second such incident in several months.

Emergency Lawyers blamed the Egyptian air force for the strike, a claim Reuters could not immediately verify. The Egyptian military did not comment on the incident and Egypt’s foreign ⁠ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Images shared on social media and by local rights groups but not verified by Reuters show dozens of bodies strewn in rubble and others wrapped in funeral shrouds, and miners describing an airstrike on the area.

Emergency Lawyers said such a cross-border attack would violate international law.

Northern Sudan has seen an influx of artisanal miners and ‌makeshift ⁠gold mines as the country’s ongoing conflict disrupted other sources of livelihoods and gold became the key cash source for both warring parties. Experts and those in the sector say much of that gold is ⁠smuggled into Egypt.

The war between Sudan’s army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has seen an increased frequency of mass-casualty events, particularly as drone ⁠warfare becomes the primary mode of fighting.

On Friday, some 31 people were killed in a drone strike on a displacement ⁠camp in an army-controlled area of Sudan’s Blue Nile state, one of the war’s frontlines, according to the United Nations.

World.title: Zelensky says Russia has already violated Trump’s surprise energy ceasefire
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia had already violated the surprise energy ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump over the weekend.

Trump announced Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to what he described as an “energy ceasefire,” a development that Zelensky said Kyiv did not know about in advance, and one that Moscow has remained tight-lipped about in the hours since.

“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” Trump said on social media Sunday morning.

Shortly after Trump’s announcement, Russia “launched a targeted strike on a power plant in Kharkiv, causing further damage to our energy system,” Zelensky said. Despite the fresh attacks, the Ukrainian leader vowed to abide by the new agreement, if Russia does too.

“We agree if they agree, and we have already shown that we mean it. Last night, Russian oil refineries were not burning, but at midnight, a Russian jet-powered Shahed struck a gas production facility in Ukraine,” Zelensky said at the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday, where he spoke via video link.

CNN has reached out to the White House for information on how the agreement was reached and what the next steps may be.

When asked about Trump and Zelensky’s comments on Monday, the Kremlin said that “contacts are ongoing,” without providing any further details. “I have nothing to add on this subject,” Kremlin ‌spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

After the announcement, Zelensky wrote on X that he had talked to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte about the news.

“Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side,” Zelensky wrote Sunday. “For our part, Ukraine always FULLY supports steps toward de-escalation, the protection of lives, and the decisions needed to end the war and guarantee lasting peace.”

Trump’s US-Russia diesel deal comes under fire

The announcement comes days after Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin and the two announced a controversial deal to supply markets with Russian diesel fuel.

That deal induced bipartisan blowback, with lawmakers warning that the administration was defying a federal law meant to crack down on Russia after its invasion of Ukraine.

Seven senators, including four Republicans, released a statement over the weekend asking the administration to “reverse course” and strike its plan to supply markets with Russian diesel.

“Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine,” the statement read. “Congress was clear: the U.S. should not import oil from Russia until it ends its aggression against Ukraine and ceases threats against our NATO Allies.”

“President Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the U.S. runs directly counter to that law,” it continued.

Talks with top Ukrainian and US officials, including Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, got underway in Miami as the diesel deal was announced Friday, but Zelensky criticized the diesel news, saying the move would prolong the war.

Trump responded by suggesting Ukraine should “get a new leader who can make a deal.”

Asked about these comments on Monday, Zelensky ruled out fresh elections in Ukraine while the war continues. “From a security standpoint, that’s completely impossible. We have attacks day and night,” he said.

U.S. President Donald Trump speaks to members of the press after landing on October 10 at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland. Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images

It was not immediately clear what led to the Sunday announcement. In an interview earlier on Sunday, Zelensky also called for a ceasefire.

“OK, if they want energy ceasefire, we are open for this,” Zelensky said about Russia during an interview with ABC News. “Don’t attack us. Don’t kill our children. We will stop attacking your diesel. And I think it’s fair, fair deal.”

Energy infrastructure has been one of the key targets of Russian attacks since the first months of the full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukraine later began targeting Russian oil refining facilities using domestically made drones to strike deep inside Russia. In recent months, both sides have escalated the aerial war as front lines remain largely stagnant.

Trump has expressed frustration about Ukraine’s attacks on Russian energy sites. But there have still been several in the past week, with Kyiv viewing them as an essential part of the Kremlin’s war machine.

Ukraine seeking further clarity

Zelensky said Sunday that Russia continued to strike Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, including a power plant in Kyiv and energy facilities in the Kharkiv region.

“And all of this happened AFTER the President of the United States made his statement about an energy ceasefire,” he posted on X.

The Ukrainian leader repeated that assertion on Monday, saying “there were Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump.”

“It is clear that Putin does not read Truth Social,” he added.

A source close to Zelensky told CNN that Ukraine was not attacking Russian oil refineries while it waits for further clarity about the ceasefire from the US side.

This story has been updated with additional information.

Correction: This story has been updated to reflect that Mark Carney is the Prime Minister of Canada.

World.title: After oil increasingly left the Gulf, Iran is trying to regain its stranglehold on shipping
World.content:
Iran is stepping up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf in an effort to restore its leverage over the critical waterway.

There have been more than a dozen strikes on shipping since the end of September, reducing the volume of oil transiting the strait and keeping crude prices above $100 a barrel.

US President Donald Trump announced Thursday that he has no plans to strike Iran before the midterm elections, where rising energy costs could play a part in his Republican Party losing the House of Representatives, the Senate – or both.

“We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd,” Trump declared on Truth Social, adding that the administration is “having productive discussions” with Tehran and that his main goal is to ensure the country does not obtain a nuclear weapon.

Tehran, however, is focused on Hormuz as a “strategic red line” and is broadening its range of targets in the Gulf.

Leverage over Hormuz is non-negotiable for Tehran as it weathers US pressure despite a sinking economy. But Washington has said that the principle of free navigation in international waters is inviolable, a stance echoed by Gulf states that rely on the strait for much of their trade.

In one of the latest incidents, the National Guard of the United Arab Emirates said Saturday it had rescued 22 people following an oil tanker fire. Those rescued were Indian citizens – India is one of the largest suppliers of seafarers.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) – which tracks shipping incidents – has reported several other attacks in recent days.

It said the master of an outbound tanker reported it was struck Saturday by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire on board. UKMTO reported another attack in the same area on Sunday, resulting in damage to the vessel. All crew members were reported safe.

An Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps serviceman salutes in front of an Iranian national flag. Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Getty Images

The navy of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) claimed on Saturday that a supertanker carrying crude oil suffered a massive explosion after striking a naval mine while attempting to leave the Strait of Hormuz through a route Tehran hadn’t authorized.

“No extra-regional power has the right to threaten, maintain a domineering presence, or interfere in it. The Strait of Hormuz is Iran’s strategic red line,” said the head of the IRGC, Ahmed Vahidi, in a post on X.

UKMTO said Sunday it had also received a report from several ships in UAE waters that they had been directed via VHF radio messages to move from their anchorages. Iran has avoided targeting the UAE recently.

Shipping analysts Ambrey said the IRGC Navy had issued a warning to six vessels anchored around 16 miles (25 kilometers) from the port of Ras al Khaimah in the UAE.

“The vessels were advised to heave up anchor, exit the area immediately, and transit to Dubai anchorage,” Ambrey noted.

Analysts say the rise in Iranian attacks and threats is in response to higher volumes of oil and petroleum products through the strait. They averaged about 13.1 million barrels per day at the end of September, according to Kpler, a marine data tracking service.

That’s just under 80% of the 17.1 million barrels that had traveled through the strait each day before the war broke out.

But flows appear to have slowed this month. Just seven tankers transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, less than half the seven-day average and the lowest number since July 23, data from Kpler showed.

However, figures are at times revised higher after ships have moved through the strait, as many switch off their identification systems to try to avoid detection.

The US military continues to enforce a blockade on Iranian ports, as part of a strategy of maintaining economic pressure on Iran.

On Saturday it had disabled a cargo vessel in the Gulf of ⁠Oman after the ship’s crew ignored warnings and ⁠attempted to run the ongoing naval blockade against Iran.

“A U.S. military ‌fighter ⁠jet struck the stern of Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (also known as the “Arika Sun”) with a precision ‌munition, fully disabling the ship’s propulsion without harming ⁠the crew,” US Central Command posted on X.

The US blockade has been highly effective, according to analysts. September was the first month that Iran loaded no crude onto tankers since maritime data tracking service Kpler began monitoring Iranian exports in 2013.

Last week, Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, described the current economic situation as one of the most difficult periods the country has faced.

Tehran has insisted that if it can’t export its oil, its neighbors won’t be able to either. It believes it holds the initiative, given US shortages of air defense interceptors, and says its military posture has moved towards the offensive.

“Both the Americans and other countries should know: As we have said before, in a region where we cannot sell oil, no one else will be able to sell oil either. And if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will be safe,” Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, said late in September.

It now seems intent on turning that threat into reality.

World.title: PM: Top priority given to food, water security ahead of “Egypt Forum 2026”
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly on Sunday, October 11, 2026, said that food and water security are top priorities for Egypt, describing them as fundamental pillars for meeting citizens’ basic needs and achieving comprehensive and sustainable development.

Madbouly said a session entitled “Food and Water Security: Today’s Challenges and Future Safeguards” at Egypt Forum 2026 would examine current challenges and the government’s unprecedented efforts to increase self-sufficiency, narrow the import gap and maximize the use of available resources.

He made the remarks during a meeting on Sunday to review preparations for Egypt Forum 2026, in line with directives of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

The meeting focused on the main themes of the session and was attended by Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation Hany Sewilam, Minister of Supply and Internal Trade Sherif Farouk, Minister of Agriculture and Land Reclamation Alaa Farouk, Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority Secretary-General Khaled Salah, and a host of officials.

During the meeting, Madbouly said a comprehensive review was under way of all the forum’s sessions as preparations continued for the event, scheduled to run between October 19-24. The forum, directed by President al-Sisi, aims to showcase Egypt’s comprehensive development pathways and the progress achieved across various sectors in recent years.

The meeting reviewed the session’s main themes, including the challenges facing food and water security, particularly pressures arising from population growth, climate change, limited water resources, fluctuations in global markets and disruptions to international supply chains.

It also highlighted the efforts made by state institutions to address these challenges, with particular emphasis on the central role of the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority and relevant ministries in leading horizontal and vertical agricultural expansion projects, securing strategic crops, and developing the infrastructure and logistics supporting food supply chains.

These efforts aim to strengthen the resilience of the national economy and its ability to adapt to international developments, the meeting heard.

Participants stressed the importance of adopting an open and transparent approach throughout the forum’s sessions and workshops, directly addressing citizens’ concerns and public questions with documented figures and facts.

The approach is intended to strengthen public participation and ensure that citizens have a full understanding of the challenges facing the country and the efforts being made to address them, recognizing them as active partners in Egypt’s development process.

The forum aims to present the progress achieved on the ground, provide an objective assessment of the implementation of state projects, and establish clear, sustainable guarantees and action plans to safeguard national resources and secure citizens’ basic needs.

World.title: PM reviews Digital Egypt plans ahead of Egypt Forum 2026
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reviewed plans to expand digital government services and upgrade telecommunications infrastructure during a meeting on Sunday, October 11, 2026, to prepare for Egypt Forum 2026.

During the talks, they reviewed the forum’s Digital Egypt session, which will examine progress in digital transformation and the remaining challenges.

The forum will take place from October 19 to 24 in the New Capital at the direction of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

For his part, Madbouly called for continued investment in telecommunications infrastructure and better integration of government digital systems, particularly amid the growing use of artificial intelligence.

He said that the government aims to improve services for citizens and investors, protect digital data and ensure that online services remain affordable and accessible.

The meeting, attended by Communications and Information Technology Minister Raafat Hindi and Justice Minister Mahmoud Helmy al-Sherif, also discussed expanding services on the Digital Egypt platform.

Officials reviewed efforts to digitize civil registry and real estate registration services, simplify procedures and reduce transaction times.

The Digital Egypt session will also examine how digital transformation supports the economy, including the outsourcing industry’s contribution to exports and job creation.

World.title: Egypt, Belgium discuss expanding scientific research cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research Abdelaziz Konsowa discussed expanding cooperation with Belgium in scientific research and innovation, particularly in applying research findings to industry.

Konsowa, who also serves as acting minister of culture, held talks with representatives of the Belgian Federal Science Policy Office (BELSPO) during a visit to Belgium.

The meeting was attended by Egypt’s Ambassador to Belgium and the European Union Ahmed Abu Zeid, and Egypt’s Cultural Attaché in France Chahinda Ezzat.

Konsowa stressed the need to connect scientific research with industrial and economic needs, turning research findings into practical applications and technological solutions.

During the talks, they also reviewed possible partnerships between universities, research centers, and industrial companies to encourage innovation, support technology transfer, and strengthen cooperation between researchers and businesses.

The meeting is part of Egypt’s efforts to expand international research partnerships and increase the use of scientific research in industrial and economic development.

World.title: PM reviews impact of urban development projects ahead of Egypt Forum 2026
World.content:
The government will use sessions at the Egypt Forum 2026 to present accurate data, address public concerns and answer citizens’ questions, while setting out clear priorities and timelines for the next phase of development, the Cabinet said Sunday.

The announcement came during a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly to review the main topics of a forum session on “Sustainable Urban Development and Its Impact on Improving Citizens’ Quality of Life.”

The forum is scheduled to take place in the New Capital from Oct. 19 to 24.

The meeting was attended by Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad, Minister of Housing, Utilities and Urban Communities Randa al-Menshawy, Deputy Minister of Transport for Railways and Electric Traction Wagdi Radwan, Deputy Minister of Housing for Utilities Ahmed Omran, Assistant Head of the Armed Forces Engineering Authority Ahmed Zaki, and other concerned officials.

Madbouly said the session would review development in unsafe and unplanned areas, the construction of new cities, road and transport projects, infrastructure initiatives, and the presidential “Decent Life” initiative to develop Egyptian rural villages.

“What matters to us in this session is examining the impact of all these projects on citizens’ lives,” Madbouly said, adding that the discussion would address public concerns, challenges facing the sector, the state’s development targets for the coming period, and implementation timelines for strengthening urban infrastructure.

The government reaffirmed that the forum’s sessions would be based on accurate facts and data, with an emphasis on transparency and open discussion.

It said citizens would be treated as active partners in understanding current challenges and development efforts and in shaping a roadmap for the next phase, supported by clear objectives and specific timelines.

World.title: Liberia: Investigators Find No Link Between Liberia’s US$19M and US$317M Cocaine Busts
World.content:
MONROVIA – For four months, Liberians have treated this year’s two great cocaine seizures as one story. The airport bust came first, the record haul followed six weeks later, and officials spoke of a single network that had burrowed into the state for more than six years.

By Rodney D. Sieh

Investigators now say that picture is wrong.



“We haven’t identified yet any connection between 19M and 317M,” investigators told FrontPageAfrica this week. “Leroy Harris doesn’t have connections to [the] 317M [case].”

If that holds, Liberia is not fighting one cartel. It is fighting two, with different suppliers, different routes, different customers and different methods. It also helps explain one of the stranger features of the State’s case: the disappearance of George Wah “Leroy” Harris, the Paynesville bar owner the government publicly charged in the US$317 million probe in August, from the indictment that followed.

It does not explain everything. A close reading of both indictments shows threads that still run between the two cases, and questions the Ministry of Justice has yet to answer.

Case one: the airport pipeline

The first case broke on June 8 at Roberts International Airport (RIA). Screeners flagged six cargo boxes declared as Maggi cubes and lappas. Inside were 198 compressed plates of cocaine, 237.6 kilograms in all, valued at about US$19.2 million.

The shipment was going out, not coming in. According to the indictment, a logistics manager arranged for the boxes to fly Brussels Airlines to London Heathrow, consigned to Usman Ali at an address in Birmingham, England. Prosecutors say a similar four-box consignment, also declared as Maggi cubes and lappas, left on May 20 for US$1,400 in fees.

This is the network investigators describe as running Sierra Leone–Liberia–United Kingdom/Netherlands. FPA sources now tie it to Jos Leijdekkers, the Dutch fugitive whom authorities believe has been sheltering in Sierra Leone. A senior security official had earlier linked Leijdekkers to Liberia’s drug trade in general terms; investigators now place him with the airport pipeline specifically. Leijdekkers has not been charged in Liberia.

A Montserrado County grand jury indicted 10 defendants in the August Term of Criminal Court “C”: Harris; Paul Jamaal King; Philip Yeoh Jr.; Mohammed O. Gbowrah; former LDEA airport deputy commander Moses Jallah; Michael U.S. Brown, alias Rahim Bah; Polo Bah; Oscar J. Brown; Usman Ali; and an unidentified “private bar” entity or person.

Harris sits at the centre of the bribery allegations. Prosecutors say that after the seizure he offered LDEA agents US$100,000 to return the boxes, handed US$5,000 to Jallah at Private Bar, offered a warehouse in Sayon Town for storage, and told Jallah he owned a quarter of the drugs. Harris is in Monrovia Central Prison and is presumed innocent.

Case two: the sea route

The second case is a different animal. On July 21, a joint security team raided a compound on Cement Road in the VOA Community, off the RIA Highway. They found 3,971 plates of cocaine in 157 bags, which the State values at US$317.68 million.

Two foreigners were arrested on the spot: Johann David Garces Grajales, who holds Spanish and Colombian passports, and Srdan Seles, a Serbian. A third man, known only as Tom, allegedly slipped away before the raid.

This cocaine came in by sea. Prosecutors say it was landed from the Atlantic in May, carried by canoe up the Po River at Royesville through ground the group had secured in Bomi County, then trucked to the VOA house. The cover was a fishing business on the riverbank and a front airline, Afri-Connect Airlines, whose aircraft was bought in August 2025 and flew into Spriggs Payne.

Investigators describe this pipeline as Colombia–Brazil–Liberia–Ghana–Eastern Europe (Serbia, Croatia, Ukraine)–Dubai. The 55-page indictment, issued with an October 7 writ, names Nikola Ivancic as the cartel’s paymaster and puts the network’s political recruitment in a Dubai meeting.

Its reach is far wider than case one. The defendants include former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor, former NSA deputy director Gerald Folley Smith, former airport operations chief Mark Kuiah, and a string of security officers. The charges run to 11 counts, including money laundering and weapons offences.

Where the two cases part

The differences are not cosmetic. They go to how each network made money.

* Direction. Case one was an export: cocaine already in Liberia leaving by air for Britain. Case two was an import and storage operation: a mother shipment landed by sea and held near the airport road.

* Scale. The VOA haul is nearly 17 times heavier and about 16 times more valuable than the airport seizure.

* Method. The airport network used ordinary commercial airfreight, false cargo declarations and small cash payments to handlers. The sea network bought land, boats, a plane and, prosecutors say, protection at the highest levels.

* People. Case one’s defendants are mostly Liberian logistics workers, airport hands and a UK consignee. Case two is run by foreign operators with Latin American and Balkan links, allegedly shielded by senior Liberian officials.

* Markets. One route ends in Britain and the Netherlands; the other fans out to Eastern Europe and the Gulf.

On that reading, the State’s treatment of Harris makes some sense. His alleged conduct — the US$100,000 offer, the US$5,000 payment, the claim to a quarter share — concerns the airport boxes. Prosecutors may simply have charged him where their evidence lies.

The Harris gap

But the record does not move in a straight line.

In early August, the Ministry of Information announced that Harris had been charged in the US$317 million probe. Security forces sealed Private Bar and searched it three times; management says nothing illegal was found. Harris was arraigned at the Monrovia City Court. Police said at the time that he had called security officials in the hours after the seizure to try to free the shipment.

On August 27, Criminal Court “C” issued its writ in the airport case, naming Harris. On October 7, the US$317 million indictment arrived. Harris is not in its caption, its counts or its narrative.

No one has told the public whether the August charge was withdrawn, merged into the airport case, or left pending.

That matters for a man in pre-trial detention: he is entitled to know which case is holding him.

The threads that remain

Investigators may be right that the two networks are distinct. Yet the 317M indictment itself keeps brushing against the smaller case.

Private Bar appears in both. The new indictment places the cartel’s introductory meeting for its front airline at Private Bar in Paynesville — Harris’s venue — while charging no one over it. Witnesses separately told FPA that Usman Ali, the airport case’s UK consignee, attended a birthday party for Harris and Michael Browne at the same bar on May 17.

The “19” in the voice notes. Among the State’s evidence against Howard-Taylor are WhatsApp exchanges with co-defendant Sheik Bashiru Kante. In them, prosecutors attribute to Kante references to “the 19 kilos” and “19 million.” If those words point to the airport seizure, the larger case’s own evidence invokes the smaller one.

The airport in the middle. Both cases run through RIA. The June boxes were caught there. The sea cartel allegedly paid Kuiah, then RIA’s operations chief, US$50,000 to smooth its path. Kuiah is named in the big indictment, though no count lists him, and he was dismissed after the airport seizure.

Leijdekkers and Sierra Leone. If the Dutch fugitive stands behind the airport pipeline, has Liberia asked Freetown and The Hague for help? The Inspector General promised in July to pursue suspects abroad through extradition and mutual legal assistance. The public has seen no request.

The 2022 shadow

Liberia has been here before. In 2022, a jury acquitted all four defendants in the US$100 million Freeport case, then the country’s largest, and all four left the country within a day.

Two indictments now stand where one case once seemed to. Whether they are two cartels or two halves of one is a question for evidence, not press briefings. But a prosecution that cannot say clearly who belongs in which case will hand defence lawyers their opening — and risk repeating 2022.

All defendants named in this report are presumed innocent unless proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: Liberia: What Judge Ousman Feika’s Ruling Against Attorney Gbawou Kowou Does, and What It Leaves Unanswered
World.content:
MONROVIA – Judge Ousman F. Feika of Criminal Court “C” did not suspend Atty. Gbawou Kowou’s law license. That distinction matters.

By Rodney D. Sieh

In a ruling dated October 9, Judge Feika dismissed a complaint in which Kowou accused the State’s prosecutors of tampering with defense witnesses. He then referred Kowou to the Supreme Court’s Grievance and Ethics Committee, “with a strong recommendation that his law license be suspended for one calendar year for unethical and unprofessional conduct unbefitting of a lawyer.”



Kowou remains a licensed lawyer. Whether he stays one is now a question for the Committee and, ultimately, the full bench of the Supreme Court.

How it started

The dispute grows out of the economic sabotage prosecution of former officials including Varney Sirleaf and Dee Maxwell Saah Kemayah. The case is brought by the Assets Recovery and Property Retrieval Task Force (AREPT), chaired by Cllr. Edwin K. Martin. Kowou represents co-defendant Wayfa Ciafa.

On Sunday, October 4, members of the Group of 77 went to AREPT’s offices. Some of them had already testified for the defense. That night, Kowou went live on Facebook and called in to the Spoon Talk Show. He alleged that AREPT had summoned his witnesses to intimidate them into recanting.

The next day he filed a Bill of Information asking the court to investigate. The court halted the trial, sent the jury back to quarters and opened an inquiry that afternoon.

What the court found

The ruling rejects Kowou’s account on almost every point:

• Why the witnesses went. The witnesses went at the instance of Raymond K. Zarby, the Group’s senior administrator. Zarby testified that he misread AREPT’s invitation, which was meant for rebuttal witnesses.

• What happened when they arrived. AREPT asked them to leave once it realized some had already testified for the defense. Witnesses for both sides said no one was threatened, though their phones were taken at the door. AREPT described that as routine for all visitors.

• Kowou’s prior knowledge. Kowou knew of the visit in advance. A witness had called him, and he advised them to go. That undercut his claim that they went without his knowledge.

• Martin’s whereabouts. Martin was not on the premises. Kowou had testified that Martin ordered him beaten and dragged out.

• The scuffle. The video showed a scuffle that began when AREPT staff tried to stop Kowou from filming and live-streaming inside the compound.

The court called the tampering allegation “absolutely false and misleading.”

The real charge: going public

The ruling says plainly that raising witness tampering is not misconduct. Counsel who has credible information, the court said, “should promptly bring the matter before the Court.”

The court’s objection is to the order of events: the Facebook live stream and the talk show came first, and the formal filing came after. It also points to a gag order issued at the start of the trial, barring lawyers from discussing the case with the media.

The judge found that Kowou breached Rules 1, 18, 20 and 22 of the Code of Moral and Professional Ethics. Those rules cover:

• Rule 1: undermining the courts

• Rule 20: publicity about pending litigation

• Rule 22: asserting unproven matters as fact

“Criticism of a judicial decision and denigration of the judicial institution are not synonymous,” the ruling says.

Where the ruling is on firm ground

On procedure, Judge Feika did what the law asks. Article 75 of the Constitution gives the Supreme Court authority over the legal profession. The Judiciary Law gives it the power to censure, suspend, or remove lawyers. Judicial Canon 21, which the ruling cites, tells trial judges to correct unprofessional conduct and, where necessary, refer it to the Grievance and Ethics Committee.

A trial judge who believes a lawyer has misbehaved before him is expected to make that referral. Feika did.

The questions it leaves open

The ruling still raises issues the Committee and the public will weigh.

Proportionality. A one-year suspension is a severe penalty. It would take Kowou out of every case he handles, not just this one. The conduct the ruling describes is publicity during a gag order and an allegation the court found unproven. Breach of a court’s own gag order is ordinarily a matter for contempt, and the ruling does not say why the court went straight to recommending a year off the roll.

Who judged the complaint? Kowou’s complaint was against the prosecuting party in a case the same court is trying. Courts routinely rule on such Bills of Information. Still, when a defense complaint against the prosecution is dismissed, and the complaining lawyer is then recommended for suspension, it raises a concern. Other defense lawyers may hesitate before raising similar complaints.

The “extreme circumstances” exception. By the ruling’s own account, Rule 20 allows that extreme circumstances may justify a public statement. Kowou will likely argue that a lawyer who believes his witnesses are being pressured faces exactly such circumstances. The court found the belief unfounded. The Committee will decide whether that makes the conduct sanctionable.

Where the ruling and Kowou agree. The ruling confirms that the witnesses’ phones were taken at AREPT’s door. It also confirms that AREPT staff physically tried to stop Kowou from filming. Neither amounts to tampering, but both help explain why a defense lawyer might have feared the worst.

What comes next

The Grievance and Ethics Committee must now conduct its own investigation, with Kowou entitled to be heard. Its recommendation then goes to the full bench of the Supreme Court. Judge Feika’s recommendation does not bind the Committee, and the Supreme Court is not bound by the Committee’s.

Kowou is also on the defense team for former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor in a separate case before the same court. How the Supreme Court handles his referral will be watched closely by lawyers on both sides of Liberia’s most politically charged prosecutions.
