World.title: Why Do Croatian Motorways Cost So Much When There are Constant Disruptions?
World.content:
October the 11th, 2026 – Croatian motorways cost a lot to use, but why is this the case when there are constant road works and extensive disruptions?

Drivers in Croatia pay the full price of tolls even on motorway sections where, due to road works, traffic is slowed, doesn’t flow, is full of bottlenecks, closed traffic lanes and speed restrictions. It’s very clear that such conditions can prolong the journey, but the price of the toll remains the same. Index’s text problematised the introduction of an expensive and complex toll collection system instead of simpler vignettes, such as those used by neighbouring Slovenia. It also warned about the very high costs of using Croatian motorways, opening the question precisely opened of why drivers need to pay the full fees even when, due to works, they cannot use the motorway under normal conditions.

Vedran Salvia reports that anyone who regularly uses Croatian motorways knows very well how frequent the works are, because of which queues form that prolong the journey itself. On individual sections, these burdensome works last for many months. For example, on the A3 motorway between Nova Gradiška and Lužani, works on doing up the carriageway have been ongoing since September, with completion scheduled for mid-November. On the A1 motorway between Gornja Ploča and Sveti Rok, the rehabilitation of two bridges began at the beginning of October and is due to last until the beginning of December. In both cases traffic on part of the motorway is two-way on one carriageway. Those are only some of the works currently being carried out on Croatian motorways.

hac remains silent

According to the applicable Toll Collection Act, the possibility of granting discounts exists, but the regulations do not provide for a reduction in price due to works or difficult driving conditions. Neither do HAC’s General Terms of Use of the motorway and toll collection provide for a special refund of money in cases when, due to works, traffic takes place on a narrowed carriageway or with speed restrictions. HAC was asked for additional clarification on whether there is a legal possibility of reducing the toll during works and under what conditions such a discount could be introduced.

In addition to asking HAC for a legal clarification of that possibility, they were also asked whether they have ever considered introducing temporary discounts. We also requested data on the scope of works and the total kilometrage of motorways affected by bottlenecks and the closing of traffic lanes during 2025 and 2026. By the time the text was closed we had not received an answer.

croatia charges enormous tolls

The question of charging the full toll during works gains particular importance when the high prices of using Croatian motorways are taken into account. Drivers for non-small amounts expect corresponding quality of service, which also opens the broader question of the relationship between the price and what they receive in return. The toll Zagreb – Split for a passenger car amounts to 26.40 euros in one direction, or 52.80 euros for a return trip. Even with the ENC discount of 21.74 percent, three return trips cost around 124 euros. As a counter-argument, it could be said that the toll is paid according to the kilometres travelled, and not according to the time spent on the motorway, so road works should not affect the price. But that does not mean that it is all the same under what conditions one drives. One takes the motorway precisely in order to travel faster and with fewer delays. In Croatia, however, works and bottlenecks are very frequent, so it isn’t remotely unreasonable that drivers expect normal driving conditions when paying such sums.

slovenia smartly extends the validity of vignettes during such works

That it is perfectly possible to compensate drivers for difficult driving conditions is also shown by the example of neighbouring Slovenia. The Slovenian parliament in November last year adopted a law by which, due to numerous works and reduced motorway throughput, it extended the validity of annual electronic vignettes by four months, without additional costs. The measure applied to all annual vignettes that were valid on the 1st of December 2025, and the extension was carried out automatically. The Slovenian Ministry of Infrastructure explained that the aim of the measure was a fairer relationship towards drivers who, due to works, suffered worse travel conditions on the roads.

additional road users could be attracted by lower fees

However, does that mean that they should not pay the full price of the toll? Marko Ševrović, associate professor and vice-dean of the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences in Zagreb, told Index that he understands drivers’ dissatisfaction, but warns that the problem must also be viewed from the perspective of traffic planning. “I understand that users look from their perspective and ask themselves why they pay the full price when the driving conditions are worse. But imagine that on a section we already have a jam due to reduced capacity and then we also lower the price. What will we achieve by that?

I believe that a reduction of the toll during works would be unusual, but also counterproductive. A lower price could attract additional traffic precisely to the sections on which traffic capacities are already reduced due to works. The goal in such situations should be to reduce traffic on those sections, and not to further encourage it. If there is an alternative road, it would make more sense to reduce the price of its use and thus encourage drivers to avoid the section on which works are being carried out,” our interlocutor believes.

road works go on for much too long in croatia

He emphasises that the problem is that the works last too long in Croatia, and become a constant source of irritation to all road users as a result.

“That’s partly a consequence of the situation in the construction sector. Contractors do not have enough workers, the costs of labour and materials have risen significantly, so savings are made on the number of employees and work shifts. The works could be completed significantly faster, but that is the current situation. We have a public procurement system that in practice favours the lowest price. In doing so, it is not calculated how much society loses due to long-lasting works. Because of such an approach deadlines are often exceeded and the works drag on. That is not only a problem of HAC, but also of state roads and city thoroughfares, which we also see in Zagreb,” he says.

neighbouring italy also does things differently

That it’s possible to regulate toll collection during works differently is also shown by the example of neighbouring Italy, which, similarly to Croatia, charges tolls according to the distance travelled. There drivers on the network of the largest Italian concessionaire Autostrade per l’Italia and related companies can obtain a partial or full refund of money if works significantly impede or prolong their journey. Such a system has existed for several years, and from June this year new rules are applied that have expanded drivers’ rights, as also reported by the Italian news agency ANSA.

An interesting example also comes from Spain, where courts sided with drivers over the charging of the full toll during works on a motorway in Galicia. The Supreme Court in 2025 ruled that charging the full amount during major delays was an unfair practice, thereby opening the way for a refund of money to the affected drivers.

In a separate procedure, about which the local newspaper La Voz de Galicia wrote, the court recognised a group of 21 plaintiffs, mostly craftsmen and local carriers, the right to a refund of half of the paid toll amount due to significantly worse driving conditions. The same question that was raised was also opened back in 2023 in the French Senate, where it was problematised why drivers pay the full toll when works prolong the journey and reduce the quality of service. The French Government replied that the prices are determined by concession contracts and that their reduction would require legislative changes or changes to the contracts, with possible financial compensation to the concessionaires. It also warned that such costs could be compensated by a later increase in tolls.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia discuss energy cooperation as electricity and oil ministers meet in Riyadh
World.content:
Riyadh (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Oil Minister, Basim Mohammed Khudair, and Iraq’s Electricity Minister, Ali Saadi Waheeb, met with Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman in Riyadh to discuss extending bilateral energy cooperation and boosting coordination between the two nations.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of the 25th WPC Energy Congress, sponsored by Saudi Arabia and attended by energy ministers, industry executives, and representatives from major international energy firms.

According to Waheeb, the talks focused on ways to increase energy cooperation and create tighter coordination in accordance with Iraq and Saudi Arabia’s interests.

The Iraqi electrical minister emphasized Baghdad’s desire to continue discussions with Riyadh and expand areas of collaboration, particularly in ways that could help improve the stability of Iraq’s power system.

The meetings brought together Iraq’s two senior energy ministers and their Saudi counterparts at a time when regional energy security, infrastructure investment, and dependable power supply are still top considerations.

Iraq has been attempting to modernize its electrical infrastructure, diversify energy suppliers, and establish regional alliances in response to local power constraints and rising demand.

The Riyadh meeting was part of a larger series of engagements by Iraqi energy officials at the congress, which included talks with neighboring countries about electrical interconnections, technical cooperation, and investment prospects.

Additionally, the high-level meeting came after a separate high-level energy meeting in Baghdad on Saturday, when Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi welcomed TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanné and ConocoPhillips CEO Andy O’Brien, along with their teams.

The talks in Baghdad centered on investment in oil production and related gas at Basra’s Bin Umar oilfield, including deadlines for raising output and chances to extend production in adjacent locations.

World.title: Tom Barrack meets Iraq’s top judge Faiq Zaidan in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US Envoy Tom Barrack met with Iraq’s top judicial leadership in Baghdad on Monday, as Washington and Baghdad strive to rebuild their bilateral relationship in the face of regional tensions and a shifting security situation.

Barrack met with Judge Faiq Zaidan, President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, to explore ways to strengthen bilateral legal and judicial collaboration.

The meeting comes at a difficult time for the region, after fatal assaults on Riyadh’s international airport over the weekend, which Saudi officials blamed on Yemen’s Houthi movement.

In a statement issued after the negotiations, Barrack praised his meeting with Zaidan as positive and emphasized the necessity of an independent judiciary for Iraq’s future.

“A strong, independent judiciary is the bedrock of sovereignty, the rule of law, and the stability that lets Iraq turn its potential into prosperity,” Barrack wrote, thanking Zaidan for his partnership.

Barrack also met with Steve Fagin, the United States’ chargé d’affaires in Baghdad, and praised his diplomatic skills while emphasizing Washington’s aspirations to broaden its relationship with Iraq beyond security cooperation.

He regarded the present time as a watershed point in bilateral ties, stating that the United States was moving toward a more comprehensive relationship based on economic cooperation and common interests.

The Baghdad talks follow Barrack’s weekend conversations with Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein in Turkey, during which the two sides discussed bilateral ties and regional events.

The diplomatic contacts follow the completion of the US-led coalition’s military mission in Iraq, signaling a move toward a bilateral partnership based on political, economic, and security cooperation.

World.title: British airbase plot ‘almost certainly directed’ by Iran Guards: UK PM
World.content:
London – Britain’s government Monday accused Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of being behind a major scare at a UK airbase used by the United States, as allies including Washington warned Tehran against hostile acts.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the British parliament that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) “almost certainly directed” an incident at Royal Air Force Fairford in southwest England last month.

The US, which had been using the base for its war in Iran, abruptly withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the site last week after the mysterious episode on September 27.

Burnham said Britain’s assessment of the incident was that it “is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard”.

“We will not tolerate these threats on our soil. We will crack down on Iran’s use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams,” he told MPs.

Shortly afterwards, 29 countries, including the US, Britain, Australia, Canada, France and Germany, released a joint statement denouncing “in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks”.

The statement said such attacks included “acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners”.

“Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable,” it read.

The Foreign Office confirmed in its own statement Monday that Iran’s ambassador to the UK had been summoned for talks.

“We are also announcing the designation of two Iranian nationals for their role in facilitating or engaging in hostile activity on behalf of the Iranian regime, with the clear intent of threatening, planning or conducting attacks overseas,” foreign minister Ed Miliband said.

The foreign ministry said the individuals included Ruhollah Bazghandi, the IRGC’s head of counterespionage operations, who is “now subject to an immediate asset freeze, travel ban and director disqualification”.

Speculation has swirled about the incident since police were called to the base after a local farmer reported a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.

– ‘Major’ incident –

Despite a major counter-terrorism probe, seven suspects arrested in the days following, including a British-Iranian national, have all since been released on bail. None has been charged.

The incident was declared “major” by British authorities and triggered the evacuation of a nearby village.

But the source and nature of the threat have remained shrouded in mystery.

Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans, but did recover some petrol, according to officials.

Burnham has previously said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, which Tehran has rejected.

Britain gave Washington permission in March to use Fairford for “specific defensive operations into Iran,” and US bombers and other planes had been seen taking off and landing at the base.

US President Donald Trump has said Washington withdrew its bombers because of “threats” he believed were linked to Tehran.

In the foreign ministry statement, Miliband noted that the UK had already “designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under our new state threats powers, and imposed major sanctions on those responsible for Iran’s malign activity”.

World.title: Iraq’s Minister of Electricity visits Riyadh to attend WPC Energy Congress
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Minister of Electricity, Ali Saadi Waheeb, attended the 25th WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh on Monday, where he met with key international energy authorities and discussed ways to develop Iraq’s electrical industry and promote regional collaboration.

Waheeb attended the event with Iraq’s Minister of Oil, Basim Mohammed Khudair, as Saudi Arabia welcomed ministers, industry executives, and officials from international energy corporations to discuss energy security, investment, and technological innovation.

The visit comes amid heightened security concerns after the weekend’s fatal strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport by Yemen’s Houthis.

According to Saudi police, an assault on Saturday killed at least 12 people and injured over 300, while another on Sunday killed one person and injured 11 others.

The attacks hampered airport operations as the monarchy continued its international energy meetings.

Waheeb accompanied Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman for the opening of the congress exhibition, which displayed advances in energy technology, infrastructure, and investments.

On the sidelines of the conference, the Iraqi minister met with Turkey’s Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, Alparslan Bayraktar, to discuss extending collaboration on power infrastructure.

According to Bayraktar, the two nations have agreed to speed power interconnection lines and transmission projects, as well as increase bilateral investment to boost regional energy security.

In a statement on X, the Turkish Minister said that Ankara and Baghdad planned to expand their energy relationship beyond oil and gas to include the electricity sector.

Waheeb also spoke with Algeria’s Energy Minister, Mohamed Arkab, on technological cooperation, renewable energy, and potential for developing power generation, transmission, and distribution projects.

Waheeb met separately with Jordan’s Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources, Saleh Ali Hamid Al-Kharabsha, to explore ways to increase bilateral energy cooperation, exchange technical skills, and improve power infrastructure.

The young Iraqi Minister also attended the 16th meeting of the Arab Council of Ministers for power in Riyadh, where officials addressed regional power integration, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and increased collaboration among Arab nations.

Waheeb stated that Iraq was looking to use foreign experience and attract investment to upgrade its energy infrastructure, extend regional power connections, and enhance electricity supply.

World.title: Federal agents search home of Trump critic Ilhan Omar: government
World.content:
Washington – US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, officials said, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump’s confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker.

The search was conducted by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement, according to Fox News, citing sources familiar with the matter.

The operation, just three weeks before Omar seeks re-election in the November 3 midterms, raised concerns about longstanding Justice Department practices intended to prevent law enforcement actions from influencing elections.

The cable network reported that the operation was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born congresswoman by her late father when she was a child.

Trump’s border enforcement chief Tom Homan told Fox News he was unwilling to give details ahead of any official announcement but confirmed that an “investigation was ongoing for a while” and that “there was a warrant executed this morning.”

US media quoted the Justice Department confirming that agents had carried out a court-authorized search in the Washington area, but officials did not identify Omar or disclose the nature of the investigation.

The search reportedly began around 6:00 am. Video footage apparently taken by a member of the public and posted to X showed several agents wearing HSI jackets outside Omar’s Washington residence.

Omar, 44, is a leftist Democrat and fierce critic of Trump, particularly his administration’s sweeping crackdown on immigration.

The Republican president has repeatedly clashed with Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child and has frequently been the target of his political attacks.

– Rare offense –

In September, Homan said that Omar was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation, but again declined to provide details.

Omar said at the time that Homeland Security officials had not contacted her about any investigation, dismissing the allegations against her as politically motivated attacks.

There was no immediate public response from Omar to Monday’s search. AFP has sought comment from her office and the Trump administration.

But Xochitl Hinojosa, a former director of public affairs at the Justice Department, criticized the timing of the search.

“There’s a longstanding rule at DOJ that you don’t take overt actions like this before an election, especially when there’s a candidate on the ballot,” she wrote on X.

Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a senior fellow at the American Immigration Council, wrote on X that the “precedent set by this action is chilling,” warning that raids targeting political candidates shortly before elections could become more common.

Omar was first elected to Congress in 2018 and represents a district including Minneapolis, home to one of the largest Somali communities in the United States.

She is a member of the group of left-wing Democratic lawmakers known as “The Squad,” who have been among Trump’s most vocal opponents in Congress.

No charges against Omar were announced in connection with Monday’s search.

Trump and his Republican allies have for years argued that non-citizens vote in significant numbers in US elections, a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and deportation.

But studies consistently find non-citizen voting to be too rare an offense to have affected the outcome of any federal election.

An election fraud database kept by the conservative Heritage Foundation, dating back decades, contains just 1,619 cases of election-related offenses — of which non-citizen voting makes up a tiny 5.5 percent.

World.title: Iraq to increase electricity imports from Turkey to 2,000 megawatts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity revealed that it imports 600 megawatts of electricity per day from Turkey, with plans to reach 2,000 megawatts during the second phase of the electrical interconnection project.

The spokesperson for the Electricity Ministry, Ahmed Turki, said that one of the key principles of the strategy to strengthen the national grid’s supply is electricity interconnections with other countries. He added that the Ministry is actively working on electrical interconnection projects with the Gulf States, Turkey, and Jordan.

Iraq’s electricity interconnection project with the Gulf States is currently around 98 percent complete, according to Turki. He added that the project has a capacity of 500 megawatts.

The Iraqi official mentioned that during the visit of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, the Iraqi electricity minister requested an increase of 300 megawatts in the electricity supply from the Turkish company. This additional capacity has already been integrated into Iraq’s national grid.

Iraq now imports 600 megawatts per day from Turkey, with a deal in place for a second phase that will increase imported capacity through the Turkish line to almost 2,000 megawatts.

In terms of the electricity interconnection project with Jordan, Turki said that Iraq was getting between 50 and 100 megawatts from the Jordanian side until the contract expired in mid-September, with expectations that it would be renewed next summer.

World.title: Saudi says resilience tested, vows response after deadly airport attacks
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia’s energy minister on Monday said the country had been tested but would mount a “serious” response after a string of attacks on Riyadh’s international airport by Yemen’s Houthis that left 18 people dead.

Lethal airport strikes since last week have rocked the world’s top oil exporter, which is pursuing an expensive economic reform drive aimed at attracting foreign investment.

Yemen’s civil war, where a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis, has reignited months into the US-Iran conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.

“Energy security can’t be taken for granted,” Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an energy conference in Riyadh, as oil prices topped $105 a barrel.

“The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”

“For Saudi Arabia, these circumstances have tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience,” he added.

On Saturday, Houthi strikes killed 13 people and wounded hundreds at King Khalid International Airport — the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade.

Four people died in earlier attacks on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh’s outskirts on Monday.

CCTV footage of Saturday’s attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden flash tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.

– ‘The whole house shook’ –

The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats, and Australia’s embassy warned its citizens in the city to shelter in place.

The Houthis on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the previous 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting Saudi transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”.

Hours later, the coalition said yet another projectile had struck Riyadh airport, sparking a fire, while air defences intercepted a missile nearby.

AFP journalists and locals reported hearing multiple blasts in the capital on Sunday.

“The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the city’s north.

Riyadh’s airport was not the only one to suffer a deadly attack: early on Monday, officials said one person had been killed and 11 wounded in a strike on Dammam airport.

The Saudi-led coalition said Monday that it had also “intercepted and destroyed” a Houthi ballistic missile heading for the southern city of Khamis Mushait, home to a major military base.

Riyadh hosts a packed calendar of events at this time of year, including its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, which draws foreign leaders and business titans.

– ‘Full-fledged war crime’ –

Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.

“Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University.

The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”.

The attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

Iran, which backs the Houthis, said Monday it was “deeply concerned” over the recent escalation.

Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath.

“Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”.

World.title: Alcaraz exits Shanghai Masters in straight-sets loss
World.content:
Shanghai – Carlos Alcaraz fell to Zizou Bergs in straight sets at the Shanghai Masters on Monday, interrupting the former world number one’s in-form return to the professional Tour after being sidelined for months by injury.

The 39th-ranked Belgian beat the second-seeded Spanish star 7-5, 7-6 (7/4) in the third round to land the tournament’s biggest upset yet, and will play either Tommy Paul or Valentin Vacherot next.

“It’s a little disbelief and not feeling too much,” Bergs, 27, said afterwards.

“You’re just really in the moment, being focused on the points you have to play,” he added.

“I’ll be very happy.”

Alcaraz started with more quality until Bergs broke the Spaniard’s serve to go up 3-2 in the first set.

The 23-year-old grabbed back that break in the next game but was uncharacteristically off-target, sending a mess of shots into the net.

He double-faulted to hand Bergs a critical break point in the 11th game, and lost the first set when a volley went short.

Alcaraz was visibly frustrated during the second set as he vented to his corner following a series of misfired shots that left him with no points in the fourth and eighth games.

Alcaraz forced a tie-break but could not reach a third set as Bergs closed things out just past the two-hour mark on his first match point.

– Fritz fumbles –

Earlier, Stefanos Tsitsipas came back to beat Taylor Fritz 3-6, 7-5, 6-3 and earn fourth round meeting with Daniil Medvedev, who brushed aside qualifier Dalibor Svrcina 6-2, 6-3.

A wardrobe malfunction delayed victory for the Greek world number 43 when a tennis ball tumbled out of the American’s pocket a second time and forced the men to replay a match point.

A tired-looking Fritz, seeded 11th, hung on for a bit longer to save the eighth game but could not stick around beyond that, with Tsitsipas holding serve to win at the fifth time of asking.

“I could have done a few things easier, but I ended up being my biggest enemy,” Tsitsipas told the crowd afterwards.

“I turned things around really well towards the end and became friends with myself and played some incredible tennis,” he said.

Felix Auger-Aliassime, Casper Ruud and Rafael Jodar also went through to the last 16.

World.title: ICMR sets up high-altitude research centre in Keylong to study health risks in Himalayas
World.content:
NEW DELHI: From how soldiers acclimatise to thin air at extreme altitudes to how low oxygen levels and harsh winters affect the health of Himalayan communities, a new research centre in Himachal Pradesh will study the distinctive medical challenges of living and working in the mountains.

Union health minister Jagat Prakash Nadda on Monday performed the bhumi pujan and laid the foundation stone of the Indian Council of Medical Research's (ICMR) Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research at Keylong, Himachal Pradesh.

Built on an ICMR field station established at Keylong nearly a decade ago, the centre will function as a permanent, year-round institution with specialised personnel and state-of-the-art laboratories.

It will generate evidence on the health effects of low oxygen levels, extreme cold and changing climatic conditions, with research spanning both military personnel and civilian populations.

The research will focus on altitude-related health risks, acclimatisation, maternal and newborn health, child nutrition and disease patterns in Himalayan communities. It will also explore drone-based medicine delivery, digital health and artificial intelligence to improve healthcare access in remote areas.





ICMR will combine its research expertise with AFMSâs field experience, with AIIMS Bilaspur studying the effects of high-altitude conditions on patients visiting the region.

Nadda said the centre would help build a strong institutional foundation for research into the health challenges faced by people in the Himalayan region and personnel deployed in high-altitude areas. He stressed the need for systematic studies to identify risks and develop appropriate preventive healthcare interventions.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM unveils logo, anthem for Haridwar Kumbh-2027
World.content:
Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday unveiled the official logo, website, and anthem for the Haridwar Kumbh Mela (Ardh Kumbh) 2027.

The logo of Haridwar Kumbh-2027 depicts Mother Ganga, the Har Ki Pauri area, the Dhanush Bridge, and the divine radiance of the sunrise.

It also incorporates the statue of Lord Shiva, sages and seers, symbols of Sanatan tradition such as the Trishul and Damru, as well as the hills of Goddess Mansa Devi and Goddess Chandi Devi.

The Mela administration had invited entries from the state's youth and students to design the logo for Kumbh Mela 2027.

After the selection committee reviewed 13 original designs from among hundreds of submissions, it selected the design submitted by Madhu Sharma, a resident of Haridwar's Jagjitpur.

The official logo for Haridwar Kumbh-2027 was finalised based on Sharma's design.

Speaking at a programme held at the Mela Control Room (CCR) auditorium, Dhami said Kumbh is a magnificent celebration of India's ancient spiritual tradition, Sanatan culture, and public faith.

World.title: 'Advance injustice': Allahabad HC flags POCSO Act's rigid application in minor couple cases
World.content:
The Allahabad high court has called on the law commission to consider recommending changes to the protection of children from sexual offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, to address cases involving minor couples while taking India's prevailing social realities into account.

A two-judge bench comprising justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev said that the strict enforcement of the legislation could, in certain exceptional circumstances, lead to outcomes that âadvance injustice rather than justiceâ, especially when a relationship has resulted in the birth of a child.

The comment was made during the court's consideration of Rakesh Yadav's habeas corpus petition, which sought an order to produce his wife.

The bench observed that the law appeared not to have adequately considered India's social conditions, where a substantial section of the population remains illiterate or semi-literate and may have limited awareness of their legal and constitutional rights, along with the responsibilities and consequences associated with them.

The girl's father told the court that she had studied up to class 5 but could not read a newspaper and was able only to sign her name.





He said he had never attended school.

The court allowed the man's habeas corpus petition. The couple had eloped, and the girl subsequently gave birth to their child, following which a case was registered against him under the POCSO Act.

Court calls for flexibility in exceptional cases

"It is definitely not an excuse to be ignorant of the law. The bench noted that the POCSO Act's execution may, in some factual circumstances, lead to outcomes that seem to promote injustice rather than justice if this concept is implemented in a purely pedantic manner."

According to the news agency PTI, the court suggested that the law commission consider amendments allowing special judges greater flexibility in exceptional cases to take the specific circumstances into account while deciding an appropriate sentence.

It also recommended examining alternative penalties, including community service, in situations where applying the POCSO Act could lead to the unnecessary disruption of a family formed amid a lack of awareness of the law.

The bench observed that the existing legislation appeared to have insufficiently considered India's prevailing social realities.

Describing the matter as a conflict between human development and the strict application of the law, the court noted that adolescents around the age of 15 may develop emotional and physical maturity that can lead to attraction towards another person.

World.title: Delhi's new protest venue Ramlila Maidan has just 3 dates available this year - check details
World.content:
A view of Ramlila Maidan, designated as a protest site along with two new venues,. (PTI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ramlila Maidan, newly designated as one of the capital's three protest sites, is already booked for most of the next two-and-a-half months, leaving just three days available for reservations this year.Additionally, while a small section of the ground can be used for protests free of charge, booking the larger venue, which spans 12 acres and can accommodate up to 50,000 people, involves a daily fee and a refundable security deposit.Revealing that only December 29, 30 and 31 as the availiable dates, an official quoted by PTI said, "The booking rate for the ground is Rs 50,000 per day, plus a Rs 55,000 security deposit that is refundable. The initial outlay including taxes comes to Rs 1.21 lakh for a day's booking."However, officials clarified that a small portion of the ground, with space for around 150 people, remains available for protests and gatherings free of charge.Permission to use the larger ground must be obtained from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi's horticulture department, which processes bookings after applicants secure a no-objection certificate from Delhi Police.The arrangement has drawn criticism from opposition leaders and protesters, who argue that the limited availability and high booking costs could make demonstrations difficult to organise.AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj questioned the decision, pointing to events already scheduled at the venue. Govt. played another fraud with its citizens. The Ramleela Maidan is occupied with two Ramleelas," Bharadwaj wrote on X."How can one hold a protest here? Do they want to create chaos?" he asked.Protesters also highlighted the financial burden, noting that demonstrations at Jantar Mantar did not require comparable payments.Civic officials, however, pointed to the revenue implications of allowing unrestricted use of the ground. "If given up for protest without any fees, the civic body will stand to lose at least Rs 50,000 plus per day," an official said, quoted by PTI.The ground is frequently reserved for public events and religious festivities, particularly around Dussehra and Diwali, contributing to the shortage of available dates.Apart from booking constraints, the venue presents traffic-management challenges. Located in a busy commercial area near three hospitals and municipal offices, Ramlila Maidan has witnessed major congestion during political rallies and other large gatherings.Officials said police often have to introduce one-way traffic restrictions on Asaf Ali Road and divert vehicles towards Jawaharlal Nehru Marg. A BJP rally in 2014 reportedly caused traffic jams extending nearly four kilometres to ITO, despite being held on a Sunday.The venue has been central to Delhi's political history for decades. Once a pond, the site was filled and levelled around 1930 to accommodate Ramlila performances, which began there in 1932. It subsequently hosted major political gatherings addressed by leaders including Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Jayaprakash Narayan and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.On June 25, 1975, the day the Emergency was declared, Jayaprakash Narayan and Vajpayee addressed a rally at the ground. Relatively recently, Arvind Kejriwal took oath as Delhi chief minister there in 2013.The controversy follows an standing order issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, which removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues and identified Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as the three new locations for demonstrations. Police said a detailed, revised standard operating procedure for protests at these sites would be issued separately.

World.title: Abdullapurmet Tahsildar, surveyor caught accepting ₹20 lakh bribe in Rangareddy district
World.content:
A Tahsildar and a Mandal Surveyor from Abdullapurmet mandal in Rangareddy district were caught by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Monday (October 12) in connection with a ₹20 lakh bribe. The bribe was demanded for conducting a land survey and issuing a joint inspection report required for a layout under Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) guidelines.

The accused were identified as B. Sudershan Reddy, Tahsildar of Abdullapurmet, and Batuka Srinivasulu, Mandal Surveyor.

According to the ACB, the two officials had initially demanded ₹30 lakh from the complainant for conducting the survey and issuing the Joint Inspection Survey Report. The amount was subsequently negotiated down to ₹20 lakh.

Acting on a complaint, ACB officials laid a trap near Abdullapurmet, where Srinivasulu was caught accepting ₹20 lakh on the instructions of the Tahsildar.

The entire bribe amount was recovered from Srinivasulu’s possession. A chemical test conducted on his fingers yielded positive results, indicating that he had handled the bribe money, the ACB said.

The bureau stated that both officials had acted dishonestly in the discharge of their public duties by demanding and accepting money in exchange for an official favour. Both officials are being arrested and produced before the Principal Special Judge for SPE and ACB Cases at Nampally, Hyderabad.

The identity of the complainant has been withheld for security reasons. Further investigation is underway.

The ACB appealed to the public to report demands for bribes by government employees through its toll-free helpline, 1064, or WhatsApp number 9440446106.

World.title: Delhi’s winter action plan hit as new road sweeping machines delayed until November-end
World.content:
Despite winter approaching and air pollution expected to worsen, the Delhi government has missed a crucial July deadline to deploy a new fleet of 140 Mechanical Road Sweepers (MRS) to curb dust. None of the new MRS machines have arrived, leaving the capital without key infrastructure as its annual pollution crisis looms, multiple officials told The Hindu.

In February, the Delhi government informed the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) that 140 MRS machines would be deployed by the end of July to curb dust pollution. The fleet was to comprise 70 large machines for wider roads and 70 smaller variants for narrower lanes. The initiative is projected to cost the government approximately ₹900 crore over the next 10 years.

On Monday, Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa told The Hindu that after tender process, work order has been issued for the 70 large MRS machines and at least some of them are expected to arrive by the end of November. “We will use the existing MRS machines and we are trying to make sure that at least some of the new large MRS machines will also be available during this winter,” Mr. Sirsa said.

An IIT-Kanpur study in 2016 found that road dust accounts for about 56% of Delhi’s annual PM10 emissions and 38% of its annual PM2.5 emissions.

While the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is executing the project, the Delhi government is funding it. The government is outsourcing the operations to private firms selected through a competitive bidding process rather than purchasing the fleet. The chosen vendors will supply both the machinery and the operational staff.

Meanwhile, the plan for the smaller machines was scaled down from 70 to 30 following a government analysis,officials said. However, the Delhi Cabinet approved the revised plan on September 29, delaying the tendering process and subsequent deployment.

Faced with these delays, the MCD proposed hiring 30 to 40 MRS machines on a temporary basis for three to four months this winter. The CAQM rejected this interim plan as it included an option to utilise diesel trucks, sources added.

Prolonged delays

The machines are part of a broader, missed-deadline initiative first announced on January 28, 2023 by the previous Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government as part of an ambitious plan for the “world-class transformation” of city roads.

Although work was scheduled to begin on the ground by April 1, 2023, the Delhi Cabinet did not pass the ₹2,388 crore proposal until April 4, 2023. The Cabinet split the original plan into two components, outsourcing the work to private firms for a period of seven to 10 years. The first phase focused on deploying 250 water sprinklers integrated with anti-smog guns to control dust. The second phase involved engaging 70 MRS machines integrated with 210 water sprinklers.

Initially, the Delhi government planned to route the funds through its Public Works Department. However, following objections from the MCD, which maintains 1,400 km of city roads, the Cabinet decided to grant the funds directly to the civic body. However, the implementation got stuck again as the MCD lacked a Standing Committee to clear the approval.

In December 2024, the project hit another snag when the MCD wrote to the environment department seeking permission to divert the funds towards solid waste management and road maintenance as part of an “integrated” sanitation plan.

The BJP government, which came to power in February 2025, revived the project and passed a new cabinet decision, subsequent structural revisions have caused further delays.

World.title: India poised to woo global investments amid US curbs: INMECC
World.content:
India has a significant opportunity to attract global technology investments and industrial establishments as the United States tightens manpower regulations, the Indo Gulf and Middle East Chamber of Commerce (INMECC) has said.

The changing international business environment presents India with an opportunity to position itself as a preferred destination for foreign investments and the establishment of fully equipped operational and technology centres, it said in a statement.

Urging the Central and State governments, along with private-sector stakeholders, to explore the emerging opportunity, the INMECC said it is actively engaged in facilitating investment opportunities in India.

“We must act strategically to attract international technology companies, industrial investments, and global operational centres,” N.M. Sharafudeen, chairman, INMECC, said.

World.title: Delhi High Court seeks police reply on Natasha Narwal’s plea to travel abroad
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Monday sought a response from the Delhi police on activist Natasha Narwal’s plea seeking permission to travel to the United Kingdom to attend an academic conference while on bail in a case linked to the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

Justice Amit Bansal issued notice on Ms. Narwal’s petition challenging an October 6 trial court order denying her permission to travel abroad in a case registered under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The matter has been listed for further hearing on October 15.

Ms. Narwal’s counsel told the court that she planned to attend a conference in the UK from November 2 to December 1 and sought an early decision on her plea. The counsel submitted that she would need time to secure the release of her passport, which had been surrendered during the criminal proceedings, apply for a visa and make travel arrangements.

The trial court had rejected her request, citing the seriousness of the allegations and the stage of the proceedings.

Ms. Narwal is an accused in three FIRs registered by the Delhi police in connection with the violence, including one alleging a “larger conspiracy” under the UAPA.

In June 2021, the High Court granted bail to Ms. Narwal and fellow activist Devangana Kalita in the UAPA case. The court observed that, “in its anxiety to suppress dissent”, the State appeared to be blurring the line between the constitutionally guaranteed right to protest and terrorist activity. It warned that if this mindset gained traction, it would be a “sad day for democracy”.

World.title: 13,505 girls get HPV vaccine in Kozhikode
World.content:
As many as 13,505 girls aged up to 14 have been vaccinated in Kozhikode district against human papilloma virus (HPV), Health department officials have said.

The department said in a release on Monday that around 51% of the target audience had been covered so far. As many as 1,854 girls were vaccinated from schools. The vaccination drive had been conducted in 169 schools till now.

The government, meanwhile, has extended the deadline for the campaign till December 31. District Medical Officer L.T. Saritha Kumari said the vaccination is available at all government health centres.

World.title: ‘Future of leadership is abilityto be a boundary-less leader’
World.content:
The future of leadership for students is the ability to be a boundary-less leader, said Sai Sudha Chandrasekaran, Alpha Alternatives and former CEO of India Fintech Foundation, at the 25th Madras Management Association (MMA) All-India Management Students’ Convention 2026, in Chennai on Monday.

She was speaking at the convention themed ‘Future-Ready Leadership: Reinventing Management for a Changing World’.

The day-long convention brought together management students and distinguished leaders from industry, entrepreneurship, and professional services to explore the capabilities, skills, and mindset needed to lead in a rapidly changing business environment.

Mithun Sacheti, Founder, Caratlane and Partner, Q Partners - Axana Estates, said, “It is really important to look around and ask what would be a new way to run the same industry. I think the big industries are ripe now for new entrepreneurship.”

Managing Director, Saint-Gobain India, and president of MMA A.R. Unnikrishnan, executive director of MMA R. Vijayakumar and convention chairman and Sify Technologies Group CFO M.P. Vijay Kumar also spoke at the event.

The Hindu was a media partner for the event.
